2.18.s:
2.86
puṣkara uvāca ..
upanīya guruḥ śiṣyaṃ śikṣayecchaucamāditaḥ ..
ācāramagnikāryaṃ ca sandhyopāsanameva ca .. 1 ..
2.18.d:
2.86
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
उपनीय गुरुः शिष्यं शिक्षयेच्छौचमादितः ॥
आचारमग्निकार्यं च सन्ध्योपासनमेव च ॥ 1 ॥
2.18.m: Puṣkara said: / Having initiated the student, the guru should teach him first of all purity, / proper conduct, the fire-rite, and twilight worship.

2.18.s:
prayataḥ kalyamutthāya snāto hutahutāśanaḥ ..
bhaktyā gurostu kurvīta abhigamyābhivādanam ..2..
2.18.d:
प्रयतः कल्यमुत्थाय स्नातो हुतहुताशनः ॥
भक्त्या गुरोस्तु कुर्वीत अभिगम्याभिवादनम् ॥2॥
2.18.m: Restrained, having risen at dawn, bathed, and offered oblations to the fire, / he should approach and perform salutation to the guru with devotion.

2.18.s:
gurostu vāmaṃ caraṇaṃ vāmahastena saṃspṛśet ..
dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇenaiva svanāma parikīrtayan .. 3 ..
2.18.d:
गुरोस्तु वामं चरणं वामहस्तेन संस्पृशेत् ॥
दक्षिणं दक्षिणेनैव स्वनाम परिकीर्तयन् ॥ 3 ॥
2.18.m: He should touch the left foot of the guru with his left hand, / and the right [foot] with his right hand, declaring his own name.

2.18.s:
anujñātastu guruṇā tato'dhyayanamācaret ..
kṛtvā brahmāñjaliṃ paśyangurorvadanamānataḥ .. 4 ..
2.18.d:
अनुज्ञातस्तु गुरुणा ततोऽध्ययनमाचरेत् ॥
कृत्वा ब्रह्माञ्जलिं पश्यन्गुरोर्वदनमानतः ॥ 4 ॥
2.18.m: Permitted by the guru, he should then undertake recitation, / having made the brahmāñjali gesture and looking humbly at the face of the guru.

2.18.s:
brahmāvasāne prārambhe praṇavaṃ caiva kīrtayet ..
anadhyāyeṣvadhyayanaṃ varjayettu prayatnataḥ .. 5 ..
2.18.d:
ब्रह्मावसाने प्रारम्भे प्रणवं चैव कीर्तयेत् ॥
अनध्यायेष्वध्ययनं वर्जयेत्तु प्रयत्नतः ॥ 5 ॥
2.18.m: At the beginning and end of sacred recitation, he should utter the Praṇava; / but he should carefully avoid recitation during forbidden study times.

2.18.s:
bhaikṣyacaryāṃ tataḥ kuryādbrāhmaṇeṣu yathāvidhi ..
guroḥ kule na bhikṣeta bhuñjīta tadanujñayā .. 6 ..
2.18.d:
भैक्ष्यचर्यां ततः कुर्याद्ब्राह्मणेषु यथाविधि ॥
गुरोः कुले न भिक्षेत भुञ्जीत तदनुज्ञया ॥ 6 ॥
2.18.m: Then he should go begging among brahmins according to rule. / He should not beg in the household of the guru; he should eat with his permission.

2.18.s:
āyuṣyaṃ prāṅmukho bhuṅkte yaśasyaṃ dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ ..
śriyaḥ pratyaṅmukho bhuṅkte ṛtaṃ bhuṅkte hyudaṅmukhaḥ .. 7 ..
2.18.d:
आयुष्यं प्राङ्मुखो भुङ्क्ते यशस्यं दक्षिणामुखः ॥
श्रियः प्रत्यङ्मुखो भुङ्क्ते ऋतं भुङ्क्ते ह्युदङ्मुखः ॥ 7 ॥
2.18.m: Facing east, he eats for long life; facing south, for renown; / facing west, he eats for prosperity; and facing north, he eats for truth.

2.18.s:
hitaṃ priyaṃ guroḥ kuryādbhaktyāhaṃkāravarjitaḥ ..
anvāsya paścimāṃ sandhyāṃ pūjayitvā hutāśanam .. 8 ..
2.18.d:
हितं प्रियं गुरोः कुर्याद्भक्त्याहंकारवर्जितः ॥
अन्वास्य पश्चिमां सन्ध्यां पूजयित्वा हुताशनम् ॥ 8 ॥
2.18.m: He should act for the good and pleasure of the guru with devotion, free from egoism. / Having performed the evening twilight worship and honored the fire,

2.18.s:
abhivādya guruṃ paścādgurorvacanakṛdbhavet ..
madhumāṃsāñjanaṃ śrāddhaṃ gītaṃ nṛtyaṃ ca varjayet .. 9 ..
2.18.d:
अभिवाद्य गुरुं पश्चाद्गुरोर्वचनकृद्भवेत् ॥
मधुमांसाञ्जनं श्राद्धं गीतं नृत्यं च वर्जयेत् ॥ 9 ॥
2.18.m: and having saluted the guru, he should obey the guru's word. / He should avoid honey, meat, collyrium, ancestral offerings, singing, and dancing;

2.18.s:
hiṃsāṃ parāpavādaṃ ca aślīlaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ ..
mekhalāmajinaṃ daṇḍaṃ dhārayetprayataḥ sadā .. 2.86.10 ..
2.18.d:
हिंसां परापवादं च अश्लीलं च विशेषतः ॥
मेखलामजिनं दण्डं धारयेत्प्रयतः सदा ॥ 2.86.10 ॥
2.18.m: especially injury, slandering others, and vulgarity. / Attentive, he should always wear the girdle, deer-skin, and staff.

2.18.s:
vinaṣṭānapsu nikṣipya tathānyāndhārayetpunaḥ ..
ādiṣṭī nodakaṃ kuryādāvratasya samāpanāt .. 11 ..
2.18.d:
विनष्टानप्सु निक्षिप्य तथान्यान्धारयेत्पुनः ॥
आदिष्टी नोदकं कुर्यादाव्रतस्य समापनात् ॥ 11 ॥
2.18.m: When they are ruined, having cast them into water, he should take others again. / An initiated student should not offer funerary water until the completion of his vow;

2.18.s:
samāpte tu vrataṃ kuryāttrirātreṇaiva śuddhyati ..
adhaḥśāyī bhavennityaṃ brahmacārī samāhitaḥ .. 12 ..
2.18.d:
समाप्ते तु व्रतं कुर्यात्त्रिरात्रेणैव शुद्ध्यति ॥
अधःशायी भवेन्नित्यं ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः ॥ 12 ॥
2.18.m: but when it is completed, he may perform the rite, and is purified after three nights. / The student of the Veda should constantly sleep on the ground, composed.

2.18.s:
evaṃ mataṃ tu kurvīta vedasvīkaraṇaṃ dvijaḥ ..
gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā snāyācca tadanantaram..13..
2.18.d:
एवं मतं तु कुर्वीत वेदस्वीकरणं द्विजः ॥
गुरवे दक्षिणां दत्त्वा स्नायाच्च तदनन्तरम्॥13॥
2.18.m: In this manner the twice-born should adopt the vow and mastery of the Veda; / and having given the sacrificial fee to the guru, he should bathe immediately afterwards.

2.18.s:
āśarīravimokṣādvā vasedgurukule sadā ..
naiṣṭhiko brahmacārī ca vāyubhūtaḥ khamūrtimān ..14..
2.18.d:
आशरीरविमोक्षाद्वा वसेद्गुरुकुले सदा ॥
नैष्ठिको ब्रह्मचारी च वायुभूतः खमूर्तिमान् ॥14॥
2.18.m: Or he may dwell constantly in the teacher's house until the release of his body; / a perpetual student of the Veda, becoming like wind, ethereal in form,

2.18.s:
tatpadaṃ samavāpnoti yatra gatvā na śocati ..
snāne caiva sagodāne kālaḥ pūrvo vidhīyate ..
pūjanaṃ vāsudevasya sarvatra ca vidhīyate..15..
2.18.d:
तत्पदं समवाप्नोति यत्र गत्वा न शोचति ॥
स्नाने चैव सगोदाने कालः पूर्वो विधीयते ॥
पूजनं वासुदेवस्य सर्वत्र च विधीयते॥15॥
2.18.m: attains that state having gone to which one does not grieve. / The earlier time is prescribed for the bath and the gift of a cow; / and the worship of Vāsudeva is prescribed everywhere.

2.18.s:
saṃpūjya devaṃ gurave ca dattvā dhanaṃ yathāvatparipūrṇavidyaḥ ..
gṛhāśramī syādvidhivannṛsiṃha yatrāsya lokadvitayaṃ pradiṣṭam .. 16 ..
2.87
puṣkara uvāca ..
vipraścatasro vindeta bhāryāstisrastu bhūmipaḥ ..
dve ca vaiśyastathā kāmaṃ bhāryaikāmapi cāntyajaḥ .. 1 ..
brāhmaṇī kṣatriyā vaiśyā śūdrī viprasya kīrtitāḥ ..
krameṇa kāmasaktasya vivāhāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..2..
vivāhamutkramātkṛtvā narakaṃ pratipadyate ..
dharmakāryāṇi sarvāṇi na kāryāṇyasavarṇayā ..3 ..
asavarṇā tu yā nārī ratyarthe sā prakīrtitā ..
ādhānaṃ tasya dharmārthaṃ na praśaṃsanti sādhavaḥ .. 4 ..
pāṇirgrāhyaḥ savarṇāsu gṛhṇīyātkṣatriyā śaram ..
vaiśyā pratodamādadyāddaśāṃ caivāntyajā tathā..5..
utkṛṣṭavedane'pyetadvidhānaṃ parikīrtitam ..
sakṛtkanyā pradātavyā haraṃstāṃ cauradaṇḍabhāk .. 6 ..
2.18.d:
संपूज्य देवं गुरवे च दत्त्वा धनं यथावत्परिपूर्णविद्यः ॥
गृहाश्रमी स्याद्विधिवन्नृसिंह यत्रास्य लोकद्वितयं प्रदिष्टम् ॥ 16 ॥
2.87
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
विप्रश्चतस्रो विन्देत भार्यास्तिस्रस्तु भूमिपः ॥
द्वे च वैश्यस्तथा कामं भार्यैकामपि चान्त्यजः ॥ 1 ॥
ब्राह्मणी क्षत्रिया वैश्या शूद्री विप्रस्य कीर्तिताः ॥
क्रमेण कामसक्तस्य विवाहाः परिकीर्तिताः ॥2॥
विवाहमुत्क्रमात्कृत्वा नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
धर्मकार्याणि सर्वाणि न कार्याण्यसवर्णया ॥3 ॥
असवर्णा तु या नारी रत्यर्थे सा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
आधानं तस्य धर्मार्थं न प्रशंसन्ति साधवः ॥ 4 ॥
पाणिर्ग्राह्यः सवर्णासु गृह्णीयात्क्षत्रिया शरम् ॥
वैश्या प्रतोदमादद्याद्दशां चैवान्त्यजा तथा॥5॥
उत्कृष्टवेदनेऽप्येतद्विधानं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
सकृत्कन्या प्रदातव्या हरंस्तां चौरदण्डभाक् ॥ 6 ॥
2.18.m:
Having worshipped the Lord and given wealth to the guru as prescribed, having completed his learning, / he should become a householder according to rule, O Narasiṃha, where both worlds are appointed for him.
Puṣkara said: / A brahmin may take four wives, a king three, / and a vaiśya two at will, and a low-born man one wife.
Brahmin, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra women are declared for a brahmin / in succession, if he is attached to desire, as prescribed marriages.
Having contracted a marriage in reverse order, he goes to hell. / All duties of dharma are not to be performed with a wife not of one's own class.
The woman who is not of one's own class is declared to be for pleasure; / the virtuous do not praise fathering a child through her for the sake of dharma.
The hand is to be taken with women of the same class; a kṣatriya woman should hold an arrow, / a vaiśya woman should take a goad, and a low-born woman the skirt of a garment.
Even when marrying an upper-caste man, this rule is declared. / A maiden should be given away only once; one who abducts her incurs the punishment of a thief.

2.18.s:
na kanyāvikayaṃ kāryaṃ kadācidapi kenacit ..
keśavikrayiṇo yānti narakāneka viṃśatīn..7..
apatyavikrayāttasya niṣkṛtirna vidhīyate ..
kanyāprajīvanātkiṃcinnopajīvati yaḥ pumān .. 8 ..
na tacchulkaṃ samuddiṣṭamānṛśaṃsyaṃ hi tatkṛtam ..
kanyādānaṃ śacīyāgo vivāho'tha caturthikā .. 9 ..
vivāhametatkathitaṃ rāma karmacatuṣṭayam ..
dattāmapi haretkanyāṃ varaśceddoṣabhāgbhavet .. 2.87.10 ..
naṣṭe mṛte pravrajite klībe'tha patite'patau ..
pañcasvāpatsu nārīṇāṃ patiranyo vidhīyate .. 11 .. .
mṛte tu devare deyā tadabhāve yadṛcchayā ..
pūrvātritayamāgneyaṃ vāyavyaṃ cottarātrayam .. 12 ..
rohiṇī ceti varuṇaṃ bhagaṇaḥ śasyate sadā ..
naikagotrāṃ ca varayennaikārṣīyāṃ ca bhārgava .. 13 ..
pitṛtaḥ saptamādūrdhvaṃ mātṛtaḥ pañcamāttathā ..
varayellakṣaṇopetāṃ sadā lokadvayecchayā .. 14 ..
2.18.d:
न कन्याविकयं कार्यं कदाचिदपि केनचित् ॥
केशविक्रयिणो यान्ति नरकानेक विंशतीन्॥7॥
अपत्यविक्रयात्तस्य निष्कृतिर्न विधीयते ॥
कन्याप्रजीवनात्किंचिन्नोपजीवति यः पुमान् ॥ 8 ॥
न तच्छुल्कं समुद्दिष्टमानृशंस्यं हि तत्कृतम् ॥
कन्यादानं शचीयागो विवाहोऽथ चतुर्थिका ॥ 9 ॥
विवाहमेतत्कथितं राम कर्मचतुष्टयम् ॥
दत्तामपि हरेत्कन्यां वरश्चेद्दोषभाग्भवेत् ॥ 2.87.10 ॥
नष्टे मृते प्रव्रजिते क्लीबेऽथ पतितेऽपतौ ॥
पञ्चस्वापत्सु नारीणां पतिरन्यो विधीयते ॥ 11 ॥ ।
मृते तु देवरे देया तदभावे यदृच्छया ॥
पूर्वात्रितयमाग्नेयं वायव्यं चोत्तरात्रयम् ॥ 12 ॥
रोहिणी चेति वरुणं भगणः शस्यते सदा ॥
नैकगोत्रां च वरयेन्नैकार्षीयां च भार्गव ॥ 13 ॥
पितृतः सप्तमादूर्ध्वं मातृतः पञ्चमात्तथा ॥
वरयेल्लक्षणोपेतां सदा लोकद्वयेच्छया ॥ 14 ॥
2.18.m:
The sale of a maiden should never be done by anyone at any time; / sellers of human hair go to twenty-one hells.
No expiation is prescribed for him for the sale of offspring; / whatever man derives no livelihood at all from the bride-price of a maiden,
that is not called a bride-price, for it was done out of compassion. / The giving of a maiden, the sacrifice to Śacī, the wedding, and then the fourth-day rite—
this fourfold ritual, O Rāma, is called marriage. / Even if she was already given, one may take away the maiden if the bridegroom is blameworthy.
When [the husband is] vanished, dead, gone forth as an ascetic, impotent, or fallen [from caste]— / in these five calamities, another husband is prescribed for women.
When he is dead, she should be given to a brother-in-law; in his absence, according to choice. / The triad of the previous [nakṣatras], the constellation of Agni, the constellation of Vāyu, and the triad of the latter,
and Rohiṇī and the constellation of Varuṇa—this group of stars is always praised. / He should not choose one of the same gotra, nor one sharing the same ṛṣi lineage, O Bhārgava,
beyond the seventh generation on the father's side, and likewise beyond the fifth on the mother's side. / Desiring both worlds, he should always select a maiden endowed with auspicious marks.

2.18.s:
brāhmo daivastathaivārṣaḥ prājāpatyastathāsuraḥ ..
gāndharvo rākṣasaścaiva paiśācaścāṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 15 ..
āhuḥ pradānaṃ brāhmeṇa kulaśīlayutāya tu ..
tajjaḥ punātyubhayataḥ puruṣānekaviṃśatīn..16..
2.18.d:
ब्राह्मो दैवस्तथैवार्षः प्राजापत्यस्तथासुरः ॥
गान्धर्वो राक्षसश्चैव पैशाचश्चाष्टमः स्मृतः ॥ 15 ॥
आहुः प्रदानं ब्राह्मेण कुलशीलयुताय तु ॥
तज्जः पुनात्युभयतः पुरुषानेकविंशतीन्॥16॥
2.18.m:
The Brāhma, Daiva, Ārṣa, Prājāpatya, and Āsura, / Gāndharva, Rākṣasa, and Paiśāca is remembered as the eighth.
They say the gift [of a daughter] by the Brāhma rite is to one endowed with good family and conduct; / the son born of it purifies twenty-one generations on both sides.

2.18.s:
daivaśca ṛtvije dānaṃ sa tu yajñaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
tajjaḥ punāti dharmajña svakule puruṣatrayān..17..
2.18.d:
दैवश्च ऋत्विजे दानं स तु यज्ञः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
तज्जः पुनाति धर्मज्ञ स्वकुले पुरुषत्रयान्॥17॥
2.18.m: The Daiva is the gift to an officiating priest; that is declared to be in a sacrifice; / the son born of it, O knower of dharma, purifies three generations in his own family.

2.18.s:
śulkena cāsuraṃ vidyātsa tu dharmādṛte mataḥ ..
parasparecchayā rāma kanyakāvarayostathā.. 18 ..
2.18.d:
शुल्केन चासुरं विद्यात्स तु धर्मादृते मतः ॥
परस्परेच्छया राम कन्यकावरयोस्तथा॥ 18 ॥
2.18.m: And one should know the Āsura by the bride-price; that is considered apart from dharma. / By mutual desire, O Rāma, between maiden and bridegroom,

2.18.s:
gāndharvo nāma nirdiṣṭaḥ sa tu manmathalakṣaṇaḥ ..
rākṣaso yuddhaharaṇātpaiśācaḥ kanyakāchalāt .. 19 ..
2.18.d:
गान्धर्वो नाम निर्दिष्टः स तु मन्मथलक्षणः ॥
राक्षसो युद्धहरणात्पैशाचः कन्यकाछलात् ॥ 19 ॥
2.18.m: is named Gāndharva, and its mark is mutual passion; / Rākṣasa is through abduction in battle; Paiśāca is by trickery toward the maiden.

2.18.s:
prājāpatyastathā brāhmaḥ samavarṇeṣu pūjyate ..
daivastu brāhmaṇasyaiva naiva cānyasya kasyacit .. 2.87.20 ..
2.18.d:
प्राजापत्यस्तथा ब्राह्मः समवर्णेषु पूज्यते ॥
दैवस्तु ब्राह्मणस्यैव नैव चान्यस्य कस्यचित् ॥ 2.87.20 ॥
2.18.m: The Prājāpatya as well as the Brāhma are praised within the same class; / but the Daiva belongs only to a brahmin, and never to anyone else.

2.18.s:
gāndharvarākṣasau śreṣṭhau kṣattriyasyaiva bhārgava ..
pūrvaṃ vivāhātkartavyaḥ śacīyāgo bhṛgūttama .. 21 ..
2.18.d:
गान्धर्वराक्षसौ श्रेष्ठौ क्षत्त्रियस्यैव भार्गव ॥
पूर्वं विवाहात्कर्तव्यः शचीयागो भृगूत्तम ॥ 21 ॥
2.18.m: The Gāndharva and Rākṣasa are best for a kṣatriya, descendant of Bhṛgu. / Prior to marriage, the sacrifice to Śacī must be performed, foremost of the Bhṛgus.

2.18.s:
vaivāhikendau kurvīta kumbhakāramṛdā śacīm ..
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyuktāṃ kuśalena ca śilpinā .. 22 ..
2.18.d:
वैवाहिकेन्दौ कुर्वीत कुम्भकारमृदा शचीम् ॥
सर्वलक्षणसंयुक्तां कुशलेन च शिल्पिना ॥ 22 ॥
2.18.m: Under the asterism of marriage, one should make [an image of] Śacī with potter’s clay, / endowed with all auspicious marks and crafted by a skilled artisan.

2.18.s:
tāṃ nayetsarasastīraṃ nadītīramathāpi vā ..
sarvabhūṣaṇasaṃpannā sarvāstvavidhavāḥ striyaḥ .. 23 ..
2.18.d:
तां नयेत्सरसस्तीरं नदीतीरमथापि वा ॥
सर्वभूषणसंपन्ना सर्वास्त्वविधवाः स्त्रियः ॥ 23 ॥
2.18.m: Women who are not widows, adorned with all ornaments, / should carry it to the bank of a lake or to the bank of a river.

2.18.s:
kausuṃbharaktavasanāḥ sarvāḥ syuḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ ..
mālyānulepanairbhakṣyairdīpairdhūpaistathaiva ca .. 24 ..
2.18.d:
कौसुंभरक्तवसनाः सर्वाः स्युः शस्त्रपाणयः ॥
माल्यानुलेपनैर्भक्ष्यैर्दीपैर्धूपैस्तथैव च ॥ 24 ॥
2.18.m: All wearing red garments dyed with safflower, carrying weapons in hand, / with garlands, unguents, edible foods, lamps, and likewise incenses,

2.18.s:
kausuṃbharaktairvastraiśca bhūṣaṇaiścaiva śaktitaḥ ..
tataḥ śūrpeṇa tāḥ sādhvyo dikṣu dattvā baliṃ śubham .. 25 ..
2.18.d:
कौसुंभरक्तैर्वस्त्रैश्च भूषणैश्चैव शक्तितः ॥
ततः शूर्पेण ताः साध्व्यो दिक्षु दत्त्वा बलिं शुभम् ॥ 25 ॥
2.18.m: and with red garments dyed with safflower and ornaments according to their means— / then, having offered a propitious oblation in the directions with a winnowing basket, those virtuous women,

2.18.s:
saṃyamya keśānprayatā gṛhītvā ca tathā śacīm ..
vādyagītena mahatā dvijavācanakena ca .. 26 ..
2.18.d:
संयम्य केशान्प्रयता गृहीत्वा च तथा शचीम् ॥
वाद्यगीतेन महता द्विजवाचनकेन च ॥ 26 ॥
2.18.m: having tied up their hair, pure, and taking up Śacī, / with loud instrumental music and singing and with the recitation of blessings by twice-borns,

2.18.s:
gṛhe praveśayetpuṃsāṃ śakrapatnīmaniṃditām ..
trisandhyaṃ tatra sā pūjyā gandhamālyānnasampadā .. 27 ..
2.18.d:
गृहे प्रवेशयेत्पुंसां शक्रपत्नीमनिंदिताम् ॥
त्रिसन्ध्यं तत्र सा पूज्या गन्धमाल्यान्नसम्पदा ॥ 27 ॥
2.18.m: should lead the unblemished wife of Śakra into the house of the men. / There she is to be worshiped at the three junctures of the day with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, and food.

2.18.s:
vandanīyodvāhasamaye tatra kālaṃ nibodha me ..
prasupte keśave rāma na tu kāryaṃ kathañcana .. 28 ..
2.18.d:
वन्दनीयोद्वाहसमये तत्र कालं निबोध मे ॥
प्रसुप्ते केशवे राम न तु कार्यं कथञ्चन ॥ 28 ॥
2.18.m: She should be honored at the time of the wedding; learn from me the proper time for that: / when Keśava is asleep, Rāma, it must not be performed under any circumstances;

2.18.s:
na pauṣe na tathā caitre na cārkakujavāsare ..
kṛṣṇatribhāge naivāntye nādye śuklasya bhārgava..29..
2.18.d:
न पौषे न तथा चैत्रे न चार्ककुजवासरे ॥
कृष्णत्रिभागे नैवान्त्ये नाद्ये शुक्लस्य भार्गव॥29॥
2.18.m: neither in Pauṣa, nor in Caitra, nor on a day of the Sun or of Mars; / neither in the last third of the dark fortnight, nor in the first [third] of the bright, descendant of Bhṛgu;

2.18.s:
tathā riktatithau naiva na viṣṭau karaṇe tathā ..
na śukre'stamanaṃ prāpte tathā cāste bṛhaspatau ..2.87.30..
2.18.d:
तथा रिक्ततिथौ नैव न विष्टौ करणे तथा ॥
न शुक्रेऽस्तमनं प्राप्ते तथा चास्ते बृहस्पतौ ॥2.87.30॥
2.18.m: likewise never on an empty lunar day, nor during the Viṣṭi astrological division; / neither when Venus has set, nor when Jupiter has set;

2.18.s:
śaśāṃke'nyagrahāścaiva vivāho na praśasyate ..
arkārkibhaumayukte bhe vyatīpātahate tathā ..31..
2.18.d:
शशांकेऽन्यग्रहाश्चैव विवाहो न प्रशस्यते ॥
अर्कार्किभौमयुक्ते भे व्यतीपातहते तथा ॥31॥
2.18.m: nor when other planets [afflict] the Moon—marriage is not recommended [then]; / nor when an asterism is joined with the Sun, Saturn, or Mars, nor when struck by Vyatīpāta;

2.18.s:
divyāntarikṣabhaumena tathotpātena ghātite ..
tathā śikhiśikhādhvaste saiṃhikeyayute tathā ..32..
2.18.d:
दिव्यान्तरिक्षभौमेन तथोत्पातेन घातिते ॥
तथा शिखिशिखाध्वस्ते सैंहिकेययुते तथा ॥32॥
2.18.m: nor when afflicted by a celestial, atmospheric, or terrestrial portent; / nor when destroyed by a comet's tail, nor when joined with Rāhu.

2.18.s:
vaivāhikānyato vakṣye nakṣatrāṇi bhṛgūttama ..
saumyaṃ pitryaṃ ca vāyavyaṃ sāvitraṃ rauhiṇaṃ tathā..33..
2.18.d:
वैवाहिकान्यतो वक्ष्ये नक्षत्राणि भृगूत्तम ॥
सौम्यं पित्र्यं च वायव्यं सावित्रं रौहिणं तथा॥33॥
2.18.m: Hereafter I shall speak of the asterisms suitable for marriage, foremost of the Bhṛgus: / Mṛgaśīrṣa, Maghā, Svātī, Hasta, and Rohiṇī;

2.18.s:
uttarātritayaṃ mūlaṃ maitraṃ pauṣṇaṃ tathaiva ca ..
mūhūrtāśca tathaiteṣāṃ śubhā abhijitā saha ..34..
2.18.d:
उत्तरात्रितयं मूलं मैत्रं पौष्णं तथैव च ॥
मूहूर्ताश्च तथैतेषां शुभा अभिजिता सह ॥34॥
2.18.m: the three Uttarās, Mūla, Anurādhā, and Revatī; / and the moments of these together with Abhijit are auspicious.

2.18.s:
mānuṣyākhyastathā lagno mānuṣyākhyastathāṃśakaḥ ..
amānuṣyākhye lagne'pi mānuṣyākhyeṃśako hitaḥ ..35..
2.18.d:
मानुष्याख्यस्तथा लग्नो मानुष्याख्यस्तथांशकः ॥
अमानुष्याख्ये लग्नेऽपि मानुष्याख्येंशको हितः ॥35॥
2.18.m: The ascendant termed human and the division termed human [are recommended]; / even when the ascendant is non-human, a division termed human is beneficial.

2.18.s:
tṛtīye ca tathā ṣaṣṭhe daśamaikādaśāṣṭame ..
arkārkibhaumatanayāḥ praśastā na kujoṣṭamaḥ .. 36 ..
2.18.d:
तृतीये च तथा षष्ठे दशमैकादशाष्टमे ॥
अर्कार्किभौमतनयाः प्रशस्ता न कुजोष्टमः ॥ 36 ॥
2.18.m: In the third, sixth, tenth, and eleventh [houses], / the Sun, Saturn, and the son of Mars [Mercury] are praised, but Mars is not [praised] in the eighth.

2.18.s:
saptāntyāṣṭamavarjyeṣu śeṣāḥ śastā grahottamāḥ ..
teṣāmapi tathā sūryaścandraḥ ṣaṣṭho na śasyate .. 37
2.18.d:
सप्तान्त्याष्टमवर्ज्येषु शेषाः शस्ता ग्रहोत्तमाः ॥
तेषामपि तथा सूर्यश्चन्द्रः षष्ठो न शस्यते ॥ 37
2.18.m: Excluding the seventh, twelfth, and eighth, the remaining excellent planets are auspicious; / even among them, the Sun and the Moon in the sixth are not commended.

2.18.s:
saṃkalpavidhinā kāryo vivāhastadanantaram ..
vaivāhike'hni kartavyāstathaiva ca caturthike .. .. 38 ..
2.18.d:
संकल्पविधिना कार्यो विवाहस्तदनन्तरम् ॥
वैवाहिकेऽह्नि कर्तव्यास्तथैव च चतुर्थिके ॥ ॥ 38 ॥
2.18.m: After that, the marriage is to be performed according to the rule of ritual intention; / [the rites] are to be performed on the day of the wedding and likewise on the fourth day.

2.18.s:
na dātavyā grahāstatra caturādyāstathaikagāḥ ..
ataḥ paraṃ gṛhe gacchedṛtukāle sadā striyam .. 39 ..
2.18.d:
न दातव्या ग्रहास्तत्र चतुराद्यास्तथैकगाः ॥
अतः परं गृहे गच्छेदृतुकाले सदा स्त्रियम् ॥ 39 ॥
2.18.m: Planets starting from the fourth and situated singly must not be cast there. / Thereafter, he should always approach his wife in the house during her fertile period.

2.18.s:
parvavarjyaṃ sadā gacchetstrīṇāṃ vā saṃsmaranvaram ..
sarvakālaṃ ratirdattā tāsāṃ satyaṃ bhṛgūttama ..2.87.40 ..
2.18.d:
पर्ववर्ज्यं सदा गच्छेत्स्त्रीणां वा संस्मरन्वरम् ॥
सर्वकालं रतिर्दत्ता तासां सत्यं भृगूत्तम ॥2.87.40 ॥
2.18.m: Excluding the sacred days, he should always approach her, or remembering the boon granted to women: / sexual pleasure was granted to them at all times—this is the truth, foremost of the Bhṛgus.

2.18.s:
parasparātikramaṇaṃ daṃpatyoḥ parivarjayet ..
niṣkāraṇaṃ tathā rāma na kāryamadhivedanam ..41..
2.18.d:
परस्परातिक्रमणं दंपत्योः परिवर्जयेत् ॥
निष्कारणं तथा राम न कार्यमधिवेदनम् ॥41॥
2.18.m: Mutual transgressions between husband and wife should be avoided; / and taking another wife must not be done without cause, Rāma.

2.18.s:
aprajā rogiṇī mūḍhā tathā ca kalahapriyā ..
kanyāprajā tathā yā ca yā caivāpriyavādinī .. 42 ..
2.18.d:
अप्रजा रोगिणी मूढा तथा च कलहप्रिया ॥
कन्याप्रजा तथा या च या चैवाप्रियवादिनी ॥ 42 ॥
2.18.m: A barren woman, a sick woman, a foolish woman, one fond of quarreling, / one who bears only daughters, and one who speaks unpleasantly—

2.18.s:
etāḥ khalvadhivettavyā gṛhakāryaparāṅmukhīḥ ..
adhivinnā viśeṣeṇa pālanīyā sutaṃ bhavet ..43..
2.18.d:
एताः खल्वधिवेत्तव्या गृहकार्यपराङ्मुखीः ॥
अधिविन्ना विशेषेण पालनीया सुतं भवेत् ॥43॥
2.18.m: these indeed, if averse to household duties, may be superseded. / Even when superseded, she must especially be maintained, as if she were a son.

2.18.s:
dharmakāryeṣu sarveṣu tathā jyeṣṭhāṃ niyojayet ..
dharmādharmau samau rāma dampatyorubhayātmakau .. 44..
2.18.d:
धर्मकार्येषु सर्वेषु तथा ज्येष्ठां नियोजयेत् ॥
धर्माधर्मौ समौ राम दम्पत्योरुभयात्मकौ ॥ 44॥
2.18.m: He should employ the senior wife in all religious duties; / dharma and adharma are equal, Rāma, pertaining to both husband and wife.

2.18.s:
poṣyā ca nityaṃ paripālanīyā bhāryā bhaveddharmaparāyaṇasya ..
dharmārthakāmānsatataṃ dvijendra tānrakṣayetsamyagathānayā svān.. 45 ..
2.18.d:
पोष्या च नित्यं परिपालनीया भार्या भवेद्धर्मपरायणस्य ॥
धर्मार्थकामान्सततं द्विजेन्द्र तान्रक्षयेत्सम्यगथानया स्वान्॥ 45 ॥
2.18.m: The wife of a man devoted to dharma should always be supported and protected; / through her, prince of twice-borns, he should properly and constantly protect his own dharma, wealth, and pleasure.

2.18.s:
iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare dvitīyakhaṇḍe mā0 saṃ0 rāmaṃ prati puṣkaropākhyāne dharmavarṇanannāma saptāśītitamodhyām .. 87
2.88
.. puṣkara uvāca ..
nidrāṃ jahyād gṛhī rāma nityamevāruṇodaye ..
vegotsargaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā dantadhāvanapūrvakam .. 1 ..
snānaṃ samācaretprātaḥ sarvakalmaṣanāśanam ..
vegotsargaṃ na kurvīta phālakṛṣṭe tathā śucau .. 2 ..
goṣṭhe na cāgnau na taṭe drumacchāyāsu śādvale ..
pathi bhasmani toye ca nāṃgaṇe na ca gopathe .. 3 ..
nāgnyarkānāgatoyeṣu prativāte tathaiva ca ..
na vegito na kāryastho vegotsargaṃ samācaret .. 4 ..
udaṅmukhastu sandhyāsu divā vai bhṛgunandana ..
dakṣiṇābhimukho rātrau nākāśe tu kathañcana .. 5 ..
karṇasthabrahmasūtrastu vastrācchāditamastakaḥ ..
abhyuddhṛtābhiradbhistu mṛdbhiḥ śaucaṃ samācaret .. 6 ..
2.18.d:
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे द्वितीयखण्डे मा0 सं0 रामं प्रति पुष्करोपाख्याने धर्मवर्णनन्नाम सप्ताशीतितमोध्याम् ॥ 87
2.88
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥
निद्रां जह्याद् गृही राम नित्यमेवारुणोदये ॥
वेगोत्सर्गं ततः कृत्वा दन्तधावनपूर्वकम् ॥ 1 ॥
स्नानं समाचरेत्प्रातः सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥
वेगोत्सर्गं न कुर्वीत फालकृष्टे तथा शुचौ ॥ 2 ॥
गोष्ठे न चाग्नौ न तटे द्रुमच्छायासु शाद्वले ॥
पथि भस्मनि तोये च नांगणे न च गोपथे ॥ 3 ॥
नाग्न्यर्कानागतोयेषु प्रतिवाते तथैव च ॥
न वेगितो न कार्यस्थो वेगोत्सर्गं समाचरेत् ॥ 4 ॥
उदङ्मुखस्तु सन्ध्यासु दिवा वै भृगुनन्दन ॥
दक्षिणाभिमुखो रात्रौ नाकाशे तु कथञ्चन ॥ 5 ॥
कर्णस्थब्रह्मसूत्रस्तु वस्त्राच्छादितमस्तकः ॥
अभ्युद्धृताभिरद्भिस्तु मृद्भिः शौचं समाचरेत् ॥ 6 ॥
2.18.m:
Thus ends the eighty-seventh chapter, entitled 'Description of Dharma,' in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Rāma, in the discourse of Puṣkara, in the second book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.
Puṣkara said: / A householder should abandon sleep at dawn every day, Rāma; / having then answered the calls of nature, preceded by brushing the teeth,
he should perform the morning bath that destroys all sins. / He should not answer the calls of nature on ploughed land, nor on pure ground,
nor in a cowpen, nor into fire, nor on a riverbank, nor in the shadows of trees, nor on turf, / nor on a road, nor on ashes, nor in water, nor in a courtyard, nor on a cattle path,
nor facing fire, the sun, or water, and likewise not against the wind; / he should not answer the calls of nature while rushing or engaged in work.
Facing north during the twilights and during the day, son of Bhṛgu, / but facing south at night, and never out in the open air.
With the sacred thread placed on the ear and head covered with cloth, / he should perform purification with fetched water and with earth.

2.18.s:
kṛtaśaucaḥ śucau deśe prāṅmukhaḥ susamāhitaḥ ..
udaṅmukhastu dharmajña tathāntarjānureva ca .. 7 ..
upaspṛśecca dharmajña śuddhapādakaraḥ sadā ..
ekahastārpitenā'tha pheṇabudbudinā tathā .. 8 ..
agnipakvena toyena nanu nopaspṛśedbudhaḥ ..
aṅgulyagre bhaveddaivaṃ brāhmamaṅgulimūlake ..9..
paitryaṃ tarjanimūle syātkaniṣṭhāyāśca mānuṣam ..
brāhmeṇa triḥ pibedāpaḥ pramṛjyāttu tato mukham ..2.88.10 ..
khānyadbhiḥ saṃspṛśetpaścānmūrdhānaṃ nābhimeva ca ..
upaspṛśya tataḥ paścādbhakṣayeddantadhāvanam .. 11 ..
bhuktvā ca nikṣipedrāma nityameva samāhitaḥ ..
udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vā na yāmyāśāparāṅmukhaḥ..12..
māṃsanna bhakṣayeccaiva nordhaśuṣkaṃ na picchilam..
suśiraṃ madhuraṃ cāmlaṃ vitvacaṃ patrasaṃyutama..13..
2.18.d:
कृतशौचः शुचौ देशे प्राङ्मुखः सुसमाहितः ॥
उदङ्मुखस्तु धर्मज्ञ तथान्तर्जानुरेव च ॥ 7 ॥
उपस्पृशेच्च धर्मज्ञ शुद्धपादकरः सदा ॥
एकहस्तार्पितेनाऽथ फेणबुद्बुदिना तथा ॥ 8 ॥
अग्निपक्वेन तोयेन ननु नोपस्पृशेद्बुधः ॥
अङ्गुल्यग्रे भवेद्दैवं ब्राह्ममङ्गुलिमूलके ॥9॥
पैत्र्यं तर्जनिमूले स्यात्कनिष्ठायाश्च मानुषम् ॥
ब्राह्मेण त्रिः पिबेदापः प्रमृज्यात्तु ततो मुखम् ॥2.88.10 ॥
खान्यद्भिः संस्पृशेत्पश्चान्मूर्धानं नाभिमेव च ॥
उपस्पृश्य ततः पश्चाद्भक्षयेद्दन्तधावनम् ॥ 11 ॥

He should chew [the twigs of] the banyan, asana, arka, khadira, and karavīra, / as well as jātī, aśva, bilva, badara, and the root of kakubha,
and arimeda, priyaṅgu, and thorny plants, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / Having washed it first, he should chew it, and having washed it again, he should discard it.
If it falls facing [him], it is auspicious; facing a calm quarter brings a [favourable] day. / Desiring good fortune, well-restrained, he should chew it first towards the east with his left [side],
O knower of dharma, and with restrained speech he should chew with the front portion. / Then, having performed purification of impurities, he should properly take a bath.
He should not bathe having eaten, nor in an unknown body of water, / nor when sick, nor when the sky is not yet touched by the dawn's rays.
Bathing at night is not recommended, except upon seeing Rāhu, / likewise in another's water [when] small, and by no means without [wetting] the head.

तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन प्रातःस्नानं समाचरेत्॥23॥

यः करोति सदा राम स्नानं तु सवनद्वयम् ॥24॥
स तु स्वर्गमनुप्राप्य त्रिदशैरपि पूज्यते ॥

रूपौदार्यगुणोपेताः स्त्रियश्चाप्नोत्यनिन्दिताः ॥

2.18.m:
Obligatory, occasional, optional, forming part of a rite, removing impurities, / and sixth is ritual bath; thus the bath is proclaimed to be of six kinds.
The bodily openings of a sleeping person discharge at night; / therefore, with all effort, he should perform the morning bath.
One who always bathes in the morning, O Rāma, never sees hell. / He who always performs bathing at the two junctions, O Rāma,
attains heaven and is honoured even by the gods. / Likewise, one who bathes at the three junctions is magnified in the world of heaven.
Attaining human birth, he becomes endowed with beauty and youth, / and is born into a flourishing family rich in wealth and grain.
He obtains irreproachable wives endowed with beauty, generosity, and virtues; / his mind is set on dharma, and he shines with fame.
Therefore, O Rāma, one devoted to dharma should always perform bathing / in prominent pilgrimage places and lakes—a bath that removes deep impurities, grants heaven, fulfills desires, and brings happiness.

Puṣkara said: / A garland named 'fortune-bringer' he should always wear on his head; / a wise man should not wear it elsewhere, nor should he wear external scent.
That which is produced from thorny plants, [or] black and red, O descendant of Bhṛgu— / but that which is white, even if born of thorny plants, may be worn.
Black and red may also be worn if born in water. / With his limbs anointed with sandalwood, saffron, and aloe,
as well as with camphor and auspicious priyaṅgu, [he should proceed]. / Clothing worn by another should not be worn, nor red, nor soiled,
nor worn out, nor lacking fringes; white should be worn with effort. / He should not wear shoes worn by another, and he should wear the sacred thread.
He should never travel with those who have missing limbs or extra limbs, / with children, the elderly, the hungry, fierce beasts, or untrained draft animals;
he should not perform bathing, eating, drinking, and the like before them. / He should not travel a road alone, nor with an adharmic companion,

कथाभङ्गं न कुर्वीत न च वासोविपर्ययम् ॥।

सुरार्चा गुरुभूपानां ब्राह्मणानां विशेषतः ॥
नाक्रमेच्च तथा छायां श्वपचस्य च भार्गव ॥ 2.89.30 ॥
द्विजयोश्चैव दम्पत्योर्भूपयोर्युध्यमानयोः ॥
अग्निब्राह्मणयोश्चैव द्विजभूपालयोस्तथा ॥ 31 ॥
शिष्योपाध्याययोश्चैव न च मध्ये न पूज्ययोः ॥
तैले जले तथा वक्त्रमादर्शे च मलान्विते ॥ 32 ॥
न पश्येन्न तथा पश्येदुपरक्तं दिवाकरम् ॥
नोच्छिष्टस्तारकाराहुः स्तुतिनाशं हुताशनम् ॥ 33 ॥
न तिष्ठेत्प्रतिवातं च तथा च प्रतिभास्करम् ॥
न संहताभ्यां पाणिभ्यां कण्डूयेदात्मनः शिरः ॥ 34 ॥
रोदनं च तथा नग्नः कुर्यात्तोयावगाहनम् ॥
निष्कारणं नदीपारं बाहुभ्यां न तरेत्तथा ॥ 35 ॥
न प्रशंसेन्नदी तोये नदीमन्यां कथंचन ॥
न गिरौ पर्वतं राम न राज्ञः पुरतो नृपम् ॥36॥
2.18.m:
And he should not step upon the shadow of the image of a deity, of elders, kings, / especially brahmins, nor of an outcaste, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
nor between two twice-born, a married couple, two kings who are fighting, / fire and a brahmin, or a twice-born and a ruler,
nor between a disciple and a teacher, nor between two persons worthy of worship. / One should not look at one's face in oil, in water, or in a mirror covered with dirt;
nor should one look at the sun during an eclipse. / One should not look when ritually impure at the stars, Rāhu, a ruined monument, or fire.
One should not stand facing the wind, nor facing the sun. / One should not scratch one's own head with both hands joined.
One should not weep, nor enter the water naked. / One should not cross to the other bank of a river with one's arms without a reason.
While in the water of a river, one should never praise another river, / nor praise a mountain while on a mountain, O Rāma, nor a king before a king.

2.18.d:
असंतर्प्य पितुर्देयं नदीपारं न च व्रजेत् ॥
भोजनं वर्जयेन्नावि ष्ठीवनं च तथांभसि ॥ 37 ॥
नैवाप्सु प्रक्षिपेद्विद्वानमेध्यं रुधिरं विषम् ॥
समाल्यो नाचरेत्स्नानं न द्विवासा विकारणम् ॥38 ॥
आत्मनश्च तथा राम नैव त्वपनयेत्स्रजम् ॥
स्नातः शिरो नावधुनेन्नांगेभ्यस्तोयमुद्धरेत् ॥ 39 ॥
तद्दिने चानुलिप्तांगं तथा स्नानं विवर्जयेत् ॥
शिरःस्नातश्च तैलेन स्पृशेदंगं न किञ्चन ॥ 2.89.40 ॥
वाससा वामभागस्य रजसा पूर्ववाससा ॥
संमार्जनं रजोवर्ज्यः खराश्वादेस्तथैव च ॥ 41 ॥
मेध्यानि च तथा राम गोगजाश्वरजांसि च ॥
नाधः कुर्वीत दहनं न च पादौ प्रतापयेत् ॥ 42 ॥
दर्भैर्न मार्जयेत्पादौ न च कांस्ये प्रधापयेत् ॥
गोगजाश्वाजपुच्छेषु खरस्य च विशेषतः ॥ 43 ॥
2.18.m:
Without offering what is due to one's ancestors, one should not cross to the other bank of a river. / One should avoid eating on a boat, and spitting into water.
A wise man should never throw impure matter, blood, or poison into water. / One wearing a garland should not bathe, nor one wearing two garments without reason.
Nor, O Rāma, should one remove one's own garland. / Once bathed, one should not shake one's head, nor wipe the water off one's limbs.
On that day, one should avoid anointing one's limbs and bathing again. / And having bathed one's head, one should not touch any part of one's body with oil.
One should avoid being wiped with a cloth from the left side, with dust, or with a garment worn previously, / and should avoid dust from donkeys, horses, and the like;
and the dust from cows, elephants, and horses, O Rāma, is pure. / One should not place fire beneath oneself, nor warm one's feet [at it].
One should not wipe one's feet with darbha grass, nor rub them on bell-metal. / On the tails of cows, elephants, horses, and goats, and especially of a donkey,

यल्लग्नमुदकं तस्माद्विप्रुषो दूरतस्त्यजेत् ॥
अकस्मादप्यशस्तास्ताः खञ्जांगस्पर्शनं तथा ॥ 44 ॥
हीनं वा न वहेद्राम श्रुतरूपधनादिभिः॥

न भूपालविहीने च न सांवत्सरवर्जिते ॥

स्त्रीनायके बालपतौ शूद्रराज्ये तथैव च ॥
म्लेच्छवेषो न कर्तव्यो म्लेच्छभाषा तथैव च ॥ 47 ॥
चण्डालैः पतितैर्म्लेच्छैर्भाषणं न कदाचन ॥
नकारं कायतः कृत्वा कीर्तयेत्केशवं विभुम् ॥ 48 ॥
नासंवृतमुखः कुर्याद्धासं जृम्भां तथा क्षुतम् ॥
गोपयेज्जन्मनक्षत्रमृणसारं गृहे मलम् ॥ 49 ॥
प्रभोरप्यवमानं स्वं तस्य दुश्चरितं च यत् ॥
नानुकूल्यं तथा कार्यमिन्द्रियाणां सुखेप्सुना ॥ 2.89.50 ॥
2.18.m:
one should avoid from afar any drops of water clinging to them; / even accidentally, those are unwholesome, as is touching a crippled limb.
One should not carry one who is inferior in learning, appearance, wealth, and the like, O Rāma; / one should not live with inferior people, nor in a country lacking a physician,
nor in one without a king, nor in one without an astrologer, / nor in one containing bad wells, O Rāma, nor in one with many leaders,
nor in one led by a woman, or ruled by a child, or in a kingdom ruled by a śūdra. / One should not adopt the dress of a barbarian, nor the speech of a barbarian.
One should never converse with caṇḍālas, outcasts, or barbarians. / Having refrained from negativity through one's body, one should glorify the all-pervading Keśava.
One should not laugh, yawn, or sneeze without covering one's mouth. / One should conceal one's birth constellation, the amount of one's debt, and dirt in one's house,
as well as any insult to oneself from a master, and whatever bad conduct he has. / Seeking happiness, one should not indulge the senses;

युक्त्या च कामसेवी स्यान्नाकस्मान्निःसुखी भवेत् ॥
वेगरोधं न कर्तव्यमन्यत्र क्रोधवेगतः ॥ 51 ॥।
नोपेक्षितव्यो व्याधिः स्याद्रिपुरल्पोऽपि भार्गव ॥
स्नात्वा भुक्त्वा च धर्मज्ञ भक्तिकामः सुरार्चने ॥ 52 ॥
मलायनानां संस्पर्शे मलानां चैव भार्गव ॥
वाससश्च परीधाने रथ्याचंक्रमणे तथा ॥ 53 ॥
आचमेच्च तथा राम तथा स्वप्नोत्थितो नरः ॥
न हुंकुर्याच्छिवं पूज्यं बिभृयान्नाग्निचारिणीम्॥54॥
न भुक्तमात्रं प्रायस्येन्नीचसेवां विवर्जयेत् ॥
पादेन नाक्रमेत्पादं न कण्डूयेन्न शौचयेत् ॥55 ॥
वर्जयेच्छवधूमं च गिरं चाश्लीलसंयुताम् ॥
प्रत्यक्षं वा परोक्षं वा कस्यचिन्नाप्रियं वदेत् ॥ 56 ॥
वेदशास्त्रनरेन्द्रर्षिदेवनिन्दां विवर्जयेत् ॥
नास्तिक्यमनृतं चैव चेतसो दूषणं तथा ॥ 57 ॥
2.18.m:
one should indulge in desires with moderation, and should not suddenly become destitute of joy. / One should not suppress natural urges, except for the surge of anger.
Even a minor disease or an enemy should not be neglected, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / Having bathed and eaten, O knower of dharma, when desirous of devotion in the worship of the gods,
or upon touching the apertures of bodily excretion or excretions themselves, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / or when putting on a garment, or wandering on a public road,
or when rising from sleep, a man should sip water, O Rāma. / One should not utter the syllable ‘huṃ’ at a deity worthy of worship; one should not maintain a woman who plays with fire.
One should not exert oneself immediately after eating; one should avoid serving the low. / One should not step on one foot with the other, nor scratch it, nor wash it [with it].
One should avoid the smoke of a corpse and speech that is vulgar. / One should not speak what is disagreeable to anyone, whether directly or behind their back.
One should avoid reviling the Vedas, treatises, kings, sages, and gods, / as well as atheism, falsehood, and corruption of the mind.

2.18.d:
स्त्रीणामीर्ष्या न कर्तव्या विश्वासं तासु वर्जयेत् ॥
लाडितास्ताडिताः कार्या देहे स्वे स्त्रीकुमारिकाः ॥ ॥ 58 ॥
सर्वेषामेव धर्माणां कर्तव्यं श्रवणं तथा ॥
नमस्कारं च देवानां सर्वेषामेव कारयेत् ॥ 59 ॥
सर्वेषां चरितं राम धर्मतो न विकुत्सयेत् ॥
न चाचरेच्च धर्मज्ञ ते हि तेजोपहाहताः ॥2.89.60॥
धर्मस्यार्थस्य कामस्य पीडावर्ज्या परस्परम् ॥
देवस्य वयसश्चैव शिल्पस्य स्वकुलस्य च ॥61॥
आचरेत्सदृशं वेषं व्यवसायानुरूपतः ॥
स्नात एवाशु बिभृयात्सोष्णीषे धौतवाससी ॥ 62 ॥
अनुलिप्येत्तथांगानि सितं माल्यं च धारयेत् ॥
नासंस्कृतं च बिभृयात्काञ्चनं पुरुषोत्तम ॥63॥
निराशनस्य सुप्तस्य शयानस्य तथैव च ॥
तथा भुक्तवतो राम स्नातस्य भाषितस्य च ॥64॥
2.18.m:
One should not be jealous of women, [yet] one should avoid placing trust in them. / Women and young girls should be fondled and disciplined within one's own family.
One should listen to all dharmas, / and one should offer obeisance to all the gods.
One should not despise the conduct of everyone, O Rāma, in terms of dharma, / nor should one practice [bad conduct], O knower of dharma, for such people are struck down by the loss of their splendour.
One should avoid mutual injury between dharma, wealth, and pleasure. / Befitting the deity, one's age, one's craft, and one's family,
one should adopt suitable attire in accordance with one's occupation. / Just after bathing, one should promptly put on clean garments along with a turban,
anoint one's limbs, and wear a white garland; / and one should not wear gold that has not been purified, O Puruṣottama.
For one who is fasting, asleep, lying down, / or who has just eaten, O Rāma, or has just bathed or spoken,

2.18.m:
or who is eager for travel or battle, shaving should be avoided. / The constellations presided over by Viṣṇu, Varuṇa, Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ, and Indra,
by Vāyu, Mitra, Pūṣan, Śakra, and the Aśvins, / by Mitra and Aditi, and Puṣya, form the group belonging to the conch and the discus.
The muhūrtas of these constellations bring well-being. / The days of the Sun, Saturn, and Mars, and the empty lunar days,
as well as the first and the sixth lunar days, should be avoided for the act of shaving. / One should avoid one's birth constellation, and likewise any that is not favourable.
When a benefic planet is in one's birth constellation, after carefully washing one's head, / one should worship Soma, as well as the constellation and oneself.
One should carefully perform a śrāddha and the worship of fire and brahmins; / one's vehicle, weapons, parasol, and other items should be carefully worshipped.
Worship of the gods should be performed, especially of Keśava. / Having bathed his head, a man should remain composed and well-adorned;

2.18.m:
and one's teeth, hair, and nails should be made clean. / On the eighth, sixth, ninth, and fourteenth lunar days,
one should not apply oil to the head, nor on the junction of the parvan days; / likewise, one should avoid bathing with myrobalan on the seventh lunar days.
Except for one's regular daily bath, one should not bathe on the tenth lunar days. / On the new moon day, during the worship of the gods, one should not wear new clothes.
Nor on a Tuesday, O Rāma, and likewise on these days when unanointed: / Hasta, Rohiṇī, Anurādhā, Punarvasu, Puṣya, and Aśvinī,
the triad of Uttarās, Citrā, Śvāti, Dhaniṣṭhā, / Viśākhā, and Revatī—these one should declare to be auspicious.
Moreover, the muhūrtas of these asterisms bestow benefit. / One should carefully avoid hostility toward others as well as injury.
Likewise, pulling hair and blows to the head are to be avoided. / Far from one's dwelling one should discharge urine and feces,

and the washing of feet, broken pots and the like; / a wise man should cast aside all of this, by which there would be destruction of enemies.
One should throw out rice water away from oneself. / Likewise, with a single mind, worship of the deities is to be performed,
and worship of the fire; and it must not be done while unbathed, O Bhārgava. / One should not take for oneself the garlands, unguents, and the like of anyone else,
or those of deities, brahmins, and gurus, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / One should avoid vegetables of the kovidāra class, fourth-[day vegetables], long pepper,
and all meat whatsoever, if one desires happiness. / One should not do what is hated by the king, nor enter into conflict with eminent persons.
One should diligently avoid unprovoked enmity and dispute. / Nor should one dwell in a house condemned by the science of architecture.
One should avoid earth from a house, earth dug up by mice, that left over from another's use, / that from saline soil, and that from an anthill, for the purpose of purification.
With whomsoever one desires extensive affection, O subduer of enemies, / one should not make business dealings with him, nor look upon his wife.

2.90
Puṣkara said:
Having sipped water properly, purified, and bathed, one should enter the house of the deity; / there, concentrated in mind, he should make prostration with devotion.
Then with the three verses "āpo hi ṣṭha" he should offer arghya; / and with the three verses "hiraṇyavarṇāḥ" the twice-born should offer pādya.
With the verse "śaṃ na āpaḥ" water for sipping is to be given; / "idam āpaḥ pravahata" is declared to be the bath mantra.
With the four verses "rathe akṣeṣu" unguent is to be offered; / and the mantra "yuvā suvāsāḥ" is prescribed for clothing.
The discerning one should offer a flower with "puṣpavatī", incense with "dhūr asi", / and a lamp with "tejo 'si śukram asi".
Likewise, he should present the honey mixture with "dadhikrāvṇo"; / eight verses beginning with "hiraṇyagarbhaḥ" are declared for the presentation

of food, O best of men, and of fragrant drink; / a fly-whisk, fan, vessel, umbrella, vehicle, and seat,
whatever there may be of this kind, he should present with the Sāvitrī mantra. / And he should recite the Puruṣasūkta, and likewise make oblations with it.
In the absence of an image, a man should worship Keśava / on an altar, on clean ground, in a full water pot, on a riverbank, or in a lotus.
The worship of the foremost of gods, Viṣṇu, destroys all inauspicious things; / having performed it, faultless, he swiftly departs to where he attains union with the Grandfather.

पुष्कर उवाच॥
नक्तं गृहीतमुदकं देवकर्मणि वर्जयेत् ॥
चन्दनागरुकर्पूर मृगदर्पं तथैव च ॥ 1 ॥
2.19.m:
2.91
Puṣkara said:
Water fetched at night should be avoided in rites for deities. / Sandalwood, aloe wood, camphor, and musk,

2.19.s:
jātīphalaṃ tathā dadyādanulepasya kāraṇāt ..
atonyaṃ naiva dātavyaṃ kiñcidevānulepanam .. 2 ..
2.19.d:
जातीफलं तथा दद्यादनुलेपस्य कारणात् ॥
अतोन्यं नैव दातव्यं किञ्चिदेवानुलेपनम् ॥ 2 ॥
2.19.m: and nutmeg one should offer for the sake of unguent. / Other than this, no unguent whatever should be given.

2.19.s:
dāridryaṃ padmakaḥ kuryādasvāsthyaṃ raktacandanam ..
uśīraśca tu vibhraṃśaṃ manye kuryurupadravam .. 3 ..
2.19.d:
दारिद्र्यं पद्मकः कुर्यादस्वास्थ्यं रक्तचन्दनम् ॥
उशीरश्च तु विभ्रंशं मन्ये कुर्युरुपद्रवम् ॥ 3 ॥
2.19.m: Padmaka wood causes poverty; red sandalwood causes illness; / and uśīra grass causes ruin; I consider that they would bring distress.

2.19.s:
na vastraṃ malinaṃ deyaṃ nīlaṃ raktaṃ tu yadbhavet ..
tau dattvā devadevāya śokamāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 4 ..
2.19.d:
न वस्त्रं मलिनं देयं नीलं रक्तं तु यद्भवेत् ॥
तौ दत्त्वा देवदेवाय शोकमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥ 4 ॥
2.19.m: One must not offer soiled cloth, or that which is dark blue or red; / having given those two to the God of gods, one undoubtedly incurs grief.

2.19.s:
kṛtrimaṃ tu na dātavyaṃ tathaivābharaṇaṃ dvija ..
pratirūpakṛtaṃ dattvā kṣipraṃ puṣṭyā viyujyate .. 5 ..
2.19.d:
कृत्रिमं तु न दातव्यं तथैवाभरणं द्विज ॥
प्रतिरूपकृतं दत्त्वा क्षिप्रं पुष्ट्या वियुज्यते ॥ 5 ॥
2.19.m: Likewise, artificial ornament should not be given, O twice-born; / having given an imitation, one is swiftly deprived of prosperity.

2.19.s:
puṣpaṃ kaṇṭakisaṃjātaṃ tathā gandhavivarjitam ..
ugragandhaṃ na dātavyaṃ tvanyadevagṛhodbhavam .. 6 ..
2.19.d:
पुष्पं कण्टकिसंजातं तथा गन्धविवर्जितम् ॥
उग्रगन्धं न दातव्यं त्वन्यदेवगृहोद्भवम् ॥ 6 ॥
2.19.m: A flower produced from a thorny plant, or devoid of fragrance, / or of fierce scent, must not be offered, nor one produced in the shrine of another deity,

2.19.s:
śmaśānacaityadrumajaṃ bhūmāvaśanipātitam ..
kalikā na tu dātavyā devadevasya cakriṇaḥ .. 7 ..
2.19.d:
श्मशानचैत्यद्रुमजं भूमावशनिपातितम् ॥
कलिका न तु दातव्या देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ॥ 7 ॥
2.19.m: nor that grown on a tree in a cremation ground or sacred enclosure, nor that struck down to the ground by lightning; / and an unopened bud must not be offered to the disc-bearing God of gods.

2.19.s:
śuklānyavarṇaṃ kusumaṃ na deyaṃ ca tathā bhavet ..
sugandhi śuklaṃ deyaṃ syājjātaṃ kaṇṭakite drume.8..
2.19.d:
शुक्लान्यवर्णं कुसुमं न देयं च तथा भवेत् ॥
सुगन्धि शुक्लं देयं स्याज्जातं कण्टकिते द्रुमे.8॥
2.19.m: A flower of a color other than white should likewise not be given; / a white, fragrant one produced on a thorny tree, however, should be given.

2.19.s:
dattvā kaṇṭakisaṃbhūtaṃ kusumaṃ paribhūyate ..
śuklānyavarṇaṃ dātavyaṃ kusumaṃ kuṃkumasya yat .. 9 ..
2.19.d:
दत्त्वा कण्टकिसंभूतं कुसुमं परिभूयते ॥
शुक्लान्यवर्णं दातव्यं कुसुमं कुंकुमस्य यत् ॥ 9 ॥
2.19.m: Having given a flower produced on a thorny plant [otherwise], one is humiliated. / A flower of saffron, even if of a color other than white, may be given,

2.19.s:
padmotpale ca dharmajña tathā vai pītayūthikām ..
tathā ca vanyakaṃ dadyāccūtaketakijaṃ ca yat .. 2.91.10 ..
2.19.d:
पद्मोत्पले च धर्मज्ञ तथा वै पीतयूथिकाम् ॥
तथा च वन्यकं दद्याच्चूतकेतकिजं च यत् ॥ 2.91.10 ॥
2.19.m: as well as the lotus and the water lily, O knower of dharma, and yellow jasmine; / and one may offer wild flowers, and whatever comes from mango and ketakī,

2.19.s:
raktāśokasya kusumamatasīkusumaṃ tathā ..
vṛkṣāyurvedavidbhiśca śuklaṃ raktīkṛtaṃ ca yat ..11..
2.19.d:
रक्ताशोकस्य कुसुममतसीकुसुमं तथा ॥
वृक्षायुर्वेदविद्भिश्च शुक्लं रक्तीकृतं च यत् ॥11॥
2.19.m: and the flower of the red aśoka, and the flax flower, / and what has been made red from white by those who know the science of plant medicine;

2.19.s:
tadraktamapi dātavyaṃ bilvapatraṃ tathaiva ca ..
dūrvāgraṃ ca tathā deyaṃ patraṃ bhṛṅgirajasya tu .. 12 ..
2.19.d:
तद्रक्तमपि दातव्यं बिल्वपत्रं तथैव च ॥
दूर्वाग्रं च तथा देयं पत्रं भृङ्गिरजस्य तु ॥ 12 ॥
2.19.m: even though red, that may be offered; and likewise bilva leaves. / The tip of dūrvā grass should also be given, and the leaf of bhṛṅgarāja;

2.19.s:
patrāṇi ca sugandhīni tathā deyāni cakriṇaḥ ..
madhyo'nyavarṇo yasya syācchuklasya kusumasya ca .. 13 ..
2.19.d:
पत्राणि च सुगन्धीनि तथा देयानि चक्रिणः ॥
मध्योऽन्यवर्णो यस्य स्याच्छुक्लस्य कुसुमस्य च ॥ 13 ॥
2.19.m: and fragrant leaves should likewise be offered to the disc-bearer. / A white flower whose center is of another color

2.19.s:
puṣpaṃ śuklaṃ tu tadvidyānmanojñaṃ keśavapriyam ..
bandhujīvakapuṣpāṇi raktānyapi ca dāpayet .. 14 ..
2.19.d:
पुष्पं शुक्लं तु तद्विद्यान्मनोज्ञं केशवप्रियम् ॥
बन्धुजीवकपुष्पाणि रक्तान्यपि च दापयेत् ॥ 14 ॥
2.19.m: One should know that white flower, pleasing and dear to Keśava. / One should also offer red bandhujīvaka flowers.

2.19.s:
anuktaraktakusuma dānāddaurbhāgyamāpnuyāt ..
sugandhi dattvā nāpnoti śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham .. 15 ..
2.19.d:
अनुक्तरक्तकुसुम दानाद्दौर्भाग्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
सुगन्धि दत्त्वा नाप्नोति शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम् ॥ 15 ॥
2.19.m: From giving a red flower that is not prescribed, one would incur misfortune. / Giving a fragrant one, he incurs neither good nor evil.

2.19.s:
mṛgadarpaṃ vinā kiñcidatha cejjīvasaṃbhavam ..
devadevasya dātavyaṃ dīpe majjānameva vā .. 16 ..
2.19.d:
मृगदर्पं विना किञ्चिदथ चेज्जीवसंभवम् ॥
देवदेवस्य दातव्यं दीपे मज्जानमेव वा ॥ 16 ॥
2.19.m: Except musk, if anything arises from a living creature, / or even marrow, [it should not] be offered in a lamp to the God of gods.

2.19.s:
nīlāṃ raktāṃ daśāṃ dīpe prayatnena vivarjayet ..
anyā ca dīpamātraṃ tu tathā varjaṃ prayatnataḥ ..17 ..
2.19.d:
नीलां रक्तां दशां दीपे प्रयत्नेन विवर्जयेत् ॥
अन्या च दीपमात्रं तु तथा वर्जं प्रयत्नतः ॥17 ॥
2.19.m: One should carefully avoid a blue or red wick in a lamp. / And any other [wick] in an ordinary lamp should likewise be carefully avoided.

2.19.s:
kṛṣṇāgarustathā devadhūpaṃ devasya yatnataḥ ..
abhakṣaṃ cāpyahṛdyaṃ ca naivedyaṃ na nivedayet .. 18 ..
2.19.d:
कृष्णागरुस्तथा देवधूपं देवस्य यत्नतः ॥
अभक्षं चाप्यहृद्यं च नैवेद्यं न निवेदयेत् ॥ 18 ॥
2.19.m: Black agallochum should likewise be carefully offered as divine incense to the god. / And one should not present food offerings that are inedible or unappealing,

2.19.s:
keśakīṭāvapannaṃ ca nakhāṃśavihitaṃ ca yat ..
mūṣikālāṃgalopetamavadhūtamavakṣatam..19..
2.19.d:
केशकीटावपन्नं च नखांशविहितं च यत् ॥
मूषिकालांगलोपेतमवधूतमवक्षतम्॥19॥
2.19.m: or that which is fallen upon by hair or insects, made with parts of nails, / touched by a mouse's tail, swept away, or bitten into.

2.19.s:
na bhakṣyamannamakṣīraṃ māhiṣaṃ kṣīrameva ca ..
varāhamatsyamāṃsaṃ ca māṃsaṃ pañcanakhasya ca ..
durāmodau tathā varjyau devakarmaṇi paṃḍitaiḥ..2.91.20..
2.19.d:
न भक्ष्यमन्नमक्षीरं माहिषं क्षीरमेव च ॥
वराहमत्स्यमांसं च मांसं पञ्चनखस्य च ॥
दुरामोदौ तथा वर्ज्यौ देवकर्मणि पंडितैः॥2.91.20॥
2.19.m: Food that is inedible, [milk that is] not cow's milk, and buffalo's milk, / meat of boar and fish, and the meat of a five-nailed animal, / and foul-smelling things are likewise to be avoided in rites for the gods by the wise.

2.19.s:
niveśya cittaṃ puruṣottamasya bhaktiṃ samāsthāya tathā viśuddhām ..
karoti śraddhāṃ satataṃ yathoktāṃ sa yāti lokaṃ madhusūdanasya ..21..
2.92
puṣkara uvāca ..
tato'gniśaraṇaṃ gatvā smārte'gnau vidhipūrvakam ..
vaiśvadevaṃ tu kartavyaṃ hutotsṛṣṭaṃ tu laukike .. 1 ..
yatra kvacana vā rāma dīpyamāne'tha codake ..
parisamūhya paryukṣya paristīrya paristaret .. 2 ..
sarvānnamagnāvuddhṛtya juhuyātprayatastataḥ ..
vāsudevāya devāya prabhave nāpyayena ca .. 3 ..
agnaye caiva somāya mitrāya varuṇāya ca ..
indrāya ca mahābhāga indrāgnibhyāṃ tathaiva ca .. 4 ..
viśvebhyaścaiva devebhyaḥ prajānāṃ pataye tathā ..
anumatyai tathā rāma dhanvaṃtariṇa eva ca .. 5 ..
vāstoṣpatyai tathā devyai tataḥ sviṣṭikṛte'gnaye ..
caturthyantena natvā ca hutvaitebhyo baliṃ haret .. 6 ..
2.19.d:
निवेश्य चित्तं पुरुषोत्तमस्य भक्तिं समास्थाय तथा विशुद्धाम् ॥
करोति श्रद्धां सततं यथोक्तां स याति लोकं मधुसूदनस्य ॥21॥
2.92
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
ततोऽग्निशरणं गत्वा स्मार्तेऽग्नौ विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
वैश्वदेवं तु कर्तव्यं हुतोत्सृष्टं तु लौकिके ॥ 1 ॥
यत्र क्वचन वा राम दीप्यमानेऽथ चोदके ॥
परिसमूह्य पर्युक्ष्य परिस्तीर्य परिस्तरेत् ॥ 2 ॥
सर्वान्नमग्नावुद्धृत्य जुहुयात्प्रयतस्ततः ॥
वासुदेवाय देवाय प्रभवे नाप्ययेन च ॥ 3 ॥
अग्नये चैव सोमाय मित्राय वरुणाय च ॥
इन्द्राय च महाभाग इन्द्राग्निभ्यां तथैव च ॥ 4 ॥
विश्वेभ्यश्चैव देवेभ्यः प्रजानां पतये तथा ॥
अनुमत्यै तथा राम धन्वंतरिण एव च ॥ 5 ॥
वास्तोष्पत्यै तथा देव्यै ततः स्विष्टिकृतेऽग्नये ॥
चतुर्थ्यन्तेन नत्वा च हुत्वैतेभ्यो बलिं हरेत् ॥ 6 ॥
2.19.m:
Fixing the mind upon Puruṣottama and resorting to completely pure devotion, / whoever constantly performs faith as prescribed goes to the world of Madhusūdana.
Puṣkara said: / Then, having gone to the fire-sanctuary, in the Smārta fire according to rule, / the Vaiśvadeva rite should be performed, but in ordinary [fire] an offering of left-overs [is made].
Or wherever [a fire] is blazing, O Rāma, or in water, / sweeping around, sprinkling with water, and strewing [grass] all around, he should strew.
Taking out all the food, he should then carefully sacrifice into the fire: / to the god Vāsudeva, the sovereign, and with [the word] "Svāhā",
and to Agni, to Soma, to Mitra, and to Varuṇa, / and to Indra, O fortunate one, and likewise to Indrāgni,
and to the Viśvedevas, and likewise to the Lord of Creatures, / and to Anumati, O Rāma, and to Dhanvantari,
and to the goddess Vāstoṣpatī, and then to Agni Sviṣṭikṛt. / Having bowed with [names ending in] the dative case and sacrificed, he should offer the bali offering to these:

2.19.s:
takṣopatakṣāvabhitaḥ pūrveṇāgnimataḥ param ..
ambānāmāsi dharmajña durgā nāmāni cāpyatha .. 7 ..
nivantī ca panīkā ca prabhavantī tathaiva ca ..
medhavantī ca nāmāsi sarveṣāmeva bhārgava..8.
āgneyādyākrameṇātha tataḥ sūktiṣu nikṣipet ..
nirdityai vasubhāgyai ca sumaṅgalyai ca bhārgava .. 9..
bhadraṃkaryai tato dattvā sthūṇāyai ca tathā śriyai ..
hiraṇyakeśyai ca tathā vanaspataya eva ca ..2.92.10..
dharmādharmābhyāṃ ca dvāre gṛhamadhye dhruvāya ca ..
mṛtyave ca bahirdadyādvaruṇāyodakāśaye..11..
bhūtebhyaśca bahirdadyāccharaṇe dhanadāya ca ..
indrāyendrapuruṣebhyo dadyātpūrveṇa mānavaḥ .. 12 ..
yamāya tatpuruṣebhyo dadyāddakṣiṇatastataḥ ..
varuṇāya tatpuruṣebhyo dadyātpaścimatastataḥ .. 13 ..
2.19.d:
तक्षोपतक्षावभितः पूर्वेणाग्निमतः परम् ॥
अम्बानामासि धर्मज्ञ दुर्गा नामानि चाप्यथ ॥ 7 ॥
निवन्ती च पनीका च प्रभवन्ती तथैव च ॥
मेधवन्ती च नामासि सर्वेषामेव भार्गव॥8.
आग्नेयाद्याक्रमेणाथ ततः सूक्तिषु निक्षिपेत् ॥
निर्दित्यै वसुभाग्यै च सुमङ्गल्यै च भार्गव ॥ 9॥
भद्रंकर्यै ततो दत्त्वा स्थूणायै च तथा श्रियै ॥
हिरण्यकेश्यै च तथा वनस्पतय एव च ॥2.92.10॥
धर्माधर्माभ्यां च द्वारे गृहमध्ये ध्रुवाय च ॥
मृत्यवे च बहिर्दद्याद्वरुणायोदकाशये॥11॥
भूतेभ्यश्च बहिर्दद्याच्छरणे धनदाय च ॥
इन्द्रायेन्द्रपुरुषेभ्यो दद्यात्पूर्वेण मानवः ॥ 12 ॥
यमाय तत्पुरुषेभ्यो दद्याद्दक्षिणतस्ततः ॥
वरुणाय तत्पुरुषेभ्यो दद्यात्पश्चिमतस्ततः ॥ 13 ॥
2.19.m:
to Takṣa and Upatakṣa on both sides; then to the east of the fire: / "Thou art named Ambā," O knower of dharma, and then the names of Durgā,
and Nivantī, Panīkā, and likewise Prabhavantī, / and "Thou art named Medhavantī," of all of them, O Bhārgava.
Then in the order beginning with the south-east, he should place [offerings] in the quarters: / to Nirṛti, to Vasubhāgyā, and to Sumaṅgalī, O Bhārgava,
then having given to Bhadraṃkarī, to the post, and likewise to Śrī, / and likewise to Hiraṇyakeśī, and to Vanaspati,
and to Dharma and Adharma at the door, and to Dhruva in the middle of the house, / and to Mṛtyu outside, and to Varuṇa in the reservoir of water;
and he should give to the spirits outside, and to the Giver of Wealth at the refuge. / A man should give to Indra and Indra's attendants in the east,
then to Yama and his attendants in the south; / then to Varuṇa and his attendants in the west;

2.19.s:
somāya somapuruṣebhya udagdadyādanantaram ..
brahmaṇe brahmapuruṣebhyo madhye dadyāttathaiva ca .. 14 ..
ākāśe ca tathaivordhvaṃ sthaṇḍile ca tathā kṣitau ..
divācarebhyaśca divā rātrau rātricarāya ca .. 15 ..
baliṃ bahistathā dadyātsāyaṃ prātastu pratyaham ..
piṇḍanirvāpaṇaṃ kāryaṃ sāyaṃ prātarna kārayet .. 16 ..
pitre tu prathamaṃ piṇḍaṃ tatpitre tadanantaram ..
tato dadyācca tatpitre mātre ca tadanantaram .. 17 ..
pitṛmātre tato dadyācchvaśrvai tadanantaram ..
dakṣiṇāgreṣu darbheṣu salileṣu viśeṣataḥ .. 18 ..
yatkiñcitpaśyate gehe bhakṣyaṃ vā bhojyameva vā ..
nivedayecca tatsarvaṃ śubhaṃ pānaṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 19 ..
puṣpairdhūpena dīpena pūjayetsatataṃ pitṝn ..
nāmagotre sadā vācye piṇḍanirvāpaṇe tathā .. 2.92.20 ..
2.19.d:
सोमाय सोमपुरुषेभ्य उदग्दद्यादनन्तरम् ॥
ब्रह्मणे ब्रह्मपुरुषेभ्यो मध्ये दद्यात्तथैव च ॥ 14 ॥
आकाशे च तथैवोर्ध्वं स्थण्डिले च तथा क्षितौ ॥
दिवाचरेभ्यश्च दिवा रात्रौ रात्रिचराय च ॥ 15 ॥
बलिं बहिस्तथा दद्यात्सायं प्रातस्तु प्रत्यहम् ॥
पिण्डनिर्वापणं कार्यं सायं प्रातर्न कारयेत् ॥ 16 ॥
पित्रे तु प्रथमं पिण्डं तत्पित्रे तदनन्तरम् ॥
ततो दद्याच्च तत्पित्रे मात्रे च तदनन्तरम् ॥ 17 ॥
पितृमात्रे ततो दद्याच्छ्वश्र्वै तदनन्तरम् ॥
दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु सलिलेषु विशेषतः ॥ 18 ॥
यत्किञ्चित्पश्यते गेहे भक्ष्यं वा भोज्यमेव वा ॥
निवेदयेच्च तत्सर्वं शुभं पानं विशेषतः ॥ 19 ॥
पुष्पैर्धूपेन दीपेन पूजयेत्सततं पितॄन् ॥
नामगोत्रे सदा वाच्ये पिण्डनिर्वापणे तथा ॥ 2.92.20 ॥
2.19.m:
next he should give to Soma and Soma's attendants in the north; / and likewise to Brahmā and Brahmā's attendants in the middle,
and likewise up in the sky, and likewise upon the altar-ground on the earth, / and to day-wanderers by day, and by night to the night-wanderer.
He should thus give the bali offering outside, morning and evening every day. / The casting of piṇḍas is to be performed; he should not perform it both morning and evening.
The first piṇḍa to the father, immediately after that to his father, / then he should give to his father, and immediately after that to the mother;
then he should give to the paternal grandmother, [and] immediately after that to the mother-in-law, / on darbha grass with their tips pointing south, especially in water.
Whatever is seen in the house, whether snack or meal, / one should present all of that, especially wholesome drink.
One should constantly worship the ancestors with flowers, incense, and lamps. / Name and gotra are always to be spoken at the casting of piṇḍas.

2.19.s:
piṇḍaṃ dadyācca kākānāṃ tatra mantramimaṃ paṭhet ..
aindrā varuṇavāyavyā yāmyā vai nairṛtāstathā .. 21 ..
2.19.d:
पिण्डं दद्याच्च काकानां तत्र मन्त्रमिमं पठेत् ॥
ऐन्द्रा वरुणवायव्या याम्या वै नैरृतास्तथा ॥ 21 ॥
2.19.m: And one should give a piṇḍa to the crows; there he should recite this mantra: / "Belonging to Indra, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Yama, and Nirṛti,

2.19.s:
te kākāḥ pratigṛhṇantu imaṃ piṇḍaṃ mayoddhṛtam ..
tataḥ piṇḍaṃ śunāṃ dadyānmantraṃ tatra nibodha me ..22 ..
2.19.d:
ते काकाः प्रतिगृह्णन्तु इमं पिण्डं मयोद्धृतम् ॥
ततः पिण्डं शुनां दद्यान्मन्त्रं तत्र निबोध मे ॥22 ॥
2.19.m: may those crows accept this piṇḍa offered by me." / Then he should give a piṇḍa to the dogs; learn from me the mantra for that:

2.19.s:
vaivasvatakule jātau dvau śyāmaśabalau śunau ..
tābhyāṃ piṇḍaṃ pradāsyāmi pathi rakṣantu māṃ sadā .. 23 ..
2.19.d:
वैवस्वतकुले जातौ द्वौ श्यामशबलौ शुनौ ॥
ताभ्यां पिण्डं प्रदास्यामि पथि रक्षन्तु मां सदा ॥ 23 ॥
2.19.m: "Born in the family of Vaivasvata, the two dogs, dark and brindled— / to them I will give a piṇḍa; may they protect me always on the road."

2.19.s:
tato grāsaṃ gavāṃ dadyādatra mantraṃ nibodha me ..
saurabheyyaḥ sarvahitāḥ pavitrāḥ pāpanāśinīḥ ..24..
2.19.d:
ततो ग्रासं गवां दद्यादत्र मन्त्रं निबोध मे ॥
सौरभेय्यः सर्वहिताः पवित्राः पापनाशिनीः ॥24॥
2.19.m: Then he should give a morsel to the cows; learn from me the mantra for this: / "Daughters of Surabhi, beneficial to all, pure, destroyers of sins,

2.19.s:
pratigṛhṇantu me grāsaṃ gāvastrailokyamātaraḥ ..
tataḥ svastayayanaṃ kāryaṃ bhikṣā deyā ca bhikṣave..25..
2.19.d:
प्रतिगृह्णन्तु मे ग्रासं गावस्त्रैलोक्यमातरः ॥
ततः स्वस्तययनं कार्यं भिक्षा देया च भिक्षवे॥25॥
2.19.m: may the cows, mothers of the three worlds, accept my morsel." / Then a pronouncement of welfare should be made, and alms should be given to a mendicant.

2.19.s:
dattvā tu saṃskṛtāṃ bhikṣāṃ godānaphalamāpnuyāt ..
bālaḥ suvāsinī vṛddhā garbhiṇyāturakanyakāḥ..26..
2.19.d:
दत्त्वा तु संस्कृतां भिक्षां गोदानफलमाप्नुयात् ॥
बालः सुवासिनी वृद्धा गर्भिण्यातुरकन्यकाः॥26॥
2.19.m: Having given prepared alms, he obtains the fruit of giving a cow. / A child, a married woman residing in her father's house, the aged, pregnant women, the sick, young girls,

2.19.s:
bhṛtyām̐śca bhojayedrāma pūjayitvā tathātithīn ..
naikagrāmīṇamatithiṃ vidyānnābrāhmaṇaṃ tathā ..27..
2.19.d:
भृत्याम्̐श्च भोजयेद्राम पूजयित्वा तथातिथीन् ॥
नैकग्रामीणमतिथिं विद्यान्नाब्राह्मणं तथा ॥27॥
2.19.m: and the servants he should feed, O Rāma, after having honoured guests. / He should not consider one from the same village as a guest, nor a non-brahmin.

2.19.s:
atithiṃ bhojayetpūrvaṃ tato bhṛtyāṃśca pūjayet ..
rājanyamathavā vaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ vā dvijasattama ..28..
2.19.d:
अतिथिं भोजयेत्पूर्वं ततो भृत्यांश्च पूजयेत् ॥
राजन्यमथवा वैश्यं शूद्रं वा द्विजसत्तम ॥28॥
2.19.m: He should feed the guest first, then he should honour his servants, / or a kṣatriya, a vaiśya, or a śūdra, O best of the twice-born.

2.19.s:
vaiśvadeve ca saṃprāptaṃ bhṛtyaiḥ saha ca bhojayet..
vayobhyaśca tathā dadyāccaṇḍālebhyastathā bhuvi..29..
2.19.d:
वैश्वदेवे च संप्राप्तं भृत्यैः सह च भोजयेत्॥
वयोभ्यश्च तथा दद्याच्चण्डालेभ्यस्तथा भुवि॥29॥
2.19.m: When one arrives at the time of the Vaiśvadeva, he should feed him along with the servants. / And he should give likewise to the birds and to caṇḍālas on the ground.

2.19.s:
sādhāraṇaṃ tatsarveṣāṃ śeṣakaṃ gṛhiṇāṃ gṛhe ..
vaiśvadeve ca saṃprāpte na kathaṃcidavamānayet..2.92.30..
2.19.d:
साधारणं तत्सर्वेषां शेषकं गृहिणां गृहे ॥
वैश्वदेवे च संप्राप्ते न कथंचिदवमानयेत्॥2.92.30॥
2.19.m: That remnant in the house of householders is common to all. / And when someone arrives at the time of the Vaiśvadeva, he should by no means disrespect him.

2.19.s:
ādāya sukṛtaṃ yāti bhagnāśaścātithirgataḥ ..
adhvanā yastu bhagnāya brāhmaṇāya tathā divi..31..
2.19.d:
आदाय सुकृतं याति भग्नाशश्चातिथिर्गतः ॥
अध्वना यस्तु भग्नाय ब्राह्मणाय तथा दिवि॥31॥
2.19.m: Taking one's good deeds, the guest whose hopes are broken goes away. / But whoever gives food with honour to a brahmin broken by the road,

2.19.s:
satkṛtya bhojanaṃ dadyāttena svarge mahīyate ..
devā brāhmaṇarūpeṇa caranti pṛthivīmimām.. 32..
2.19.d:
सत्कृत्य भोजनं दद्यात्तेन स्वर्गे महीयते ॥
देवा ब्राह्मणरूपेण चरन्ति पृथिवीमिमाम्॥ 32॥
2.19.m: by that he is exalted in heaven. / Gods wander this earth in the form of brahmins;

2.19.s:
tasmātsaṃprāptamatithiṃ prayatnena tu pūjayet ..
atithiṃ pūjayeccāgre daśagodaphalaṃ labhet..33..
2.19.d:
तस्मात्संप्राप्तमतिथिं प्रयत्नेन तु पूजयेत् ॥
अतिथिं पूजयेच्चाग्रे दशगोदफलं लभेत्॥33॥
2.19.m: therefore one should carefully honour a guest who has arrived. / One should honour a guest first; he obtains the fruit of ten cows.

2.19.s:
pādaśaucaṃ tato dattvā prāptāyāṃtithaye gṛhe ..
godānaphalamāpnoti dattvā caiva tathāsanam ..34..
2.19.d:
पादशौचं ततो दत्त्वा प्राप्तायांतिथये गृहे ॥
गोदानफलमाप्नोति दत्त्वा चैव तथासनम् ॥34॥
2.19.m: Having given washing for the feet to a guest who has arrived in the house, / and having given a seat, he obtains the fruit of the gift of a cow.

2.19.s:
pratiśrayapradānena nākapṛṣṭhe mahīyate ..
tālavṛntānilaṃ kṛtvā tathā prāptāya mānavaḥ ..35..
2.19.d:
प्रतिश्रयप्रदानेन नाकपृष्ठे महीयते ॥
तालवृन्तानिलं कृत्वा तथा प्राप्ताय मानवः ॥35॥
2.19.m: By granting shelter, he is glorified in the heights of heaven. / By creating a breeze with a palm-leaf fan for one who has arrived,

2.19.s:
godānaphalamāpnoti vāyulokaṃ sa gacchati ..
tālavyajanahastastu kṛtvā tadabhicāraṇam..36..
2.19.d:
गोदानफलमाप्नोति वायुलोकं स गच्छति ॥
तालव्यजनहस्तस्तु कृत्वा तदभिचारणम्॥36॥
2.19.m: a man attains the fruit of giving a cow and goes to the realm of Vāyu. / But holding a palm-leaf fan in hand and attending to him,

2.19.s:
atithirbhojane prāpte godānaphalamāpnuyāt ..
śītāhatātithiṃ prāpya kāṣṭhānprajvālayennaraḥ .. 37 ..
2.19.d:
अतिथिर्भोजने प्राप्ते गोदानफलमाप्नुयात् ॥
शीताहतातिथिं प्राप्य काष्ठान्प्रज्वालयेन्नरः ॥ 37 ॥
2.19.m: when the guest receives food, he should obtain the fruit of giving a cow. / Finding a guest struck by cold, a man should kindle logs of wood;

2.19.s:
pratāpayenmahābhāga daśadhenuphalaṃ labhet ..
kāyāgnidīptimāpnoti prākāśyaṃ paramaṃ tathā .. 38 ..
2.19.d:
प्रतापयेन्महाभाग दशधेनुफलं लभेत् ॥
कायाग्निदीप्तिमाप्नोति प्राकाश्यं परमं तथा ॥ 38 ॥
2.19.m: he should warm him, O fortunate one, and will obtain the fruit of ten cows. / He attains brilliance of the bodily fire and also supreme radiance.

2.19.s:
tṛṣṇārtāyodakaṃ dattvā pāne godānamāpnuyāt ..
śrāntasaṃvāhanaṃ kṛtvā dhenudānaphalaṃ labhet .. 39 ..
2.19.d:
तृष्णार्तायोदकं दत्त्वा पाने गोदानमाप्नुयात् ॥
श्रान्तसंवाहनं कृत्वा धेनुदानफलं लभेत् ॥ 39 ॥
2.19.m: Giving water to drink to one afflicted with thirst, he obtains [the fruit of giving] a cow. / Massaging an exhausted [guest], he obtains the fruit of giving a cow.

2.19.s:
rogiṇaḥ paricaryāṃ ca kṛtvā daśaguṇaṃ labhet ..
pādābhyaṃgaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā prāptāyātithaye gṛhe ..2.92.40..
2.19.d:
रोगिणः परिचर्यां च कृत्वा दशगुणं लभेत् ॥
पादाभ्यंगं नरः कृत्वा प्राप्तायातिथये गृहे ॥2.92.40॥
2.19.m: And caring for a sick person, he obtains tenfold. / A man who performs an anointing of the feet for a guest who has arrived at his house,

2.19.s:
godānaphalamāpnoti nāgalokaṃ ca gacchati..
pratiśrayaṃ tathā dīnaṃ dattvā cātithaye naraḥ..41..
2.19.d:
गोदानफलमाप्नोति नागलोकं च गच्छति॥
प्रतिश्रयं तथा दीनं दत्त्वा चातिथये नरः॥41॥
2.19.m: obtains the fruit of giving a cow and goes to the world of the Nāgas. / And a man who gives humble shelter to a guest,

2.19.s:
dhenudānaphalaṃ prāpya sūryaloke mahīyate ..
cakṣuṣmāṃśca prakāśāṃśca virodhaścaiva jāyate ..42..
2.19.d:
धेनुदानफलं प्राप्य सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥
चक्षुष्मांश्च प्रकाशांश्च विरोधश्चैव जायते ॥42॥
2.19.m: having obtained the fruit of giving a cow, is glorified in the realm of the Sun. / He becomes endowed with sight and light, and is born free of hostility.

2.19.s:
śayanīyapradānena vasudānaphalaṃ labhet ..
dantakāṣṭhapradānena saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnuyāt..43..
2.19.d:
शयनीयप्रदानेन वसुदानफलं लभेत् ॥
दन्तकाष्ठप्रदानेन सौभाग्यं महदाप्नुयात्॥43॥
2.19.m: By giving a bed, he obtains the fruit of giving wealth. / By giving a tooth-stick, he attains great good fortune.

2.19.s:
śaucodakapradānena godānaphalamāpnuyāt ..
mṛtpradānena dharmajña virodho nābhijā yate..44..
2.19.d:
शौचोदकप्रदानेन गोदानफलमाप्नुयात् ॥
मृत्प्रदानेन धर्मज्ञ विरोधो नाभिजा यते॥44॥
2.19.m: By giving water for purification, he attains the fruit of giving a cow. / By giving earth [for cleaning], O knower of dharma, no discord arises.

2.19.s:
dattvānulepanaṃ mālāṃ parāṃ lakṣmīmupāsate ..
tathauṣadhipradānena virogastvabhijāyate.. 45 ..
2.19.d:
दत्त्वानुलेपनं मालां परां लक्ष्मीमुपासते ॥
तथौषधिप्रदानेन विरोगस्त्वभिजायते॥ 45 ॥
2.19.m: Having given anointing ointment and a garland, he waits upon supreme fortune. / Likewise, by giving medicine, he is born free from disease.

2.19.s:
snānābhyaṅgapradānena rūpavānabhijāyate ..
tathā snānīyadānena gandharvaiḥ saha modate .. 46 ..
2.19.d:
स्नानाभ्यङ्गप्रदानेन रूपवानभिजायते ॥
तथा स्नानीयदानेन गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते ॥ 46 ॥
2.19.m: By giving an anointing bath, he is born handsome. / Likewise, by giving bath preparations, he rejoices with the Gandharvas.

2.19.s:
snānodakapradānena vāruṇaṃ lokamāpnuyāt ..
upānahaḥ pradānena vimānamadhirohati .. 47 ..
2.19.d:
स्नानोदकप्रदानेन वारुणं लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥
उपानहः प्रदानेन विमानमधिरोहति ॥ 47 ॥
2.19.m: By giving bath-water, he attains the realm of Varuṇa. / By giving sandals, he mounts a flying chariot.

2.19.s:
tathā chatrapradānena gāṇapatyamavāpnuyāt ..
vastrapradānādbhavati rūpavānsubhagastathā .. 48 ..
2.19.d:
तथा छत्रप्रदानेन गाणपत्यमवाप्नुयात् ॥
वस्त्रप्रदानाद्भवति रूपवान्सुभगस्तथा ॥ 48 ॥
2.19.m: Likewise, by giving an umbrella, he attains lordship over the attendants. / From giving clothing, he becomes handsome and blessed.

2.19.s:
aśvamedhamavāpnoti tathā bhūmiprado naraḥ ..
yānadaḥ svargamāpnoti pauṇḍarīkapadaṃ tathā ..49..
2.19.d:
अश्वमेधमवाप्नोति तथा भूमिप्रदो नरः ॥
यानदः स्वर्गमाप्नोति पौण्डरीकपदं तथा ॥49॥
2.19.m: A man who gives land attains [the fruit of] a horse sacrifice. / One who gives a vehicle attains heaven and the realm of the Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice.

2.19.s:
vāridhānīstathā dattvā pūrṇāḥ śītena vāriṇā ..
sarvā sabhakṣāḥ prāpnoti golokaṃ mānuṣottama .. 2.92.50 ..
2.19.d:
वारिधानीस्तथा दत्त्वा पूर्णाः शीतेन वारिणा ॥
सर्वा सभक्षाः प्राप्नोति गोलोकं मानुषोत्तम ॥ 2.92.50 ॥
2.19.m: Having given water jars filled with cool water, / and full of all kinds of food, O best of men, he attains Goloka,

2.19.s:
trapuṣairvārukāyuktaiḥ śarkarāghṛtasaṃyutaiḥ ..
saktubhirlavaṇopetaighṛrtairharitasaṃyutaiḥ .. 51..
2.19.d:
त्रपुषैर्वारुकायुक्तैः शर्कराघृतसंयुतैः ॥
सक्तुभिर्लवणोपेतैघृर्तैर्हरितसंयुतैः ॥ 51॥
2.19.m: with cucumbers and wild cucumbers, accompanied by sugar and ghee, / with barley meal accompanied by salt, [and] with ghee accompanied by fresh vegetables.

2.19.s:
tarpayitvātithiṃ samyagvāridhānyaiśca gorasaiḥ ..
golokaṃ ciramāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 52 ..
2.19.d:
तर्पयित्वातिथिं सम्यग्वारिधान्यैश्च गोरसैः ॥
गोलोकं चिरमाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 52 ॥
2.19.m: Having properly satisfied a guest with water jars and milk products, / he attains Goloka for a long time; no doubt should be entertained on this point.

2.19.s:
tṛptimāpnoti ca tathā yatrayatrābhijāyate ..
kimicchakena saṃyojya cāśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 53 ..
2.19.d:
तृप्तिमाप्नोति च तथा यत्रयत्राभिजायते ॥
किमिच्छकेन संयोज्य चाश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ॥ 53 ॥
2.19.m: And he attains satisfaction wherever he is born. / Granting whatever one desires, he obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

2.19.s:
tāṃbūlasya pradānena gandharvaiḥ saha modate ..
uptimāsāvṛtaṃ kṛtvā svargaloke mahīyate .. 54 ..
2.19.d:
तांबूलस्य प्रदानेन गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते ॥
उप्तिमासावृतं कृत्वा स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥ 54 ॥
2.19.m: By giving betel, he rejoices with the Gandharvas. / Having provided covering and shelter, he is honored in the heavenly realm.

2.19.s:
itihāsānathāśrāvya godānaphalamāpnuyāta ..

इतिहासानथाश्राव्य गोदानफलमाप्नुयात ॥
गोप्रदानेन वित्तेन तोषयित्वा तथातिथिम् ॥ 55 ॥
2.19.m: By reciting the ancient histories, he obtains the fruit of giving a cow. / Having satisfied a guest with the gift of a cow and wealth,

anuvrajyātithiṃ rāma godānaphalamāpnuyāt .. 56 ..
2.19.d:
महत्फलमवाप्नोति गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते ॥
अनुव्रज्यातिथिं राम गोदानफलमाप्नुयात् ॥ 56 ॥
2.19.m: he obtains a great reward and rejoices with the Gandharvas. / Accompanying a departing guest, O Rāma, he obtains the fruit of giving a cow.

gṛhastho'tithidaivatyastasmāttaṃ pūjayetsadā ..57..
2.19.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन पूजयेदतिथिं सदा ॥
राजन्या विप्रदैवत्या नार्यश्च पतिदेवताः ॥
गृहस्थोऽतिथिदैवत्यस्तस्मात्तं पूजयेत्सदा ॥57॥
2.19.m: Therefore, with every effort one should always honor a guest. / Nobles have brahmins as their deities, and women have their husbands as their deities; / a householder has the guest as his deity, therefore he should always honor him.

सततमिह नरो यः पूजनं चातिथीनां तृणजलमृदुवाक्यैः सारशक्त्या विदध्यात् ॥
सुरसदसि स पूज्यो देवतानां तथा स्याद्भवति च नरलोके जायमानः समृद्धः ॥ ॥ 58 ॥
2.93
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥
चन्द्रस्य यदि वा भानोर्यस्मिन्नहनि भार्गव ॥
ग्रहणं तु भवेत्तत्र न पूर्वं भोजनक्रिया ॥ 1 ॥
नाचरेत्सग्रहे तस्मिंस्तथैवास्तमुपागते ॥
यावत्स्यादुदयं तस्य नाश्नीयात्तावदेव तु ॥2॥
गोब्राह्मणश्चोपरागे न चाश्नीयात्प्रयत्नतः ॥
न राज्ञो विप्लवेऽश्नीयात्सुरार्चाविप्लवे तथा ॥ ॥ 3 ॥
न हुत्वा न च दत्त्वा च नाशौचे न च गर्हितम् ॥
नापथ्यं न च बालानां तथा भार्गव पश्यताम् ॥ 4 ॥
प्रार्थितं बालकानां च दातव्यं स्यात्प्रयत्नतः ॥
बालानां प्रार्थितं दत्त्वा नाकलोके महीयते ॥ 5 ॥
2.19.m:
A man here who constantly performs the worship of guests with grass, water, and gentle words according to his utmost capacity, / would be worthy of worship among the deities in the assembly of the gods, and when reborn in the world of men, he is prosperous.
Puṣkara said: / On whichever day an eclipse of the moon or sun takes place, O Bhārgava, / on that day one should not engage in eating beforehand.
One should not eat when it sets while eclipsed. / Only as long as it takes to rise again should one not eat.
During an eclipse, neither a cow nor a brahmin should eat, with diligence. / One should not eat during an upheaval of the king, nor during an affliction of the images of the gods,
nor without having offered into the fire, nor without having given [gifts], nor during ritual impurity, nor food that is censured, / nor unwholesome food, nor while children are watching, O Bhārgava.
What is requested by children should be given with care. / Having given what is asked by children, one is honored in the heavenly world.

2.19.d:
बालका लालनीयाश्च धर्मकामैः सदा नरैः ॥
तेषां भोज्यप्रदानेन गोदानफलमाप्नुयात् ॥ 6 ॥
तेषां क्रीडनकं दत्त्वा मोदते नन्दने चिरम् ॥
आह्लादं यान्ति सततं यस्मिन्दृष्ट्वा तु बालकाः ॥ 7 ॥
सौभाग्यं महदाप्नोति यत्रयत्राभिजायते ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन बालानग्रे तु भोजयेत् ॥8॥
अभुक्तवत्सु बालेषु न चाश्नीयात्कथञ्चन ॥
यो न दद्यान्न चाश्नी यात्कदाचिदपि तन्मयम् ॥ 9 ॥
य एको मिष्टमश्नाति न ततोऽन्योऽस्ति पातकी ॥
नैकवासास्तथाश्नीयाद्भिन्नभाण्डे न मानवः ॥ 2.93.10 ॥
भिन्नासनोपविष्टश्च शयनीयगतस्तथा ॥
अनार्द्रपाणिपादान्तस्तथा चैवार्द्रमस्तकः ॥ 11 ॥
नोत्सङ्गे भक्षयेद्भक्ष्यान्न पाणौ लवणं तथा ॥
सकृद्दानं पृथक्पानं मांसेन पयसा निशि ॥ 12 ॥
दन्तच्छेदनमुष्णं च सप्तकन्तु सुवर्जयेत् ॥
दधि रात्रौ न चाश्नीयाज्जलन्नाञ्जलिना पिबेत् ॥ ॥ 13 ॥
2.19.m:
Children should always be cherished by men who desire dharma. / By giving food to them, one obtains the fruit of giving a cow.
Having given a toy to them, one rejoices in the Nandana garden for a long time. / The man upon seeing whom children are always delighted
attains great good fortune wherever he is born. / Therefore, with every effort one should feed children first.
While the children have not eaten, one should by no means eat. / He who would not give [to children] should never eat what is desired by them.
He who eats sweet food alone—there is no greater sinner than he. / Likewise, a man should not eat wearing only a single garment, nor from a broken vessel,
nor seated on a broken seat, nor lying in bed, / nor without wet hands and feet, nor with a wet head.
One should not eat foods from one's lap, nor salt placed directly in the hand. / Giving once, drinking separately, meat with milk at night,
cutting with the teeth, and hot food—one should carefully avoid these seven. / One should not eat curds at night, nor drink water with folded hands.

2.19.d:
सर्वं तैलसमृद्धं च नाद्यादस्तमिते रवौ ॥
वर्जनीया दिवा धानाः कोविदारः सदैव तु ॥ 14 ॥
दिवा धानाः स्वरं हन्ति रात्रौ च दधि सक्तुषु ॥
अलक्ष्मीः कोविदारेषु नित्यमेव कृतालया ॥ 15 ॥
निःशेषकृत्तथा राम न स्यादन्यत्र माक्षिकात् ॥
क्षीरस्य राम सक्तूनां पाथसस्योदकस्य च ॥ 16 ॥
शेषं तु कार्यमन्यस्य न तु निःशेषकृद्भवेत् ॥
शूद्राय दद्यान्नोच्छिष्टं नोच्छिष्टश्च घृतं स्पृशेत् ॥ 17 ॥
मूर्धानं न स्पृशेद्राम न स्पृशेच्च हुताशनम् ॥
नानुकुत्सा च कर्तव्या सुमनास्तन्मनास्तथा ॥ 18 ॥
भुञ्जीत प्रयतो भूत्वा दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥
वामहस्तेन पानीयं पीतोच्छिष्टं तथैव च ॥ 19 ॥
न पिबेन्न तथाश्नीयात्कृत्वा पर्यस्तिकं नरः ॥
पादप्रसारणं कृत्वा न च वेष्टितमस्तकः ॥ 2.93.20 ॥
2.19.m:
One should not eat anything rich in oil after the sun has set. / Roasted grain during the day and kovidāra are always to be avoided.
Roasted grain by day harms the voice, as do curds with barley meal at night. / Misfortune has constantly made its dwelling in kovidāra trees.
Likewise, O Rāma, one should not leave a plate completely empty, except in the case of honey, / milk, O Rāma, barley meal, and drinking water.
One should leave a remainder of other things, and not leave [the vessel] completely empty. / One should not give leftovers to a śūdra, nor should one touch ghee while impure with food.
One should not touch the crown of the head, O Rāma, nor touch the sacrificial fire [while impure]. / Nor should one criticize the food; one should be cheerful and focused on it,
and eat with restraint, not gazing around at the directions. / Water taken with the left hand, or having been drunk from, is considered leftover food.
A man should not drink, nor should he eat, sitting with his knees bound [with a cloth], / with his legs stretched out, or with his head covered.

2.19.d:
आचम्य तु ततः कार्यं दन्तकाष्ठस्य भक्षणम् ॥
भूयोऽप्याचम्य कर्तव्यं ततस्ताम्बूलधारणम् ॥21 ॥
श्रवणं चेतिहासस्य ततः कुर्यात्समाहितः ॥
शास्त्रान्वेषा च कर्तव्या ततः सम्यग्भृगूत्तम ॥ 22 ॥
शास्त्रान्ववेक्षणं कृत्वा कृत्वा चंक्रमणं ततः ॥
उपास्य पश्चिमां सन्ध्यां तिष्ठेत्प्रयतमानसः ॥ 23 ॥।
पूर्वां सन्ध्यां जपंस्तिष्ठेदुपविष्टश्च पश्चिमाम् ॥
अर्क्कस्योदयनात्तावद्यावद्भास्करदर्शनम् ॥ 24 ॥
पूर्वां सन्ध्यां जपेत्स्नातः पश्चिमां सति भास्करे ॥
उपविष्टो जपेत्तावद्यावत्तारकदर्शनम् ॥ 25 ॥
सम्पूजनं देववरस्य कृत्वा ततश्च कुर्यात्खलु वैश्वदेवम् ॥
भुक्त्वा ततोऽन्नं लघु यच्च हृद्यं ततः स्वपेद्भार्गववंशमुख्य ॥26॥
2.94
पुष्कर उवाच॥
शून्यालये श्मशाने वानेकवृक्षे चतुष्पथे ॥
महादेवगृहे वापि मातृवेश्मनि वा स्वपेत्॥1॥
2.19.m:
Having sipped water, he should then chew the tooth-stick; / having sipped water once again, he should then take betel.
Concentrated, he should then listen to traditional history; / he should also thoroughly study the treatises, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
Having studied the treatises and having taken a stroll, / he should perform the evening twilight worship and remain restrained in mind.
Reciting [the prayer], he should stand for the morning twilight and sit for the evening, / from the rising of the sun until the sun is visible.
Bathed, he should recite [the prayer] for the morning twilight; and for the evening twilight while the sun is still present, / seated, he should recite until the appearance of the stars.
Having worshipped the supreme god, he should then indeed perform the vaiśvadeva offering; / having then eaten food that is light and agreeable, he should sleep, O chief of the lineage of Bhṛgu.
Puṣkara said: / In a deserted house or a cremation ground, under a single tree, at a crossroads, / in a temple of Mahādeva, or in a shrine of the Mothers, one should sleep.

2.19.d:
न यक्षनागायतने स्कन्दस्यायतने तथा॥
कूलच्छायासु च तथा शर्करालोष्टपांसुषु ॥2॥
प्रस्वपेच्च तथा दर्भे विना दीक्षां व्रतं न च ॥
धान्यगोदेवविप्राणां गुरूणां च तथोपरि ॥ 3 ॥।
न चापि भिन्नविषये नाशुचौ नाशुचिस्तथा ॥
नार्द्रपादश्च नग्नश्च नोत्तरापरमस्तकः ॥4॥
नाकाशे सर्वतः शून्ये न च चैत्यद्रुमे तथा॥
न गच्छेद्गुर्विणीं नारीं न गच्छेत्सितमूर्धजाम् ॥5॥
रजस्वलां रोगवतीं नायोनौ न बुभुक्षितः ॥
नाभ्यक्तो न तथाभ्यक्तां न च पर्वणि भार्गव ॥
शुक्रमोक्षमथाकाशे तिर्यग्योनौ च वर्जयेत् ॥6॥
एवं सदा यः कुरुते नृवीर सम्यग्यथोक्तं सुमनास्तरस्वी ॥
तस्याशु पापं विलयं प्रयाति श्रियं च मुख्यां लभते सुखं च ॥ 7 ॥
2.95
पुष्कर उवाच॥
वैवाहिकेऽग्नौ कुर्वीत कर्म स्मार्तं सदा गृही ॥
दायकालाहृते वापि पितुर्मरणकालिके ॥ 1 ॥
2.19.m:
[One should] not [sleep] in a shrine of a Yakṣa or a Nāga, nor in a shrine of Skanda, / nor in the shade of a riverbank, nor on gravel, clods, or dust.
Nor should one sleep on darbha-grass without an initiation or a vow, / nor upon grain, cows, gods, brahmins, and teachers;
nor in a divided country, nor in an impure place, nor while impure; / nor with wet feet, nor naked, nor with head to the north or west;
nor under the open sky on all sides, nor at a sacred tree. / He should not have intercourse with a pregnant woman, nor with a gray-haired woman,
nor with a menstruating woman, a sick woman, nor in an unnatural place, nor when hungry, / nor when anointed, nor with one who is anointed, nor on a sacred day, O descendant of Bhṛgu; / he should also avoid ejaculation into the air and into an animal.
He who always acts thus properly as prescribed, O hero among men, pure in mind and resolute, / his sin quickly dissolves, and he attains foremost prosperity and happiness.
Puṣkara said: / In the marriage fire a householder should always perform the rites prescribed by the smṛti, / or in [the fire] brought at the time of inheritance, at the time of the father's death,

द्विराग्रहायणेष्टिश्च पाके च यवधान्ययोः ॥13॥
विरूढा पशुबन्धश्च तथा सौत्रामणिर्द्विजः ॥

2.19.m:
One should know that the sacrifice to the gods is what is offered in fire, the sacrifice to beings is the rite of bali, / the sacrifice to the ancestors is through rice-balls, and the sacrifice to the sages, O descendant of Bhṛgu,
is known as devotion to Vedic study; likewise, worship of guests / is known as the human sacrifice: he should not omit the five sacrifices.
He should also sacrifice to Lord Viṣṇu with the seven oblation sacrifices: / the establishment of the fires, O fortunate one, and the rite of the fire oblation,
the New Moon and the Full Moon sacrifices, and likewise the Four-Month sacrifices, / and the sacrifice twice at the Āgrahāyaṇa, and at the ripening of barley and grain,
the new-sprouting [sacrifice], the animal sacrifice, and the Sautrāmaṇī, O twice-born. / With the seven forms of Soma sacrifice he should sacrifice to the eternal god:
the Agniṣṭoma, O fortunate one, the Atyagniṣṭoma, / the Ukthya, the Pāvanī, and the Atirātra,
and the Vājapeya, O knower of dharma, and likewise the Āptoryāma; / and through various other sacrifices, such as the Pauṇḍarīka,
