गोसवेनाश्वमेधेन राजसूयेन वा पुनः ॥
तथा पुरुषमेधेन सर्वमेधेन भार्गव ॥ 17 ॥
अन्यैश्च विविधैर्यज्ञैर्नामकल्पोचितैस्तथा ॥
यजनं देवदेवस्य वासुदेवस्य कारयेत् ॥ 18 ॥
यज्ञो विष्णुर्महातेजा यजमानः स एव हि ॥
त एव यज्ञपात्राणि यज्ञद्रव्याणि यानि च ॥ 19 ॥
तं यजेत्सततं राम सर्वदेवमयं हरिम् ॥
सत्येन वै यजेद्देवं प्रत्यब्दं मुनिपुङ्गव ॥ 2.95.20 ॥
पशुप्रत्ययनं कुर्याच्चातुर्मासिकमेव च ॥
इष्टिं वैश्वानरीं कुर्यात्तथा स्वल्पधनो नरः ॥ 21 ॥
अत्येवाल्पे धने सोमं पिबेद्भार्गवसत्तम ॥
आयुः पुत्रान्यशो मेधां धनमन्त्रगणं तथा ॥ .22 ॥
हन्त्यल्पदक्षिणो यज्ञस्तस्मान्नाल्पधनो यजेत् ॥
यस्य त्रैवार्षिकं भक्तं पर्याप्तं भृत्यतृप्तये ॥ 23 ॥
अधिकं वापि विद्येत स सोमं पातुमर्हति ॥
प्राजापत्यमदत्त्वा च अग्न्याधेयस्य दक्षिणा ॥ 24 ॥
2.19.m:
with the Gosava, the Aśvamedha, or again the Rājasūya, / and with the Puruṣamedha and Sarvamedha, O descendant of Bhṛgu,
and through other various sacrifices proper to particular rites, / he should cause worship of the god of gods, Vāsudeva, to be performed.
Viṣṇu of great splendour is the sacrifice, and he indeed is the sacrificer; / those sacrificial vessels and whatever sacrificial substances there are are him as well.
One should constantly sacrifice to him, O Rāma, Hari who comprises all the gods; / with truth indeed one should sacrifice to the god year after year, O bull among sages.
He should perform the animal renewal and the Four-Month sacrifice; / a man of little wealth should also perform the Vaiśvānara sacrifice.
Only with very little wealth [should he not] drink soma, O best of the Bhṛgus; / [for] a sacrifice with meager sacrificial fee destroys life, sons, fame,
intelligence, wealth, and host of mantras; therefore one of little wealth should not sacrifice. / He who has grain sufficient for three years to satisfy his dependents,
or if more is found, is worthy to drink soma. / But without having given the Prājāpatya as the sacrificial fee for the establishment of the fires,

अनाहिताग्निर्भवति ब्राह्मणो विभवे सति॥
सर्वदेवमयो विष्णुः प्रत्यहं तस्य पूजनम् ॥ 25 ॥
प्रतिमायामपि तथा कर्तव्यं भृगुसत्तम ॥
विष्णुमेवाभिजानन्ति सर्वयज्ञेषु वै द्विजाः ॥ 26 ॥
पायसैः सुमनोभिश्च तस्यापि यजनं स्मृतम् ॥
तत्तद्देवनिकायेषु तथैव स्वयमेव वा ॥ 27 ॥
पूजा कार्या बहिर्वेदौ श्रद्धया भृगुनन्दन ॥
नत्वल्पदक्षिणैर्यज्ञैर्यजेतेह कदाचन ॥ 28 ॥
विष्णुं देवनिकायस्थं यथाश्रद्धमरिन्दम ॥
तपसा पूजयेन्नित्यं तस्मादल्पधनो नरः ॥ 29 ॥
संपूज्य देवं परमान्नगन्धैर्धूपैः सुगन्धैश्च फलैश्च मुख्यैः ॥
तस्मादवाप्नोति स सर्वयज्ञांस्तस्मात्प्रपूज्यः सततं महात्मा॥2.95.30॥
2.19.m:
a brahmin is one who has not established his sacred fires, even if he possesses wealth. / Viṣṇu comprises all the gods; daily worship of him,
even in an image, should be performed, O best of the Bhṛgus; / twice-born men recognize Viṣṇu alone in all sacrifices.
Sacrificing to him with milk-rice and flowers is also prescribed, / among various groups of gods, or indeed by oneself.
worship should be performed outside the sacrificial altar with faith, O scion of Bhṛgu. / One should never sacrifice here with sacrifices that have small sacrificial fees.
A man of little wealth, O vanquisher of foes, / should therefore constantly worship with ascetic practice Viṣṇu residing among the host of gods, according to his faith.
Having fully worshipped the god with the fragrances of the best food, with fragrant incenses, and with the finest fruits, / he thereby attains [the fruits of] all sacrifices; therefore, the Great-Souled One is to be worshipped continually.

2.20.d:
कर्मैतत्सततं कृत्वा वह्न्याधानमथाप्नुयात् ॥ ।
कर्मैतदुक्तं रिपुनाशकारि सर्वाग्निकर्मप्रसमृद्धिदं च ॥
धन्यं यशस्यं च तथैव काम्यं नित्यं कृतं धर्मविदां वरिष्ठ ॥ 2.96.10 ॥
2.97
राम उवाच ॥ ॥
अग्न्याधानमथाप्नोति शत्रुनाशमथापि वा ॥
स्वेच्छया कर्मणा केन सदा यादोनृपात्मज ॥ 1 ॥
शत्रुनाशकरं कर्म कथयस्व ततः परम् ॥
तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्र श्रद्धा सदा मम ॥ 2 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
कृतोपवासो याम्यर्क्षे कृत्तिकासु सदैव तु ॥
पूजयेद्वासुदेवं तु कुङ्कुमेन सुग न्धिना ॥3॥
रक्तैश्च कुसुमैर्हृद्यैर्धूपं दद्याच्च गुग्गुलम् ॥
घृतेन दीपं दद्याच्च रक्तवर्णं तथैव च॥4॥
निवेदनीयं देवाय तथा सर्वं निवेदयेत् ॥
होतव्यं सुसमिद्धेऽग्नौ तथैवात्र शुभं हविः ॥
आयुधानि च देयानि ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च दक्षिणा ॥5 ॥
2.20.m:
Having constantly performed this rite, he may then attain the establishment of the sacred fire. / This rite is declared to be the destroyer of enemies, granting success in all fire-rituals, / conferring fortune, bestowing renown, and fulfilling desires, when performed regularly, O best among knowers of dharma.
2.97
Rāma said: / By which voluntary rite does one always attain the establishment of the sacred fire / or the destruction of enemies, O prince of aquatic beings?
Declare to me the further rite that causes the destruction of enemies; / I desire to hear that, for my faith is ever therein.
Puṣkara said: / Having fasted under the constellation of Yama, one should always / worship Vāsudeva under the Kṛttikās with fragrant saffron,
and with charming red flowers, and should offer guggulu incense; / and he should offer a ghee lamp of red colour.
He should offer to the god whatever is to be offered; / and an auspicious oblation must be poured into a well-kindled fire; / weapons should be presented, and a sacrificial fee to the brahmins.

2.20.s:
karmaitaduktaṃ ripunāśakāri dhāryaṃ sadā śatrugaṇapramāthi ..
kṛtvaitadagryaṃ ripunāśamāśu prāpnoti martyo na hi saṃśayo'tra .. 6 ..
2.98
rāma uvāca ..
kāmyāni tvaṃ samācakṣva snānānyanyāni devaja ..
kena snānena dharmajña kaṃ kaṃ kāmamavāpnuyāt ..1..
puṣkara uvāca ..
purodhāḥ sopavāsastu sarvasnānāni kārayet ..
sopavāsasya dharmajña tathā sarvatra mānavaḥ .. 2 ..
akālamūlāḥ kalaśāḥ kāryāḥ sarveṣu bhārgava ..
pūjā candramasaḥ kāryā varuṇasya tathaiva ca .. 3 ..

sarvagasyāprameyasya vāsudevasya cāpyathā..4..

kāmyaṃ snānaṃ sadā kuryānnakṣatraṃ tu na laṃghayet..
mantrayetsnānakalaśaṃ mantreṇānena bhārgava ..5 ..
2.20.d:
कर्मैतदुक्तं रिपुनाशकारि धार्यं सदा शत्रुगणप्रमाथि ॥
कृत्वैतदग्र्यं रिपुनाशमाशु प्राप्नोति मर्त्यो न हि संशयोऽत्र ॥ 6 ॥
2.98
राम उवाच ॥
काम्यानि त्वं समाचक्ष्व स्नानान्यन्यानि देवज ॥
केन स्नानेन धर्मज्ञ कं कं काममवाप्नुयात् ॥1॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
पुरोधाः सोपवासस्तु सर्वस्नानानि कारयेत् ॥
सोपवासस्य धर्मज्ञ तथा सर्वत्र मानवः ॥ 2 ॥
अकालमूलाः कलशाः कार्याः सर्वेषु भार्गव ॥
पूजा चन्द्रमसः कार्या वरुणस्य तथैव च ॥ 3 ॥
नक्षत्रदेवतानां च नक्षत्रस्य तथैव च ॥
सर्वगस्याप्रमेयस्य वासुदेवस्य चाप्यथा॥4॥
येषां च पूजा कर्तव्या तेषां च जुहुयाद्धविः ॥
काम्यं स्नानं सदा कुर्यान्नक्षत्रं तु न लंघयेत्॥
मन्त्रयेत्स्नानकलशं मन्त्रेणानेन भार्गव ॥5 ॥
2.20.m:
This rite is declared to be the destroyer of enemies, constantly to be observed, crushing the host of adversaries; / having performed this foremost rite, a mortal quickly achieves the destruction of enemies; of this there is no doubt.
2.98
Rāma said: / Explain to me the other optional ablutions, O divine-born; / by which ablution, O knower of dharma, does one obtain what particular desire?
Puṣkara said: / The family priest, having fasted, should perform all ablutions / for the man who has fasted, O knower of dharma, everywhere in this manner.
Unbaked earthen pots are to be used in all of them, O Bhārgava; / worship must be paid to the Moon, and likewise to Varuṇa,
and to the deities of the asterism, and to the asterism itself, / and also to all-pervading, immeasurable Vāsudeva.
And for those to whom worship is due, an oblation should be offered; / one should always perform the optional ablution, but must not transgress the asterism. / One should consecrate the bath-pot with this mantra, O Bhārgava:

2.20.s:
mantraḥ-
āpaḥ somādyāḥ saṃbabhūvuḥ pavitrāgniḥ pāvanaḥ somasūryasaṃsthitā vāyunā naṣṭadoṣāśca yo nitya macchreyase satkṛtyāpsu syuḥ svāhā śāntiḥ śrīrnavapuṣṭirmahyaṃ bhūyāsaṃ sarvaśiraḥ ..
sādhusvāheti sūryaḥ saṃsthitā vāyunāmāṣṭadoṣā ..'
karmaitaduktaṃ ripunāśakāri sādhāraṇaṃ snānamidaṃ pavitram ..
ataḥ paraṃ te kathayāmi rāma snānāni kāmyāni sukhapradāni .. 6 ..
2.99
puṣkara uvāca ..
kṛttikāsnānamuktaṃ te vahnikarmaprasādhanam ..
tathārināśanaṃ mukhyaṃ vahnyādhyeyapradaṃ tathā .. 1..
rohiṇīṣu tathā snānaṃ proktaṃ putrapradaṃ putrapradaṃ tava ..
brahmavarcasakāmasya snānaṃ saumyamidaṃ śṛṇu .. 2 ..
pūrṇamaudumbaraiḥ patraiḥ kṛtvā rāma ghaṭatrayam ..
pūrṇacandrāṅkitaiḥ śuklaiḥ sūtramālyairalaṃkṛtam .. 3 ..
2.20.d:
मन्त्रः-
आपः सोमाद्याः संबभूवुः पवित्राग्निः पावनः सोमसूर्यसंस्थिता वायुना नष्टदोषाश्च यो नित्य मच्छ्रेयसे सत्कृत्याप्सु स्युः स्वाहा शान्तिः श्रीर्नवपुष्टिर्मह्यं भूयासं सर्वशिरः ॥
साधुस्वाहेति सूर्यः संस्थिता वायुनामाष्टदोषा ॥'
कर्मैतदुक्तं रिपुनाशकारि साधारणं स्नानमिदं पवित्रम् ॥
अतः परं ते कथयामि राम स्नानानि काम्यानि सुखप्रदानि ॥ 6 ॥
2.99
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
कृत्तिकास्नानमुक्तं ते वह्निकर्मप्रसाधनम् ॥
तथारिनाशनं मुख्यं वह्न्याध्येयप्रदं तथा ॥ 1॥
रोहिणीषु तथा स्नानं प्रोक्तं पुत्रप्रदं पुत्रप्रदं तव ॥
ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्य स्नानं सौम्यमिदं शृणु ॥ 2 ॥
पूर्णमौदुम्बरैः पत्रैः कृत्वा राम घटत्रयम् ॥
पूर्णचन्द्राङ्कितैः शुक्लैः सूत्रमाल्यैरलंकृतम् ॥ 3 ॥
2.20.m:
Mantra: / 'Waters arose from Soma and the rest; purifying fire is the purifier; residing in the moon and sun, their faults dispelled by the wind, may they ever be honoured in the waters for my welfare. Svāhā! May peace, prosperity, and renewed nourishment be mine. I am the head of all. / Sādhu svāhā! The sun, residing... their faults wiped away by the wind.' / This rite is declared to be the destroyer of enemies; this is the common, purifying bath. / Henceforth I shall tell you, O Rāma, of the optional ablutions that bestow happiness.
2.99
Puṣkara said: / The ablution under Kṛttikā, which accomplishes fire rituals, has been declared to you, / and which is pre-eminent in destroying foes, and bestowing the sacred fire.
Likewise, the bath under Rohiṇī has been declared to you as granting sons; / hear this mild [or Mrgaśīrṣa] ablution for one who desires the splendour of Brahman.
Having filled three jars with udumbara leaves, O Rāma, / decorated with white threads and garlands marked with full moons,

2.20.s:
tena saṃsnāpitaḥ paścātkṣaumavāsā yathāvidhi ..
devatāpūjanaṃ kṛtvā ghṛtaṃ hutvā hutāśane .. 4 ..
oṅkārapūtaṃ somāya kṣīraṃ hutvā tathā jale ..
nivedanīyaṃ somāya tathā pṛṣṭhamṛgatrayam .. 5 ..
mṛgaśṛṅgeṇa dhūpaṃ ca tathā dadyādanantaram ..
somena ca maṇirdhāryo jātarūpapariṣkṛtaḥ .. 6 ..
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā śubhadhenuḥ payasvinī ..
kṛtvā tannityamāpnoti brahmavarcasamuttamam .. 7 ..
ghṛtāmramadhupūrṇena snātaḥ kumbhena mānavaḥ ..
paṭṭiśālaṃkṛtenātha raktacandanavāriṇā .. 8 .. .
rudrāya māṃsaṃ rudhiraṃ tathā ca madhu pāyasam ..
kṛṣṇāni vāsāṃsi tathā dhūpaṃ guggulameva ca ..9..
dadyādghṛtena ca tathā homo mantrairvidhīyate ..
kṛṣṇāni vāsāṃsi tathā dātavyā dakṣiṇā bhavet .. 2.99.10 ..
2.20.d:
तेन संस्नापितः पश्चात्क्षौमवासा यथाविधि ॥
देवतापूजनं कृत्वा घृतं हुत्वा हुताशने ॥ 4 ॥
ओङ्कारपूतं सोमाय क्षीरं हुत्वा तथा जले ॥
निवेदनीयं सोमाय तथा पृष्ठमृगत्रयम् ॥ 5 ॥
मृगशृङ्गेण धूपं च तथा दद्यादनन्तरम् ॥
सोमेन च मणिर्धार्यो जातरूपपरिष्कृतः ॥ 6 ॥
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या शुभधेनुः पयस्विनी ॥
कृत्वा तन्नित्यमाप्नोति ब्रह्मवर्चसमुत्तमम् ॥ 7 ॥
घृताम्रमधुपूर्णेन स्नातः कुम्भेन मानवः ॥
पट्टिशालंकृतेनाथ रक्तचन्दनवारिणा ॥ 8 ॥ ।
रुद्राय मांसं रुधिरं तथा च मधु पायसम् ॥
कृष्णानि वासांसि तथा धूपं गुग्गुलमेव च ॥9॥
दद्याद्घृतेन च तथा होमो मन्त्रैर्विधीयते ॥
कृष्णानि वासांसि तथा दातव्या दक्षिणा भवेत् ॥ 2.99.10 ॥
2.20.m:
bathed with that, dressed in linen clothes according to rule, / having worshipped the deity, having offered ghee into the sacrificial fire,
having offered milk purified with the sound Oṃ into the water for Soma, / three backs of deer are likewise to be offered to Soma.
And he should then immediately offer incense with deer horn; / and an amulet adorned with gold is to be worn under [the asterism of] Soma.
And a sacrificial fee should be given here: an auspicious cow yielding milk. / Having done this constantly, he obtains the highest splendour of Brahman.
A man bathed with a jar filled with ghee, mango, and honey, / adorned with a paṭṭiśa weapon, and with red sandalwood water,
To Rudra [he should offer] meat and blood, and likewise honey, rice boiled in milk, / black garments, and incense of guggulu alone.
He should make offerings with ghee, and the fire offering is prescribed with mantras; / black garments should be given as the sacrificial fee.

2.20.s:
meṣāśvanaralomāni gardabhasya viśeṣataḥ ..
āyasī tu maṇau kṛtvā dvāri śatrornidhāpayet .. 11 ..
2.20.d:
मेषाश्वनरलोमानि गर्दभस्य विशेषतः ॥
आयसी तु मणौ कृत्वा द्वारि शत्रोर्निधापयेत् ॥ 11 ॥
2.20.m: The hair of a ram, a horse, and a man, and especially of a donkey, / he should put into an iron amulet and place at the enemy's door.

2.20.s:
ārdrāsnānamidaṃ rāma sarvaśatruvināśanam ..
sarvagandhaiḥ phalairbījaiḥ pūrṇaṃ kṛtvā ghaṭatrayam .. 12 ..
2.20.d:
आर्द्रास्नानमिदं राम सर्वशत्रुविनाशनम् ॥
सर्वगन्धैः फलैर्बीजैः पूर्णं कृत्वा घटत्रयम् ॥ 12 ॥
2.20.m: This is the bath under Ārdrā, O Rāma, which destroys all enemies. / Having filled three water jars with all perfumes, fruits, and seeds,

2.20.s:
snāpanaṃ tena kartavyamādityaistadanantaram ..
navanītaṃ ca kulmāṣaṃ matsyāṃścaiva svarāṃstathā .. 13 ..
2.20.d:
स्नापनं तेन कर्तव्यमादित्यैस्तदनन्तरम् ॥
नवनीतं च कुल्माषं मत्स्यांश्चैव स्वरांस्तथा ॥ 13 ॥
2.20.m: a bath should next be taken with that [water] under the Ādityas [Punarvasū]. / Butter, boiled grain, fish, and likewise drinks,

2.20.s:
nivedayeccaiva tathā matsyāni surabhīṇi ca ..
ghṛtākṣatābhyāṃ dhūpena homaścaiva vidhīyate .. 14 ..
2.20.d:
निवेदयेच्चैव तथा मत्स्यानि सुरभीणि च ॥
घृताक्षताभ्यां धूपेन होमश्चैव विधीयते ॥ 14 ॥
2.20.m: and fragrant fish he should offer. / The fire offering is prescribed with ghee, unbroken grains, and incense.

2.20.s:
taddine tu nadī yatra yoge gacchatu tāṃ mudā ..
suvarṇarūpyagandhaśca dhāraṇīyastathā maṇiḥ .. 15 ..
2.20.d:
तद्दिने तु नदी यत्र योगे गच्छतु तां मुदा ॥
सुवर्णरूप्यगन्धश्च धारणीयस्तथा मणिः ॥ 15 ॥
2.20.m: On that day, wherever there is a river, he should gladly go to it at the confluence [or astrological conjunction]; / an amulet of gold, silver, and fragrant substances should be worn.

2.20.s:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā rāma dhenuḥ payasvinī ..
snātaḥ punarvasāveva jātiśraiṣṭhyamavāpnuyāt .. 16 ..
2.20.d:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या राम धेनुः पयस्विनी ॥
स्नातः पुनर्वसावेव जातिश्रैष्ठ्यमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 16 ॥
2.20.m: And here a milch cow should be given as the sacrificial fee, O Rāma. / Having bathed under Punarvasu alone, one attains superiority of caste,

2.20.s:
putrānvā sumahābhāga yadīcchati tadāpnuyāt ..
gaurasarṣapakalkena rāmotsāditavigrahaḥ ..17..
2.20.d:
पुत्रान्वा सुमहाभाग यदीच्छति तदाप्नुयात् ॥
गौरसर्षपकल्केन रामोत्सादितविग्रहः ॥17॥
2.20.m: or sons, O highly fortunate one, if he desires; he obtains whatever he wishes. / With his body smeared with paste of white mustard, O Rāma,

2.20.s:
gavyājyapūrṇakumbhena snātaḥ snātastathauṣadhaiḥ ..
ahatāmbarasaṃvītaḥ pāyasaṃ vinivedayet .. 18 ..
2.20.d:
गव्याज्यपूर्णकुम्भेन स्नातः स्नातस्तथौषधैः ॥
अहताम्बरसंवीतः पायसं विनिवेदयेत् ॥ 18 ॥
2.20.m: bathed with a jar filled with cow's ghee, and likewise bathed with medicinal herbs, / dressed in unwashed garments, he should offer rice boiled in milk,

2.20.s:
śuklāni caiva mālyāni vāsāṃsyapahatāni ca ..
homaśca pāyasenātra dhūpaṃ gandhaiśca dāpayet .. 19 ..
2.20.d:
शुक्लानि चैव माल्यानि वासांस्यपहतानि च ॥
होमश्च पायसेनात्र धूपं गन्धैश्च दापयेत् ॥ 19 ॥
2.20.m: and white garlands and unwashed garments. / Here the fire offering is with rice boiled in milk, and he should offer incense of perfumes.

2.20.s:
maṇiḥ śirasi dhāryaśca daṇḍāgre brahmacāriṇaḥ ..
suvarṇagarbhaṃ puṣpeṇa snānaṃ puṣṭikaraṃ bhavet ..2.99.20...
2.20.d:
मणिः शिरसि धार्यश्च दण्डाग्रे ब्रह्मचारिणः ॥
सुवर्णगर्भं पुष्पेण स्नानं पुष्टिकरं भवेत् ॥2.99.20॥।
2.20.m: The amulet should be worn on the head, or on the tip of the staff for a brahmacārin. / The bath containing gold and flowers brings nourishment.

2.20.s:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā ghṛtaṃ kanakasaṃyutam ..
ṣaḍdhvajāṃ nīlasūtreṇa nīlapuṣpaiśca veṣṭitām .. 21 ..
2.20.d:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या घृतं कनकसंयुतम् ॥
षड्ध्वजां नीलसूत्रेण नीलपुष्पैश्च वेष्टिताम् ॥ 21 ॥
2.20.m: And here ghee accompanied by gold should be given as the sacrificial fee. / Having six banners, wrapped with blue thread and blue flowers,

2.20.s:
sarṣapānveṣṭayedrāma nāgapuṣpeṇa bhūriṇā ..
valmīkānāṃ sahastasya tathaivāgramṛdā dvija..22..
2.20.d:
सर्षपान्वेष्टयेद्राम नागपुष्पेण भूरिणा ॥
वल्मीकानां सहस्तस्य तथैवाग्रमृदा द्विज॥22॥
2.20.m: he should wrap mustard seeds with abundant nāgapuṣpa, O Rāma, / with the earth from ant-hills and likewise earth from the tip of an elephant's trunk, O twice-born.

2.20.s:
tai snātaḥ sarvanāgebhyo madhulājāṃ nivedayet..
gandhodakaṃ tathā dhānāḥ ṣaṭkṛtvātha punaḥpunaḥ..23...
2.20.d:
तै स्नातः सर्वनागेभ्यो मधुलाजां निवेदयेत्॥
गन्धोदकं तथा धानाः षट्कृत्वाथ पुनःपुनः॥23॥।
2.20.m: Bathed with these, he should offer parched grain with honey to all the nāgas, / and perfumed water and parched grain six times, repeatedly.

2.20.s:
kṣīreṇa homaḥ kartavyo dhūpaḥ sarvatvacā tathā ..
sarpatvaṅ nāgapuṣpaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ ca maṇirbhavet .. 24 ..
2.20.d:
क्षीरेण होमः कर्तव्यो धूपः सर्वत्वचा तथा ॥
सर्पत्वङ् नागपुष्पं च सुवर्णं च मणिर्भवेत् ॥ 24 ॥
2.20.m: The fire offering should be made with milk, and the incense with all [aromatic] barks; / snake-skin, nāgapuṣpa, and gold should form the amulet.

2.20.s:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā śayanīyaṃ manoharam ..
snānaṃ sārpeṇa te proktaṃ bhogyaṃ siddhikaraṃ bhavet ..25..
2.20.d:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या शयनीयं मनोहरम् ॥
स्नानं सार्पेण ते प्रोक्तं भोग्यं सिद्धिकरं भवेत् ॥25॥
2.20.m: And here a delightful bed should be given as the sacrificial fee. / The bath under the serpent asterism [Āśleṣā] has been declared to you; it brings enjoyment and success,

2.20.s:
śrīpradaṃ vā mahābhāga kathitaṃ kāmatastava ..
plakṣapatraistilaiḥ kṛṣṇairghaṭaṣaṭkaṃ tu pūrayet ..26..
2.20.d:
श्रीप्रदं वा महाभाग कथितं कामतस्तव ॥
प्लक्षपत्रैस्तिलैः कृष्णैर्घटषट्कं तु पूरयेत् ॥26॥
2.20.m: or it bestows prosperity, O highly fortunate one, declared according to your desire. / One should fill six jars with plakṣa leaves and black sesame seeds,

2.20.s:
veṣṭayetkṛṣṇamālyaiśca tena snāto'hatāmbaraḥ ..
dakṣiṇāgreṣu darbheṣu saptapiṇḍānupāharet .. 27 ..
2.20.d:
वेष्टयेत्कृष्णमाल्यैश्च तेन स्नातोऽहताम्बरः ॥
दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु सप्तपिण्डानुपाहरेत् ॥ 27 ॥
2.20.m: and wrap them with black garlands. Bathed with that [water] and wearing unwashed garments, / he should offer seven piṇḍas on darbha grass with their points directed south.

2.20.s:
subhāsvaro barhiṣado hyagniṣvāttāstathaiva ca ..
kravyādaścopahūtāśca ājyapāśca sukālinaḥ .. 28 ..
2.20.d:
सुभास्वरो बर्हिषदो ह्यग्निष्वात्तास्तथैव च ॥
क्रव्यादश्चोपहूताश्च आज्यपाश्च सुकालिनः ॥ 28 ॥
2.20.m: The Subhāsvaras, the Barhiṣads, the Agniṣvāttas, / the Kravyāds, the Upahūtas, the Ājyapas, and the Sukālins:

2.20.s:
pitaraḥ kathitāsteṣāṃ piṇḍaṃ dadyātkrameṇa ca ..
dhūpaṃ vrīhiyavairdadyāttilairhomaṃ tu kārayet .. 29 ...
2.20.d:
पितरः कथितास्तेषां पिण्डं दद्यात्क्रमेण च ॥
धूपं व्रीहियवैर्दद्यात्तिलैर्होमं तु कारयेत् ॥ 29 ॥।
2.20.m: these are declared to be the ancestors; he should offer a piṇḍa to them in order. / He should offer incense with rice and barley, and make the fire offering with sesame.

2.20.s:
dātavyā dakṣiṇā cātra tilānrajatameva ca ..
vacā ca korakaṃ caiva trivṛtaṃ dhārayenmaṇim .. 2.99.30 ..
2.20.d:
दातव्या दक्षिणा चात्र तिलान्रजतमेव च ॥
वचा च कोरकं चैव त्रिवृतं धारयेन्मणिम् ॥ 2.99.30 ॥
2.20.m: And here sesame and silver should be given as the sacrificial fee. / He should wear an amulet of three strands containing vacā and buds.

2.20.s:
pitṛprasādaṃ prāpnoti karmasiddhimathāpi ca ..
maghāsnānamidaṃ kṛtvā nityameva samāhitaḥ .. 31 ..
2.20.d:
पितृप्रसादं प्राप्नोति कर्मसिद्धिमथापि च ॥
मघास्नानमिदं कृत्वा नित्यमेव समाहितः ॥ 31 ॥
2.20.m: He attains the favor of the ancestors and the success of his work, / having performed this bath under Maghā, always composed in mind.

2.20.s:
mākṣikaṃ ca madhūkaṃ ca tathaiva madhuyaṣṭikām ..
kṛtvā kumbhadvayaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhagnāṅgaḥ snāpayennaram .. 32 ..
2.20.d:
माक्षिकं च मधूकं च तथैव मधुयष्टिकाम् ॥
कृत्वा कुम्भद्वयं पूर्णं भग्नाङ्गः स्नापयेन्नरम् ॥ 32 ॥
2.20.m: Having filled two jars with honey, madhūka, and liquorice, / a man with fractured limbs should bathe.

2.20.s:
śālipiṣṭaṃ tataḥ snāto ghṛtena madhunā yutam ..
gandhamālyaṃ bahuvidhaṃ bahukṛtvā bhagāya tu .. 33 ..
2.20.d:
शालिपिष्टं ततः स्नातो घृतेन मधुना युतम् ॥
गन्धमाल्यं बहुविधं बहुकृत्वा भगाय तु ॥ 33 ॥
2.20.m: Then, having bathed, [he should offer] rice flour mixed with ghee and honey, / and manifold perfumes and garlands, abundantly prepared, to Bhaga.

2.20.s:
nivedayitvā deyāni citramāṃsāni cāpyatha ..
ghṛtena dhūpo dātavyo homaḥ kāryaḥ priyaṅgunā .. 34 ..
2.20.d:
निवेदयित्वा देयानि चित्रमांसानि चाप्यथ ॥
घृतेन धूपो दातव्यो होमः कार्यः प्रियङ्गुना ॥ 34 ॥
2.20.m: Having offered [these], various kinds of meat should then be given. / Incense should be given with ghee, and the fire offering should be made with priyaṅgu.

2.20.s:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā citravāsāṃsi cāpyatha ..
pārāvatasya pakṣāṇi cakravākasya mānada .. 35 ..
2.20.d:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या चित्रवासांसि चाप्यथ ॥
पारावतस्य पक्षाणि चक्रवाकस्य मानद ॥ 35 ॥
2.20.m: And here various garments should be given as the sacrificial fee. / The wings of a pigeon and of a cakravāka bird, O honor-giver,

2.20.s:
trivṛtāni tathā kṛtvā maṇiṃ śirasi dhārayet ..
saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnoti snātvaiva bhagadaivate .. 36 ..
2.20.d:
त्रिवृतानि तथा कृत्वा मणिं शिरसि धारयेत् ॥
सौभाग्यं महदाप्नोति स्नात्वैव भगदैवते ॥ 36 ॥
2.20.m: having made into a three-stranded amulet, he should wear it on his head. / Having bathed under the deity Bhaga [Pūrvaphalgunī], he attains great good fortune.

2.20.s:
tilamākṣikapūrṇena snātaḥ kumbhadvayena tu ..
āryakṣe pāyasaṃ dadyātpītarakte ca vāsasī .. 37 ..
2.20.d:
तिलमाक्षिकपूर्णेन स्नातः कुम्भद्वयेन तु ॥
आर्यक्षे पायसं दद्यात्पीतरक्ते च वाससी ॥ 37 ॥
2.20.m: Bathed with two jars filled with sesame and honey, / under the asterism of Aryaman [Uttarāphalgunī] he should offer rice boiled in milk and yellow and red garments.

2.20.s:
dhūpe śatāvarī deyā homaḥ kāryastathākṣataiḥ ..
tejovantī priyaṅguśca trivṛtaṃ dhārayenmaṇim .. 38 ..
2.20.d:
धूपे शतावरी देया होमः कार्यस्तथाक्षतैः ॥
तेजोवन्ती प्रियङ्गुश्च त्रिवृतं धारयेन्मणिम् ॥ 38 ॥
2.20.m: Śatāvarī should be given for incense, and the fire offering should be made with unbroken grains. / He should wear a three-stranded amulet of tejovantī and priyaṅgu.

2.20.s:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā tathā rakte ca vāsasī ..
uttarāphalgunīsnānaṃ sarvārambhaprasiddhidam .. 39 ..
2.20.d:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या तथा रक्ते च वाससी ॥
उत्तराफल्गुनीस्नानं सर्वारम्भप्रसिद्धिदम् ॥ 39 ॥
2.20.m: And here two red garments should be given as the sacrificial fee. / The bath under Uttarāphalgunī grants success in all undertakings,

2.20.s:
vīryasya vardhanaṃ cāpi kartavyamanusūnunā ..
gajakāmasya te snānaṃ haste pūrvaṃ mayoditam .. 2.99.40 ..
2.20.d:
वीर्यस्य वर्धनं चापि कर्तव्यमनुसूनुना ॥
गजकामस्य ते स्नानं हस्ते पूर्वं मयोदितम् ॥ 2.99.40 ॥
2.20.m: and it increases strength; it should be performed by one who has sons. / The bath under Hasta for one desiring elephants was declared by me previously;

2.20.s:
parasainyajayārthāya snānaṃ tadapi śasyate ..
maṃjiṣṭhāṃ ca samaṅgāṃ ca misikāntāṃ ca bhārgava .. 41 ..
2.20.d:
परसैन्यजयार्थाय स्नानं तदपि शस्यते ॥
मंजिष्ठां च समङ्गां च मिसिकान्तां च भार्गव ॥ 41 ॥
2.20.m: that bath is also commended for victory over an enemy's army. / Mañjiṣṭhā, samaṅgā, and misikāntā, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

2.20.s:
kanakaṃ rajataṃ caiva pūrṇakumbhe vinikṣipet ..
tenābhiṣiktaścitrāṇi mālyavāsāṃsyanantaram .. 42 ..
2.20.d:
कनकं रजतं चैव पूर्णकुम्भे विनिक्षिपेत् ॥
तेनाभिषिक्तश्चित्राणि माल्यवासांस्यनन्तरम् ॥ 42 ॥
2.20.m: and gold and silver he should cast into a full jar. / Bathed with that [water], he should immediately with devotion offer variegated

2.20.s:
tvāṣṭre nivedayedbhaktyā homaṃ kṣīreṇa kārayet ..
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā citravastrāṇi mānada .. 43 ..
2.20.d:
त्वाष्ट्रे निवेदयेद्भक्त्या होमं क्षीरेण कारयेत् ॥
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या चित्रवस्त्राणि मानद ॥ 43 ॥
2.20.m: garlands and garments to Tvaṣṭṛ, and perform the fire offering with milk. / And here variegated garments should be given as the sacrificial fee, O honor-giver,

2.20.s:
sarvagandhaistathā dhūpaṃ baliṃ citraṃ tathaiva ca ..
pṛthaksrutiprasūtānāṃ puṣpānāṃ kanakairvṛtam .. 44 ..
2.20.d:
सर्वगन्धैस्तथा धूपं बलिं चित्रं तथैव च ॥
पृथक्स्रुतिप्रसूतानां पुष्पानां कनकैर्वृतम् ॥ 44 ॥
2.20.m: and incense with all perfumes, and a variegated offering of food. / An amulet covered in gold, made of eighteen flowers

2.20.s:
aṣṭādaśānāṃ ca tathā maṇiṃ śirasi dhārayet ..
evaṃ snātastu citrāsu saubhāgyaṃ mahadaśnute .. 45 ..
2.20.d:
अष्टादशानां च तथा मणिं शिरसि धारयेत् ॥
एवं स्नातस्तु चित्रासु सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते ॥ 45 ॥
2.20.m: sprung from separate streams, he should wear on his head. / Bathed thus under Citrā, he attains great good fortune,

2.20.s:
sarvabhūteṣu cādhikyaṃ yadicchati tadāpnuyāt ..
rukmamaśvavatthapatraṃ ca khaḍgaśṛṅgaṃ tathaiva ca .. 46 ..
2.20.d:
सर्वभूतेषु चाधिक्यं यदिच्छति तदाप्नुयात् ॥
रुक्ममश्ववत्थपत्रं च खड्गशृङ्गं तथैव च ॥ 46 ॥
2.20.m: and preeminence among all beings; whatever he wishes, that he obtains. / Gold, an aśvattha leaf, and the horn of a rhinoceros

2.20.s:
pūrṇakumbhe vinikṣipya snātaḥ śīdhusurāsavam ..
vāyavye prayato dadyātkṣīraṃ sapalalaṃ dadhi .. 47 ..
2.20.d:
पूर्णकुम्भे विनिक्षिप्य स्नातः शीधुसुरासवम् ॥
वायव्ये प्रयतो दद्यात्क्षीरं सपललं दधि ॥ 47 ॥
2.20.m: having placed in a full jar, bathed, restrained in mind, he should offer rum, wine, and liquor, / milk, sesamum paste, and curds to Vāyu [the deity of Svātī].

2.20.s:
gandhaṃ dhūpaṃ tathā dadyāddhome kāryaṃ tathā ghṛtam .. .
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca .. 48 ..
2.20.d:
गन्धं धूपं तथा दद्याद्धोमे कार्यं तथा घृतम् ॥ ।
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या वासांसि विविधानि च ॥ 48 ॥
2.20.m: He should give perfume and incense, and ghee should be used in the fire offering. / And here various garments should be given as the sacrificial fee.

2.20.s:
dvaṣṭāśvaśyāmahārītahaṃsapakṣaiḥ payo'nvitam ..
dhārayecca maṇiṃ vidvānsvātāvevaṃ samācaret .. .. 49 ..
2.20.d:
द्वष्टाश्वश्यामहारीतहंसपक्षैः पयोऽन्वितम् ॥
धारयेच्च मणिं विद्वान्स्वातावेवं समाचरेत् ॥ ॥ 49 ॥
2.20.m: With the wings of sixteen dark hārīta birds and geese, accompanied by milk, / the wise man should wear an amulet; he should perform thus under Svātī.

2.20.s:
vāṇijye samyagāpnoti siddhiṃ ca mahatīṃ naraḥ ..
viśākhāsu tathā snānaṃ kāryaṃ kumbhadvayena tu .. 2.99.50 ..
2.20.d:
वाणिज्ये सम्यगाप्नोति सिद्धिं च महतीं नरः ॥
विशाखासु तथा स्नानं कार्यं कुम्भद्वयेन तु ॥ 2.99.50 ॥
2.20.m: A man fully attains great success in commerce. / Under Viśākhā, a bath should likewise be performed with two jars.

2.20.s:
kṛttikāsu mahābhāga tataḥ śākaṃ nivedayet ..
indrāgnibhyāṃ ca vāsāṃsi pītaraktāni cāpyatha .. 51 ..
2.20.d:
कृत्तिकासु महाभाग ततः शाकं निवेदयेत् ॥
इन्द्राग्निभ्यां च वासांसि पीतरक्तानि चाप्यथ ॥ 51 ॥
2.20.m: Under Kṛttikā, O highly fortunate one, he should then offer vegetables, / and yellow and red garments to Indra and Agni,

2.20.s:
mālyāni ca mahābhāga dhūpaṃ ca ghṛtaguggulam ..
homārthe ca ghṛtaṃ kuryāddakṣiṇā kanakaṃ tathā .. 52 ..
2.20.d:
माल्यानि च महाभाग धूपं च घृतगुग्गुलम् ॥
होमार्थे च घृतं कुर्याद्दक्षिणा कनकं तथा ॥ 52 ॥
2.20.m: and garlands, O highly fortunate one, and incense of ghee and guggulu. / And for the fire offering he should use ghee, and gold as the sacrificial fee.

2.20.s:
gaṇādhipatyamāpnoti kṛtvaivaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
sahasravīryaṃ cānantāṃ madhūkaṃ ca tathā misim .. 53 ..
2.20.d:
गणाधिपत्यमाप्नोति कृत्वैवं नात्र संशयः ॥
सहस्रवीर्यं चानन्तां मधूकं च तथा मिसिम् ॥ 53 ॥
2.20.m: By doing this, one attains leadership over hosts, there is no doubt of this. / [Placing] sahasravīryā, anantā, madhūka, and also misi

2.20.s:
pūrṇakumbhatraye kṛtvā kṛtasvastikalakṣaṇe ..
ahatāmbarasaṃvītaḥ sarvagandhaphalākṣataiḥ .. 54 ..
2.20.d:
पूर्णकुम्भत्रये कृत्वा कृतस्वस्तिकलक्षणे ॥
अहताम्बरसंवीतः सर्वगन्धफलाक्षतैः ॥ 54 ॥
2.20.m: in three full jars marked with a svastika, / clad in unwashed garments, with all kinds of perfumes, fruits, and unbroken grains,

2.20.s:
madhunā ca baliṃ dadyānmitrāya ca mahātmane ..
vṛścikena tathā dhūpaṃ yavairhomaṃ ca mānada .. 55 ..
2.20.d:
मधुना च बलिं दद्यान्मित्राय च महात्मने ॥
वृश्चिकेन तथा धूपं यवैर्होमं च मानद ॥ 55 ॥
2.20.m: and with honey, he should offer an oblation to the great-souled Mitra. / [He should offer] incense with scorpion[-grass], and an oblation into fire with barley, O respectful one.

2.20.s:
puradvāraṃ kaṭāhāśca cūḍākāṣṭhaṃ sakāñcanam ..
dhārayeddakṣiṇāṃ dadyāttathā ca kanakaṃ dvija .. 56 ..
2.20.d:
पुरद्वारं कटाहाश्च चूडाकाष्ठं सकाञ्चनम् ॥
धारयेद्दक्षिणां दद्यात्तथा च कनकं द्विज ॥ 56 ॥
2.20.m: Wood from a city gate, frying pans, and crest-wood, together with gold, / he should wear; and he should give sacrificial fee, likewise gold, O twice-born.

2.20.s:
evaṃ maitre sadā snātaḥ sarvabhūtaiḥ samāpnuyāt ..
maitrīṃ manujaśārdūla puraṃ vā kurute vaśe .. 57 ..
2.20.d:
एवं मैत्रे सदा स्नातः सर्वभूतैः समाप्नुयात् ॥
मैत्रीं मनुजशार्दूल पुरं वा कुरुते वशे ॥ 57 ॥
2.20.m: Having bathed thus always under the star of Mitra, / he attains friendship with all beings, O tiger among men, or brings a city under his control.

2.20.s:
taḍāgapadminīkūlanadīnadasamudbhavaiḥ ..
toyaiḥ pūrṇa ghaṭānkṛtvā sarvabījasamanvitān .. 58 ..
2.20.d:
तडागपद्मिनीकूलनदीनदसमुद्भवैः ॥
तोयैः पूर्ण घटान्कृत्वा सर्वबीजसमन्वितान् ॥ 58 ॥
2.20.m: Having filled jars with water originating from ponds, lotus-pools, banks, / and flowing rivers, accompanied by all seeds,

2.20.s:
sarvaratnauṣadhīpūrṇānstrīsnānaṃ taiḥ samācaret ..
kṣaumavāsāstu ratnāni mālyāni ca phalāni ca .. .. 59 ..
2.20.d:
सर्वरत्नौषधीपूर्णान्स्त्रीस्नानं तैः समाचरेत् ॥
क्षौमवासास्तु रत्नानि माल्यानि च फलानि च ॥ ॥ 59 ॥
2.20.m: filled with all gems and medicinal herbs, one should perform a woman's bath with them. / Clad in linen garments, [offering] gems, garlands, and fruits,

2.20.s:
ratnāni dadyācchakrāya prāṅmukhaḥ susamāhitaḥ ..
dhūpaṃ dadyācca śīrṣeṇa viśākhāvanmaṇirbhavet .. 2.99.60 ..
2.20.d:
रत्नानि दद्याच्छक्राय प्राङ्मुखः सुसमाहितः ॥
धूपं दद्याच्च शीर्षेण विशाखावन्मणिर्भवेत् ॥ 2.99.60 ॥
2.20.m: facing east, deeply concentrated, he should offer gems to Śakra. / He should offer incense with his head; [and] there should be an amulet like Viśākhā.

2.20.s:
chatraṃ ca dakṣiṇā deyā jyeṣṭhāyāṃ bhṛgunandana ..
snānameva sadā kṛtvā rājyamāpnotyakaṇṭakam .. 61 ..
2.20.d:
छत्रं च दक्षिणा देया ज्येष्ठायां भृगुनन्दन ॥
स्नानमेव सदा कृत्वा राज्यमाप्नोत्यकण्टकम् ॥ 61 ॥
2.20.m: An umbrella should be given as the sacrificial fee under Jyeṣṭhā, O son of Bhṛgu. / By performing this bath constantly, he attains a kingdom free of thorns.

2.20.s:
kṛṣikāmasya mūlena snānamuktaṃ mayā purā ..
tathā vāṇijyakāmasya prāgaṣāḍhāsu bhārgava .. 62 ..
2.20.d:
कृषिकामस्य मूलेन स्नानमुक्तं मया पुरा ॥
तथा वाणिज्यकामस्य प्रागषाढासु भार्गव ॥ 62 ॥
2.20.m: The bath for one desiring agriculture under Mūla was spoken by me previously, / as well as for one desiring commerce under Pūrvāṣāḍhā, O Bhārgava.

2.20.s:
athottarāsu ṣāḍhāsu kuryādghaṭacatuṣṭayam ..
puṣpabījaphalopetaṃ tena snātastu mānavaḥ .. 63 ..
2.20.d:
अथोत्तरासु षाढासु कुर्याद्घटचतुष्टयम् ॥
पुष्पबीजफलोपेतं तेन स्नातस्तु मानवः ॥ 63 ॥
2.20.m: Now under Uttarāṣāḍhā he should prepare four jars / provided with flowers, seeds, and fruits; and having bathed therewith, a man,

2.20.s:
kṣaumavāsāḥ surāṃ caiva pāyasaṃ ca nivedayet ..
mudgamiśraṃ ca dharmajña mālyavāsāṃsi cecchayā .. 64 ..
2.20.d:
क्षौमवासाः सुरां चैव पायसं च निवेदयेत् ॥
मुद्गमिश्रं च धर्मज्ञ माल्यवासांसि चेच्छया ॥ 64 ॥
2.20.m: wearing linen garments, should offer liquor and milk-rice / mixed with mung beans, O knower of dharma, and garlands and garments at will.

2.20.s:
home ca pāyasaṃ kuryāddhūpe gośṛṅgameva ca ..
dhātrīpuṣpaśamībilvairmaṇirdhāryaḥ sakāñcanaiḥ .. 65 ..
2.20.d:
होमे च पायसं कुर्याद्धूपे गोशृङ्गमेव च ॥
धात्रीपुष्पशमीबिल्वैर्मणिर्धार्यः सकाञ्चनैः ॥ 65 ॥
2.20.m: For the oblation into fire he should use milk-rice, and cow-horn for incense. / An amulet of emblic myrobalan flower, śamī, and bilva, together with gold, should be worn.

2.20.s:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā suvarṇaṃ raupyameva ca ..
rājaśreṣṭhatvamāpnoti vivādeṣu jayaṃ tathā .. 66 ..
2.20.d:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या सुवर्णं रौप्यमेव च ॥
राजश्रेष्ठत्वमाप्नोति विवादेषु जयं तथा ॥ 66 ॥
2.20.m: And the sacrificial fee to be given here is gold and silver. / He attains supremacy among kings and victory in disputes.

2.20.s:
bilvaṃ ca tagaraṃ caiva candanaṃ madhuyaṣṭikām ..
priyaṅguṃ ca madhūkaṃ ca triṣu kumbheṣu nikṣipet .. 67 ..
2.20.d:
बिल्वं च तगरं चैव चन्दनं मधुयष्टिकाम् ॥
प्रियङ्गुं च मधूकं च त्रिषु कुम्भेषु निक्षिपेत् ॥ 67 ॥
2.20.m: Bilva, tagara, sandalwood, liquorice, / priyaṅgu, and madhūka he should cast into three jars,

2.20.s:
saṃgamādāhṛtaṃ toyaṃ tanmṛdaṃ ca bhṛgūttama ..
tena snātastataḥ snānaṃ kuryātsarvauṣadhairdvija .. 68 ..
2.20.d:
संगमादाहृतं तोयं तन्मृदं च भृगूत्तम ॥
तेन स्नातस्ततः स्नानं कुर्यात्सर्वौषधैर्द्विज ॥ 68 ॥
2.20.m: and water brought from a confluence and clay from it, O foremost of the Bhṛgus. / Having bathed with that, the twice-born should then perform a bath with all medicinal herbs.

2.20.s:
kulatthā'nnaṃ saśālyannaṃ mukhyāni ca phalāni ca ..
baliṃ ca viṣṇave dadyānmudgairdhūpaṃ tathaiva ca .. 69 ..
2.20.d:
कुलत्थाऽन्नं सशाल्यन्नं मुख्यानि च फलानि च ॥
बलिं च विष्णवे दद्यान्मुद्गैर्धूपं तथैव च ॥ 69 ॥
2.20.m: Food made of horse-gram together with śāli-rice food and choice fruits / and an offering he should present to Viṣṇu, and likewise incense with mung beans.

2.20.s:
rājacchatrasya daṇḍāgrātkāṣṭhaṃ śakradhvajāttathā ..
siṃhadaṃṣṭrāmaṇiścātra sarukmaḥ śirasi smṛtaḥ .. 2.99.70 ..
2.20.d:
राजच्छत्रस्य दण्डाग्रात्काष्ठं शक्रध्वजात्तथा ॥
सिंहदंष्ट्रामणिश्चात्र सरुक्मः शिरसि स्मृतः ॥ 2.99.70 ॥
2.20.m: Wood from the tip of the staff of a royal umbrella and from Śakra's banner, / and an amulet of a lion's tooth together with gold, is prescribed here for the head.

2.20.s:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā dhenuḥ kāṃsyopadohinī..
evaṃ tu śravaṇasnāyī rājyamāpnotyakaṇṭakam .. 71 ..
2.20.d:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या धेनुः कांस्योपदोहिनी॥
एवं तु श्रवणस्नायी राज्यमाप्नोत्यकण्टकम् ॥ 71 ॥
2.20.m: And the sacrificial fee to be given here is a milk-cow with a bronze milking vessel. / Bathing thus under Śravaṇa, he attains a kingdom free of thorns,

2.20.s:
anyadeśādhipatyaṃ vā rājyamāpnoti bhārgava ..
atimuktakapatrāṇi bilvasya ca tathā kṣipet .. 72 ..
2.20.d:
अन्यदेशाधिपत्यं वा राज्यमाप्नोति भार्गव ॥
अतिमुक्तकपत्राणि बिल्वस्य च तथा क्षिपेत् ॥ 72 ॥
2.20.m: or he attains sovereignty over another realm or kingship, O Bhārgava. / He should then cast leaves of atimuktaka and bilva

2.20.s:
kumbheṣu pañcasu tataḥ snānaṃ taistu samācaret ..
vāstubhyastu baliṃ dadyātsuvarṇaṃ mākṣike tataḥ .. 73 ..
2.20.d:
कुम्भेषु पञ्चसु ततः स्नानं तैस्तु समाचरेत् ॥
वास्तुभ्यस्तु बलिं दद्यात्सुवर्णं माक्षिके ततः ॥ 73 ॥
2.20.m: into five jars, and then perform a bath with them. / Then he should present an offering to the Vāstus, [and] gold in honey;

2.20.s:
dhūpaṃ vāyasapakṣaistu homaḥ kāryo ghṛtena tu ..
brahmacāriśilālopakākapakṣaṃ tathaiva ca .. 74 ..
2.20.d:
धूपं वायसपक्षैस्तु होमः कार्यो घृतेन तु ॥
ब्रह्मचारिशिलालोपकाकपक्षं तथैव च ॥ 74 ॥
2.20.m: incense with crow-feathers, and an oblation into fire should be made with ghee. / [With] a stone-flake of a celibate student and a crow's feather likewise,

2.20.s:
kākamācīṃ rukmayutāṃ maṇiṃ śirasi dhārayet ..
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā dhenu kāṃsyopadohinī .. 75 ..
2.20.d:
काकमाचीं रुक्मयुतां मणिं शिरसि धारयेत् ॥
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या धेनु कांस्योपदोहिनी ॥ 75 ॥
2.20.m: and black nightshade joined with gold, he should wear an amulet on his head. / And the sacrificial fee to be given here is a milk-cow with a bronze milking vessel.

2.20.s:
dhanaṃ prāpnoti sumahadvivāhe vāpi kanyakām ..
evaṃ snāto dhaniṣṭhāsu nityameva bhṛgūttama .. 76 ..
2.20.d:
धनं प्राप्नोति सुमहद्विवाहे वापि कन्यकाम् ॥
एवं स्नातो धनिष्ठासु नित्यमेव भृगूत्तम ॥ 76 ॥
2.20.m: He attains immense wealth, or indeed a maiden in marriage, / having bathed thus constantly under Dhaniṣṭhā, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.

2.20.s:
ārogyakārakaṃ snānaṃ pūrvamuktaṃ tu vāruṇam ..
ratnodakena snātastu naraḥ kumbhadvayena tu .. 77 ..
2.20.d:
आरोग्यकारकं स्नानं पूर्वमुक्तं तु वारुणम् ॥
रत्नोदकेन स्नातस्तु नरः कुम्भद्वयेन तु ॥ 77 ॥
2.20.m: The bath under the star of Varuṇa that produces health was described previously. / But a man bathed with gem-water from two jars

2.20.s:
ajaikapādāya baliṃ chāgaṃ dadyāttu pāyasam ..
śuklāni caiva mālyāni phalāni vividhāni ca .. 78 ..
2.20.d:
अजैकपादाय बलिं छागं दद्यात्तु पायसम् ॥
शुक्लानि चैव माल्यानि फलानि विविधानि च ॥ 78 ॥
2.20.m: should give an offering to Aja Ekapād: a goat and milk-rice, / and white garlands and diverse fruits,

2.20.s:
khaṭvāṅgañca tathā dhūpaṃ homaṃ ca payasā tathā ..
vyāghradaṃṣṭrā tathā lomanakhaṃ kanakameva ca .. 79 ..
2.20.d:
खट्वाङ्गञ्च तथा धूपं होमं च पयसा तथा ॥
व्याघ्रदंष्ट्रा तथा लोमनखं कनकमेव च ॥ 79 ॥
2.20.m: and khaṭvāṅga for incense, and an oblation into fire with milk. / A tiger's tooth, hair, a claw, and gold—

2.20.s:
maṇirdhāryo bhavedrāma chāgo deyā ca dakṣiṇā ..
ajaikapāde snātastu nityameva samāhitaḥ .. 2.99.80 ..
2.20.d:
मणिर्धार्यो भवेद्राम छागो देया च दक्षिणा ॥
अजैकपादे स्नातस्तु नित्यमेव समाहितः ॥ 2.99.80 ॥
2.20.m: an amulet [of these] should be worn, O Rāma, and a goat should be given as sacrificial fee. / Bathing under Aja Ekapād, always concentrated,

2.20.s:
uddharettu nidhiṃ rāma śatrūnvā vijayeddhruvam ..
āhirbudhnyaṃ tathā snānaṃ godamuktaṃ purā tava .. 81..
2.20.d:
उद्धरेत्तु निधिं राम शत्रून्वा विजयेद्ध्रुवम् ॥
आहिर्बुध्न्यं तथा स्नानं गोदमुक्तं पुरा तव ॥ 81॥
2.20.m: he would recover a treasure, O Rāma, or surely conquer his enemies. / The bath under Ahirbudhnya, granting cattle, was previously spoken to you.

2.20.s:
candanaṃ ca haridrā ca darbhamūlaṃ tathaiva ca..
kṛtvā kumbhe naraḥ snāyātkṛtvā piṣṭena kanyakām.. .. 82 ..
2.20.d:
चन्दनं च हरिद्रा च दर्भमूलं तथैव च॥
कृत्वा कुम्भे नरः स्नायात्कृत्वा पिष्टेन कन्यकाम्॥ ॥ 82 ॥
2.20.m: Having placed sandalwood, turmeric, and root of darbha-grass / in a jar, a man should bathe, having made a maiden of flour.

2.20.s:
snānālaṅkāravastrādyānpūṣṇe dadyādbaliṃ tataḥ ..
madhulājāstathaivātra dhūpaṃ dadyādghṛtena ca .. 83..
2.20.d:
स्नानालङ्कारवस्त्राद्यान्पूष्णे दद्याद्बलिं ततः ॥
मधुलाजास्तथैवात्र धूपं दद्याद्घृतेन च ॥ 83॥
2.20.m: After [presenting] bath, ornaments, garments, and so forth, he should give an offering to Pūṣan; / likewise honey and parched grains here, and he should offer incense with ghee.

2.20.s:
homaṃ ghṛtena kartavyaṃ dakṣiṇā kanakaṃ bhavet ..
brāhmīṃ suvarcalāṃ homaṃ homagarbho maṇirbhavet .. 84 ..
2.20.d:
होमं घृतेन कर्तव्यं दक्षिणा कनकं भवेत् ॥
ब्राह्मीं सुवर्चलां होमं होमगर्भो मणिर्भवेत् ॥ 84 ॥
2.20.m: An oblation into fire should be made with ghee, [and] the sacrificial fee should be gold. / An oblation with brāhmī and suvarcalā; the amulet should contain [ashes of] the oblation.

2.20.s:
evaṃ pauṣṇe sadā snāto yaḥ sadā yujyate naraḥ ..
āśvine supradaṃ snānaṃ pūrvamuktaṃ mayā tava .. .. 85 ..
2.20.d:
एवं पौष्णे सदा स्नातो यः सदा युज्यते नरः ॥
आश्विने सुप्रदं स्नानं पूर्वमुक्तं मया तव ॥ ॥ 85 ॥
2.20.m: Thus bathed constantly under the star of Pūṣan, a man is always joined [with prosperity]. / The bath under the star of the Aśvins, bestowing beauty, was previously spoken by me to you.

2.20.s:
vaijayantīṃ balāṃ caiva samaṅgāṃ ca bhṛgūttama ..
indrahastāṃ madhūkaṃ ca kuryādrāma ghaṭatraye .. 86 ..
2.20.d:
वैजयन्तीं बलां चैव समङ्गां च भृगूत्तम ॥
इन्द्रहस्तां मधूकं च कुर्याद्राम घटत्रये ॥ 86 ॥
2.20.m: Vaijayantī, balā, and samaṅgā, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / indrahastā, and madhūka, he should place in three jars, O Rāma.

2.20.s:
tena snāto yamāyātha prapadyāttilataṇḍulam ..
mālyāni caiva citrāṇi pītāni vasanāni ca .. 87 ..
2.20.d:
तेन स्नातो यमायाथ प्रपद्यात्तिलतण्डुलम् ॥
माल्यानि चैव चित्राणि पीतानि वसनानि च ॥ 87 ॥
2.20.m: Bathed with that, he should then offer sesame and rice to Yama, / and variegated garlands and yellow garments,

2.20.s:
urabhraśṛṅgaṃ dhūpārthe homārthe ca tathā tilam ..
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā tilaṃ kanakameva ca .. 88 ..
2.20.d:
उरभ्रशृङ्गं धूपार्थे होमार्थे च तथा तिलम् ॥
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या तिलं कनकमेव च ॥ 88 ॥
2.20.m: a ram's horn for the purpose of incense, and likewise sesame for the purpose of the fire-oblation. / And the sacrificial fee to be given here is sesame and gold.

2.20.s:
darbhamūlairmaṇiḥ kāryaḥ kanakena ca veṣṭitaḥ ..
evaṃ snāto naro yāmye dīrghaṃ jīvitamāpnuyāt .. 89 ..
2.20.d:
दर्भमूलैर्मणिः कार्यः कनकेन च वेष्टितः ॥
एवं स्नातो नरो याम्ये दीर्घं जीवितमाप्नुयात् ॥ 89 ॥
2.20.m: An amulet should be made with roots of darbha-grass and wrapped with gold. / Bathed thus under the star of Yama, a man attains a long life.

2.20.s:
snānāni mukhyāni tavoditāni kāmyāni pāpapraśamāya rāma ..
etāni kāryāṇi sadā dvijendra dharānvitenātha vicakṣaṇena ..2.99.90..
2.100
puṣkara uvāca ..
upoṣya cottarāṣāḍhāṃ brahmasnānaṃ vidhīyate ..
sūrye madhyamanuprāpte narendro - - - ..
sarvairbījaistathā ratnaiḥ phalaiḥ puṣpaistathauṣadhaiḥ ..
snātaśca sodakaiḥ kuryāttataḥ pūjāṃ svayaṃbhuvaḥ .. 2 ..
dhūpaṃ ca dadyāddharmajña kuśamūlaghṛtākṣataiḥ ..
homaṃ ghṛtākṣataiḥ kuryāddadyātkanakameva ca .. 3 ..
kriyamāṇe sruve cūrṇaṃ tathā caiva raṇo dvijaḥ ..
somaṃ cūrṇaṃ ca trivṛtaṃ maṇiṃ śirasi dhārayet .. 4 ..
snānaṃ tu rājyakāmasya proktametanmayā tava ..
brahmavarcasakāmasya svecchayā ca yathoditam .. 5 ..
brāhmaṃ tava snānamidaṃ pradiṣṭaṃ sarvādhināśāya bhṛgupradhāna ..
kāryaṃ sadā vā dinamadhyayāte divākare kāmakaraṃ praśastam .. 6 ..
2.20.d:
स्नानानि मुख्यानि तवोदितानि काम्यानि पापप्रशमाय राम ॥
एतानि कार्याणि सदा द्विजेन्द्र धरान्वितेनाथ विचक्षणेन ॥2.99.90॥
2.100
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
उपोष्य चोत्तराषाढां ब्रह्मस्नानं विधीयते ॥
सूर्ये मध्यमनुप्राप्ते नरेन्द्रो - - - ॥
सर्वैर्बीजैस्तथा रत्नैः फलैः पुष्पैस्तथौषधैः ॥
स्नातश्च सोदकैः कुर्यात्ततः पूजां स्वयंभुवः ॥ 2 ॥
धूपं च दद्याद्धर्मज्ञ कुशमूलघृताक्षतैः ॥
होमं घृताक्षतैः कुर्याद्दद्यात्कनकमेव च ॥ 3 ॥
क्रियमाणे स्रुवे चूर्णं तथा चैव रणो द्विजः ॥
सोमं चूर्णं च त्रिवृतं मणिं शिरसि धारयेत् ॥ 4 ॥
स्नानं तु राज्यकामस्य प्रोक्तमेतन्मया तव ॥
ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्य स्वेच्छया च यथोदितम् ॥ 5 ॥
ब्राह्मं तव स्नानमिदं प्रदिष्टं सर्वाधिनाशाय भृगुप्रधान ॥
कार्यं सदा वा दिनमध्ययाते दिवाकरे कामकरं प्रशस्तम् ॥ 6 ॥
2.20.m:
The principal optional baths for the pacification of sins have been spoken to you, O Rāma. / These should always be performed, O chief of the twice-born, by a discerning man accompanied by dharma.
2.100 / Puṣkara said: / Having fasted under Uttarāṣāḍhā, the bath to Brahmā is prescribed. / When the sun has reached the middle, the king […] / and bathed with water containing all seeds, gems, fruits, flowers, and medicinal herbs, / he should then perform the worship of the Self-born.
He should also offer incense, O knower of dharma, with kuśa roots, ghee, and unbroken grains. / He should make an oblation into fire with ghee and unbroken grains, and give gold.
While the ladle is being made, powder […], and likewise […], O twice-born; / with soma powder and trivṛt, he should wear an amulet on his head.
This bath has been described by me to you for one who desires kingship, / and according to what was taught, at one's own pleasure, for one who desires brahmic splendor.
This bath of Brahmā has been ordained for you for the destruction of all mental distress, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / it should always be performed when the sun has reached midday, fulfilling desires and praiseworthy.

पुष्कर उवाच ॥
जन्मनक्षत्रगे सोमे सर्वौषधिसमन्वितम् ॥
कुम्भं सुपूजितं कृत्वा स्नपनं तेन कारयेत् ॥ 1 ॥
स्नातश्चैवार्चयेद्देवं वासुदेवं जगत्पतिम् ॥
नक्षत्रदैवतं चन्द्रं नक्षत्रं वारुणं तथा ॥2॥

चन्द्ररूपी च भगवान्पिता विष्णुः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 6 ॥ ]
2.21.m:
A person who has bathed at the conjunction with the asterism of Śravaṇa always attains desired wishes; / he abandons all sin, O Rāma, and attains dharma and preeminent fame.
Puṣkara said: / When the moon is in one's birth asterism, one should prepare a well-worshiped pitcher / filled with all medicinal herbs, and have the bath performed with it.
Having bathed, one should worship the god Vāsudeva, the lord of the universe, / the deity of the asterism, the moon, and likewise the asterism sacred to Varuṇa,
and one should worship Vāyu, the pedestal of weapons and so forth, as well as the parasol; / and one should offer clarified butter with mantras containing the marks of the deities as prescribed.
And a sacrificial fee should be given according to one's capacity to the brahmins, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / then anointed, fragrant, wearing garlands and adorned with various ornaments,
standing, O tiger among men, eating sacrificial food, with senses subdued— / even without fasting, this is purifying and destroys sin.
The birth star is prescribed in the position of the mother of the worlds, / and the blessed Viṣṇu, possessing the form of the moon, is proclaimed as the father.

2.21.m: Therefore, with every effort, one should worship with devotion that moon / situated in the natal asterism, and especially the birth asterism itself.

2.103
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
चन्द्रमंडलवृद्धौ तु तथा चैवोत्तरायणे ॥
शुभे दिवसनक्षत्रे मुहूर्ते च तथा शुभे ॥ 1 ॥
तिष्याश्विनगते चन्द्रे हस्तश्रवणगेऽपि च ॥
प्राचीं वाप्यथवोदीचीं निष्क्रम्य नगराद्दिशम् ॥ 2 ॥
वास्तुविद्याविनिर्दिष्टे भूमिभागे मनोहरे ॥
अष्टहस्तं शुभं कुर्याच्चतुरस्रं च मण्डलम् ॥ 3 ॥
बल्यर्थमपरं कुर्याद्वह्निवेद्यर्थमेव च ॥
गोमये नोपलिप्ते तु सुधालेखासमन्विते ॥ 4 ॥
ध्वजातपत्रव्यजनमाल्यदामकुशाक्षतैः ॥
लाजागन्धादिभिर्मुख्यैर्मङ्गल्यैस्तं समर्चयेत्॥5॥
लाजालाजोपकरणैस्तथैव च विभूषयेत् ॥
ततः प्रस्रवणेभ्यस्तु चतुर्भ्यस्तु घटान्नवान् ॥ 6 ॥
2.21.m:
Having always performed worship of the moon when situated in the birth asterism, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / a man attains all desires, and would always be happy on earth, with sins destroyed.
Puṣkara said: / During the waxing of the lunar orb, and also during the northern course of the sun, / on an auspicious lunar day and asterism, and at an auspicious muhūrta,
when the moon is in Tiṣya or Aśvinī, and also when it is in Hasta or Śravaṇa, / having gone out of the city toward either the east or the north direction,
on a delightful plot of ground specified by the lore of architecture, / one should make an auspicious, square sacred diagram measuring eight cubits.
One should make another for the bali offering, and one specifically for the fire-altar, / smeared with cow dung and furnished with lines of lime,
One should honor it with banners, parasols, fans, garlands, strings, kuśa grass, and unbroken grains, / with fried grain, scents, and other principal auspicious articles.
One should likewise adorn it with fried grain and utensils for parched grain; / then, indeed, the learned man should arrange new jars from four springs,

2.21.s:
pratyekaṃ kalpayedvidvānkalpite maṇḍaladvaye ..
sūktiṣvatha mahābhāga bījamātrasamanvitān .. 7 ..
tatastu kalpayetkumbhānsaptamukhyānnadījalaiḥ ..
sarvauṣadhiyutaḥ kāryaḥ kumbha eko dvijanmanā .. 8 ..

Then one should prepare seven principal pitchers with waters from rivers; / one pitcher should be prepared by the twice-born with all medicinal herbs,

2.21.s:
sarvabījayuto dhānyaratnopetastathā paraḥ ..
tathā caivāparaṃ yuktaṃ kāryaṃ vṛkṣāgrapallavaiḥ .. 9 ..

puṣpaiścaivāparaṃ yuktaṃ phalaiścaivāparaṃ tathā ..

pūrvamantreṇa ca tathā sarvānevābhimantrayet ..
tato bhadrāsanaṃ dattvā tatra carmāstared budhaḥ .. 11 ..

ततो भद्रासनं दत्त्वा तत्र चर्मास्तरेद् बुधः ॥ 11 ॥

2.21.s:
viprasya snātukāmasya sauramārṣabhakaṃ śubham ..
kṣattriyasya tathā saiṃhaṃ vaiyāghraṃ ca tathā viśaḥ..12..

विप्रस्य स्नातुकामस्य सौरमार्षभकं शुभम् ॥

2.21.m: An auspicious skin of an ox or bull is for a brahmin who desires to bathe, / a lion's skin for a kṣatriya, and a tiger's skin for a vaiśya,

2.21.s:

2.21.m: Having fasted, with head bathed using white mustard without a comb, / a learned brahmin should bathe [him] along with many brahmins,

2.21.s:
śaṅkhapuṇyāhaghoṣeṇa vīṇāveṇuraveṇa ca ..

शङ्खपुण्याहघोषेण वीणावेणुरवेण च ॥
जयशब्देन महता बन्दिनां निस्वनेन च ॥15॥
2.21.m: to the sound of conches and the proclamation of an auspicious day, the melody of lutes and flutes, / with the great cry of victory and the loud chanting of bards.

2.21.s:
sauvarṇaṃ ca śatacchidraṃ pātraṃ śirasi dhārayet ..
tatra dadyādghaṭaistoyaṃ krameṇānena śāstravit .. 16 ..

सौवर्णं च शतच्छिद्रं पात्रं शिरसि धारयेत् ॥
तत्र दद्याद्घटैस्तोयं क्रमेणानेन शास्त्रवित् ॥ 16 ॥
2.21.m: And one should place upon the head a golden vessel with a hundred holes; / there, he who knows the scriptures should pour water from the jars in this order:

2.21.s:
yā auṣadhaya ityeṣa mantraḥ syādauṣadhīghaṭe ..
ābrahman brahmaṇetyeṣa bījakumbhe prakīrtitaḥ .. 17 ..

आब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मणेत्येष बीजकुम्भे प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 17 ॥
2.21.m: The mantra 'yā auṣadhayaḥ' should be over the herbal jar; / 'ā brahman brāhmaṇaḥ' is prescribed over the seed-pitcher;

2.21.s:
āśuḥ śiśāna iti ca tathā ratnaghaṭe bhavet ..
mantraḥ puṣpavatītyeṣa puṣpakumbhe prakīrtitaḥ .. 18 ..
2.21.d:
आशुः शिशान इति च तथा रत्नघटे भवेत् ॥
मन्त्रः पुष्पवतीत्येष पुष्पकुम्भे प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 18 ॥
2.21.m: 'āśuḥ śiśānaḥ' should be used likewise over the gem-jar; / the mantra 'puṣpavatīḥ' is proclaimed over the flower-pitcher;

2.21.s:
eṣa eva tathā mantraḥ phalakumbhe prakīrtitaḥ ..
gandhadvāreṇa ca tathā gandhakumbhe vidhīyate .. 19 ..
2.21.d:
एष एव तथा मन्त्रः फलकुम्भे प्रकीर्तितः ॥
गन्धद्वारेण च तथा गन्धकुम्भे विधीयते ॥ 19 ॥
2.21.m: this same mantra is likewise proclaimed over the fruit-pitcher; / and with 'gandhadvārām' it is prescribed over the perfume-pitcher.

2.21.s:
evaṃ snātaḥ parīdhāya suśukle vāsasī śubhe ..
maṅgalyāni spṛśedrāma saṃpaśyedvadanaṃ ghṛte .. 2.103.20 ..
2.21.d:
एवं स्नातः परीधाय सुशुक्ले वाससी शुभे ॥
मङ्गल्यानि स्पृशेद्राम संपश्येद्वदनं घृते ॥ 2.103.20 ॥
2.21.m: Having thus bathed and put on two pure, white, auspicious garments, / he should touch auspicious things, O Rāma, and behold his face in clarified butter

2.21.s:
vimale ca tathādarśe tataḥ saṃpūjayeddharim ..
vaiṣṇavāṃśca tathā mantrāñjuhuyājjātavedasi .. 21 ..
2.21.d:
विमले च तथादर्शे ततः संपूजयेद्धरिम् ॥
वैष्णवांश्च तथा मन्त्राञ्जुहुयाज्जातवेदसि ॥ 21 ॥
2.21.m: and in a spotless mirror; then he should worship Hari, / and offer oblations with Vaiṣṇava mantras into the sacred fire.

2.21.s:
tatastūttaradigbhāge vahniṃ tasyopakalpayeta ..
bhadrāsanaṃ śubhe deśe yuktaṃ pūrvoktacarmaṇā .. 22 ..
2.21.d:
ततस्तूत्तरदिग्भागे वह्निं तस्योपकल्पयेत ॥
भद्रासनं शुभे देशे युक्तं पूर्वोक्तचर्मणा ॥ 22 ॥
2.21.m: Then in the northern region one should prepare a fire for him, / and an auspicious seat in a pure place, furnished with the previously mentioned skin.

2.21.s:
śvetānulepanaḥ sragvī maṅgalyābharaṇastathā ..
niviśetāsane tasminsabhāryo bhṛgunandana .. 23 ..
2.21.d:
श्वेतानुलेपनः स्रग्वी मङ्गल्याभरणस्तथा ॥
निविशेतासने तस्मिन्सभार्यो भृगुनन्दन ॥ 23 ॥
2.21.m: Anointed with white unguent, wearing a garland, and adorned with auspicious ornaments, / he should sit on that seat together with his wife, O scion of Bhṛgu.

2.21.s:
gandhadvāretimantreṇa tasya rocanayā tataḥ ..
kaṇṭhe mūrdhni tataḥ kuryāttilakaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ svayam .. 24 ..
2.21.d:
गन्धद्वारेतिमन्त्रेण तस्य रोचनया ततः ॥
कण्ठे मूर्ध्नि ततः कुर्यात्तिलकं ब्राह्मणः स्वयम् ॥ 24 ॥
2.21.m: With the mantra beginning with "gandhadvārā", using yellow pigment, / a brahmin himself should then make a tilaka on his neck and forehead.

2.21.s:
yena devā jyotiṣeti darbhārgrairbrāhmaṇastataḥ ..
pādatastu prabhṛtyenaṃ sarvāṅgeṣu pramārjayet .. 25 ..
2.21.d:
येन देवा ज्योतिषेति दर्भार्ग्रैर्ब्राह्मणस्ततः ॥
पादतस्तु प्रभृत्येनं सर्वाङ्गेषु प्रमार्जयेत् ॥ 25 ॥
2.21.m: Then, with the mantra "yena devā jyotiṣā", using tips of darbha grass, / the brahmin should wipe him all over his limbs, beginning from the feet.

2.21.s:
gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dadyādbrāhmaṇebhyaśca śaktitaḥ ..
gandharatnājyamālyāni kanakaṃ rajataṃ tathā .. 26 ..
2.21.d:
गुरवे दक्षिणां दद्याद्ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च शक्तितः ॥
गन्धरत्नाज्यमाल्यानि कनकं रजतं तथा ॥ 26 ॥
2.21.m: He should give a sacrificial fee to the preceptor and to the brahmins according to his ability: / perfumes, gems, ghee, garlands, gold, and silver.

2.21.s:
śatacchidraṃ ca tatpātraṃ gurave vinivedayet ..
maṅgalālambhanaṃ kṛtvā gatapāpo dvijāśiṣā..27..
2.21.d:
शतच्छिद्रं च तत्पात्रं गुरवे विनिवेदयेत् ॥
मङ्गलालम्भनं कृत्वा गतपापो द्विजाशिषा॥27॥
2.21.m: He should present that vessel with a hundred holes to the preceptor; / having touched auspicious items, freed from evil through the benediction of the twice-born,

2.21.s:
śaṅkhapuṇyāhaghoṣeṇa praviśecca gṛhaṃ svakam ..
vināpi bhāryayā rāma snānaṃ kāryamidaṃ tathā ..28..
2.21.d:
शङ्खपुण्याहघोषेण प्रविशेच्च गृहं स्वकम् ॥
विनापि भार्यया राम स्नानं कार्यमिदं तथा ॥28॥
2.21.m: he should enter his own house to the sound of conches and "Auspicious Day!". / This bath may also be performed without a wife, O Rāma.

2.21.s:
saptarātramidaṃ snānaṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśanam ..
madhu māṃsaṃ tathā kṣaudraṃ maithunaṃ ca vivarjayet ..29..
2.21.d:
सप्तरात्रमिदं स्नानं सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥
मधु मांसं तथा क्षौद्रं मैथुनं च विवर्जयेत् ॥29॥
2.21.m: This seven-night bath destroys all defilements. / One should avoid honey, meat, wild honey, and sexual intercourse.

2.21.s:
alakṣmīśamanaṃ puṇyaṃ rakṣoghnaṃ buddhivardhanam ..
ārogyadaṃ dīptikaraṃ yaśasyaṃ śatrusūdanam .. 2.103.30 ..
2.21.d:
अलक्ष्मीशमनं पुण्यं रक्षोघ्नं बुद्धिवर्धनम् ॥
आरोग्यदं दीप्तिकरं यशस्यं शत्रुसूदनम् ॥ 2.103.30 ॥
2.21.m: It dispels misfortune, is meritorious, slays demons, and increases intelligence; / it grants health, creates radiance, brings fame, and slays enemies.

2.21.s:
maṅgalyaṃ pāpaśamanaṃ kalidusvapnanāśanam ..
bṛhaspatiridaṃ cakre snānaṃ maghavataḥ svayam ..
brahmahatyābhibhūtasya vṛtte vṛtravadhe purā ..31..
2.21.d:
मङ्गल्यं पापशमनं कलिदुस्वप्ननाशनम् ॥
बृहस्पतिरिदं चक्रे स्नानं मघवतः स्वयम् ॥
ब्रह्महत्याभिभूतस्य वृत्ते वृत्रवधे पुरा ॥31॥
2.21.m: It is auspicious, dispels sin, and destroys the Kali age and bad dreams. / Bṛhaspati himself performed this bath for Maghavat / long ago, when he was overcome by the murder of a brahmin after the slaying of Vṛtra had occurred.

2.21.s:
tato'sya dattaḥ svayameva vajriṇā varo nṛlokepi varo'sya kārakaḥ ..
kāmānabhīṣṭānsamavāpya pūjito mahendralokaṃ sa sukhī prayāsyati .. 32 ..
2.21.d:
ततोऽस्य दत्तः स्वयमेव वज्रिणा वरो नृलोकेपि वरोऽस्य कारकः ॥
कामानभीष्टान्समवाप्य पूजितो महेन्द्रलोकं स सुखी प्रयास्यति ॥ 32 ॥
2.21.m: Then a boon was indeed granted to him by the Wielder of the Thunderbolt himself: even in the world of men, a performer of this [bath] will be a giver of boons; / having attained his desired wishes and been venerated, he will go happily to the world of Mahendra.

राम उवाच ॥
स्नानमन्यत्समाचक्ष्व भगवन्दुरितापहम् ॥
सकृदेव कृतं यत्तु पापेभ्यो विप्रमोचयेत् ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
राजयक्ष्माभिभूतेषु विषमज्वरितेषु च ॥

गर्भः प्रस्रवते यस्या जातो वापि विनश्यति ॥
पुष्पं यस्याः क्षयं याति न च किञ्चित्प्रजायते ॥ 6 ॥

2.21.s:
gṛhṇāti yā na bījaṃ ca janayedvāpyamānuṣān ..
nāpnoti ca patiṃ kanyā tasmātsnehamathāpi vā .. 7 ..

evamukteṣu cānyeṣu tvanukteṣu ca bhārgava .. 8 ..

snāpayetsaritastīre grahāviṣṭānvicakṣaṇaḥ .. 9 ..

kāntāre vā vane tīrthe teṣāṃ snānaṃ praśasyate .. 14 ..
2.21.d:
गृह्णाति या न बीजं च जनयेद्वाप्यमानुषान् ॥
नाप्नोति च पतिं कन्या तस्मात्स्नेहमथापि वा ॥ 7 ॥
सौभाग्यं च न चायाति सुहृत्स्वजनबन्धुषु ॥
एवमुक्तेषु चान्येषु त्वनुक्तेषु च भार्गव ॥ 8 ॥
प्रसमीक्ष्य विधानज्ञः स्नानमेतत्समाचरेत् ॥
स्नापयेत्सरितस्तीरे ग्रहाविष्टान्विचक्षणः ॥ 9 ॥
राजयक्ष्माभिभूता ये विषम ज्वरिताश्च ये ॥
तेषां देवालये स्नानं कुर्याद्वा सिद्धसेविते ॥ 2.104.10 ॥
छायोन्मादोपतप्ता ये ये चापस्मारशोषिणः ॥
तेषां मुनिगणावासे तीर्थे वा स्नानमिष्यते ॥ 11 ॥
विनायकग्रहार्ता ये ये च मूढा विचेतसः ॥
सज्जनाचरिते देशे तेषां स्नानं विधीयते ॥ 12 ॥
त्रैविद्या येन सिध्यन्ति गुणा येषां प्रपूजिताः ॥
तेषां स्नानमिहोद्दिष्टं सिद्धदेवस्य मन्दिरे ॥ 13 ॥
येषां नास्ति जयो युद्धे येषां स्वजनसंक्षयः ॥
कान्तारे वा वने तीर्थे तेषां स्नानं प्रशस्यते ॥ 14 ॥
2.21.m:
she who does not receive seed, or gives birth to non-humans; / or the maiden who does not obtain a husband, or love from him;
and who attains no good fortune among friends, kin, and relatives— / for these mentioned and others not mentioned, O descendant of Bhṛgu,
the expert who knows the ritual, having considered [their case], should perform this bath. / The wise man should bathe those possessed by planets on a riverbank.
For those afflicted by consumption and those with malarial fever, / he should perform the bath in a temple of God or in a place frequented by the perfected.
For those tormented by shadow-madness and those wasting from epilepsy, / bathing is prescribed at a hermitage of sages or at a sacred bathing place.
For those afflicted by the seizure of Vināyaka and those who are deluded and out of their minds, / bathing is prescribed in a place frequented by virtuous people.
For those who do not master the triple knowledge, whose virtues are revered, / bathing is prescribed here in a temple of a perfected god.
For those who have no victory in battle, and those whose kin are dying out, / bathing is commended in a wilderness, in a forest, or at a sacred bathing place.

2.21.d:
सततं कलहो येषां जायते च यतस्ततः ॥
त्रिपथे वा तडागे वा स्नानं तेषां प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 15 ॥
पद्मिन्यां स्नपयेन्नारीं गर्भो यस्याः स्रवेत्तथा ॥
अशोकसन्निधौ स्नाप्या जातो यस्याः विनश्यति ॥ 16 ॥
न च गृह्णाति या शुक्रं स्नाप्या सा सफले तरौ ॥
महोदधितटे स्नाप्या यदापत्यं विनश्यति ॥ 17 ॥
अमानुषान्या जनयेत्स्नापयेत्तां चतुष्पथे ॥
यादृशं या च भर्तारं न लभेत वराङ्गना ॥ 18 ॥
स्नापयेदेकलिङ्गे तां स्थाने वा वृक्षसंकुले ॥
रूपलावण्ययुक्ता या सौभाग्यं या न विन्दति ॥ 19 ॥
स्नानं वृद्धिकरं तस्या वेश्यागारे प्रकल्पयेत्॥
अन्येषामथ कर्तव्यं सदा स्नानं मनोहरम्॥2.104.20॥
समे सज्जनसंकीर्णे शुचौ देशे विकण्टके॥
सहायैः प्रयतैः सार्धमहोरात्रोषितो द्विजः॥21॥
स्नानकर्म प्रयुञ्जीत सोपवासस्य मानद॥
अहोरात्रासमर्थस्य कार्यं वा हविषाशनम्॥22॥
2.21.m:
For those between whom constant quarrel arises everywhere, / one should arrange the bath at a crossroads of three paths or at a pool.
One should bathe a woman whose fetus miscarries in a lotus pond; / she whose child dies as soon as born should be bathed near an aśoka tree.
She who does not conceive semen should be bathed near a fruit-bearing tree; / she whose offspring perishes should be bathed on the shore of the ocean.
She who gives birth to non-humans should be bathed at a four-way crossroads; / and the excellent woman who cannot obtain a husband suited to her
should be bathed at a solitary liṅga or in a place dense with trees. / For a woman endowed with beauty and charm who finds no good fortune,
one should arrange a bath that increases it in a courtesan's house. / Then for others, an attractive bath should always be performed
in an even, clean, thornless place crowded with virtuous people. / Along with restrained assistants, a twice-born, having fasted for a day and night,
should employ the rite of bathing for one who is fasting, O giver of honor; / or for one unable to fast for a day and night, eating sacrificial food is to be observed.

2.21.d:
शरद्वसन्तयोः कार्यं स्नानं स्वस्थस्य भार्गव ॥
सर्वकालेष्वथार्त्तस्य ग्रहव्याधिनिबर्हणम् ॥ 23 ॥
मुहूर्ते तत्र सावित्रे ब्राह्मणः स्नापयेद्द्विज ॥
मैत्रेऽथ विजये चैव राजन्यं स्नापयेत्तथा ॥ 24 ॥
वैश्यं पैतामहे शूद्रं शेषेषु स्नापयेत्तथा ॥
पञ्चमी सप्तमी श्रेष्ठा स्नपने ब्राह्मणस्य व ॥ 25 ॥
त्रयोदशी तृतीया च क्षत्त्रियस्य विशिष्यते ॥
द्वितीया दशमी चैव तथा वैश्यस्य मानद ॥ 26 ॥
षष्ठी चतुर्दशी चैव शूद्राणां स्नानकर्मणि ॥
एकादशी द्वादशी च तथा कृष्णचतुर्दशी ॥ 27 ॥
सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां स्नानकर्मणि पूजिता ॥
ध्रुवेषु वैष्णवे पुष्ये रेवत्यां भगदैवते ॥ 28 ॥
हस्ते पुनर्वसौ सौम्ये ज्येष्ठायामथ वारुणे ॥
धनिष्ठायां तथा स्नानं सर्वेषामेव पूजितम् ॥ 29 ॥

2.21.d:
वेत्रासनं भद्रपीठं वैदलं दारवं तथा ॥
वर्णानामानुपूर्व्येण परिकीर्तितमासनम् ॥ 2.104.30॥
कृष्णाजिनं च वैयाघ्रं रौरवं बास्तमेव च ॥
पादोपधानं वर्णानामानुपूर्व्येण कल्पयेत ॥ 31 ॥
वृषाश्वरथ पृष्ठे च गजपृष्ठे तथैव च ॥ ॥
नरस्कन्धेङ्गनाङ्गे वा प्रायशः स्नापयेच्छिशून् ॥ 32 ॥
स्नातुकामस्य तस्याथ पूर्वमुत्सारसः स्मृतम् ॥
यैर्द्रव्यैर्भृगुशार्दूल तानि वक्ष्याम्यतः परम् ॥ 33 ॥
पुनर्नवां रोचनां च शताह्वागुरुणीं त्वचम् ॥
मधूकं च रजन्यौ द्वे तगरं नागकेसरम् ॥ 34 ॥
आसुरीं सर्जिकां चैव मांसीं रामठ चन्दनम् ॥
प्रियङ्गुं सर्षपान्कुष्ठं कुंकुमं बहुपुत्रिकाम् ॥ 35 ॥
बलेन्द्रहस्तीं ब्राह्मीं च पञ्चगव्यं तथैव च ॥
सक्तुना मिश्रयित्वा च कार्यमुद्वर्तनं भवेत् ॥ 36॥
2.21.m:
A cane seat, an auspicious stool, a wicker seat, and a wooden seat / are proclaimed as the seat for the castes in regular order.
A black antelope skin, a tiger skin, a ruru deer skin, and a goat skin / should be arranged as the footstool for the castes in regular order.
Upon the back of a bull, a horse, a chariot, and likewise on the back of an elephant, / or on a man's shoulder or in a woman's lap, one should generally bathe children.
For him who desires to bathe, anointing is prescribed beforehand; / I shall declare next, O tiger of the Bhṛgus, the substances with which it is to be done:
Punarnavā, rocanā, śatāhvā, aguru, and cinnamon bark, / madhūka, the two turmerics, tagara, nāgakesara,
āsurī, sarjikā, māṃsī, asafoetida, and sandalwood, / priyaṅgu, mustard seeds, kuṣṭha, saffron, and bahuputrikā,
balā, indrahastī, and brāhmī, and likewise the five products of the cow; / mixing these with barley-meal, an unguent should be made.

2.21.d:
ततः स्नानदिने प्राप्ते प्राग्वदुत्सादयेत्पुनः ॥
ततो मनोहरे देशे मण्डलं कल्पयेद् बुधः ॥37 ॥
चतुरस्रं गोमयेन सर्वतोऽष्टदिशं समम् ॥
सतोरणं चतुर्द्वारं प्राकारैरुपशोभितम् ॥ 38 ॥
तत्र मध्ये लिखेत्पद्ममष्टपत्रं सुशोभितम् ॥
कर्णिकायां लिखेद्विष्णुं मेघाभं पीतवाससम् ॥39॥
कौस्तुभोद्भासितोरस्कं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम्॥
ब्रह्माणं दक्षिणे न्यस्य पद्मवर्णं समालिखेत् ॥ 2.104.40॥
अजिनाम्बरसंयुक्तं श्वेतयज्ञोपवीतिनम् ॥
रजताभ्रनिभं वामे भागे रुद्रं समालिखेत् ॥ 41 ॥
व्याघ्रचर्माम्बरधरं त्रिनेत्रं शूलधारिणम् ॥
पूर्वपत्रे लिखेच्छक्रं सवज्रं च सुदर्शनम् ॥ 42 ॥
गजपृष्ठाधिरूढं तु स्वर्णाभं पीतवाससम् ॥
प्राग्दक्षिणे तथा पत्रे लिखेद्वह्निं महाप्रभम् ॥ 43 ॥
2.21.m:
Then, when the day of the bath arrives, he should rub [him] again as before; / thereafter, in a delightful place, the wise man should fashion a sacred diagram,
square, [smeared] with cow-dung, equal on all eight directions, / having arches, four gateways, and adorned with enclosing walls.
There in the middle he should draw a beautiful eight-petalled lotus; / on the pericarp he should draw Viṣṇu, cloud-hued and dressed in yellow garments,
his chest illuminated by the Kaustubha, bearing the conch, discus, and mace; / having placed Brahmā to the right, he should draw him with the color of a lotus,
accompanied by an antelope-skin garment, wearing a white sacred thread; / in the left part he should draw Rudra, resembling a silver cloud,
wearing a tiger-skin garment, three-eyed, and bearing a trident; / on the eastern petal he should draw Śakra, handsome and holding a thunderbolt,
mounted upon the back of an elephant, golden-hued, and wearing yellow garments; / on the south-eastern petal he should draw Fire of great splendor,

2.21.d:
धूमाभवसनं देवं शुकयानगतं प्रभुम् ॥
अतसीपुष्पसंकाशं पीताम्बरधरं शुभम् ॥ 44 ॥
सदण्डं महिषारूढं लिखेत्पत्रे तु दक्षिणे ॥
उष्ट्रारूढं विरूपाक्षं लिखेद्दक्षिणपश्चिमे ॥ 45 ॥
रक्ताम्बरधरं कृष्णं खड्गपाणिं विभीषणम् ॥
पश्चिमे वरुणं देवं सपाशं हंसवाहनम् ॥ 46 ॥
सशुक्लवसनं देवं स्वच्छवैडूर्यसन्निभम् ॥
पश्चिमोत्तरतो वायुं वायुमण्डलमध्यगम् ॥ 47 ॥
लिखेच्छुभ्राम्बरं श्वेतं सर्वाभरणभूषितम् ॥
कुबेरमुत्तरे पत्रे व्योमयानगतं लिखेत् ॥ 48 ॥
कवचोत्तमसंयुक्तं गदिनं कमलप्रभम् ॥
वृषारूढमथेशानं पत्रे पूर्वोत्तरे लिखेत् ॥49॥
व्याघ्रचर्माम्बरधरं भालचन्द्र विभूषितम् ॥
चतुर्भिः सागरैः पद्मं चतुरस्रं समन्ततः ॥ 2.104.50 ॥

2.21.d:
यादोगणयुतैश्चैव क्रमेण परिवारयेत् ॥
सागराणां तु पूर्वेण लिखेत्पद्मं मनोहरम् ॥ 51 ॥
ततश्चक्रं तथा दण्डं वज्रं मकरमेव च ॥
शक्तिं ध्वजं त्रिशूलं तु क्रमेणैव तु विन्यसेत् ॥ 52 ॥
ततः प्राकारसंलग्नानिषून्द्वादश विन्यसेत् ॥
चतुरः सूक्तिषु तथा द्वारेष्वष्टौ भृगूत्तम ॥ 53 ॥
सुसंहतान्समाञ्श्लक्ष्णान्दुरङ्गान्पत्रनिर्गतान् ॥
व्यामार्धसम्मितांस्तीक्ष्णान्पार्श्वे तक्षविभूषितान् ॥ 94 ॥
पञ्चरङ्गं ततः सूत्रं बध्नीयात्तेषु भार्गव ॥
अरुन्धन्द्वारमार्गांस्तु सुदृढं सुमनोहरम् ॥ 55 ॥
वितानं मण्डलीकुर्याच्छ्वेतवर्णं मनोहरम् ॥
ध्वजं छत्राणि खड्गांश्च घण्टादर्शांश्चतुर्दिशम् ॥ 56 ॥
प्राकारोपरि दण्डेषु सुदृढेष्वनिरोधयेत्॥
स्नाने मण्डलकान्कुर्यात्प्राकारस्य ततो बहिः ॥ 57 ॥
2.21.m:
filled with hosts of aquatic creatures, he should surround it in order; / to the east of the oceans he should draw a charming lotus.
Then the discus, the staff, the thunderbolt, and the makara, / the spear, the banner, and the trident he should place in sequence.
Then, attached to the wall, he should set twelve arrows: / four at the corners and eight at the gates, O foremost of the Bhṛgus,
well-formed, smooth, polished, fitted with feathers, / measuring half a fathom, sharp, decorated on the side by an artisan.
Then, O descendant of Bhṛgu, he should bind a five-colored thread to them, / firmly and very pleasantly, without blocking the paths of the doorways.
He should arrange a charming white canopy as a circular pavilion; / a banner, umbrellas, swords, bells, and mirrors in the four directions,
he should fasten firmly onto poles above the wall without obstruction; / outside the wall he should then make small circles for bathing,

2.21.d:
त्रिसमान्भृगुशार्दूल चतुरस्रान्मनोहरान् ॥
ज्वालामाल्यार्घरचितान्दिशासु विदिशासु च ॥ 58 ॥
स्नानमण्डलकानां तु समीपे सुसमन्ततः ॥
गावः सवत्साः संस्थाप्या वृषभाश्च सुपूजिताः ॥ 59 ॥
अजाश्चार्भकसम्पन्ना जीवमोक्षाश्च पक्षिणः ॥
प्राकारस्योत्तरे भागे वेदिं कुर्यात्सुशोभिताम् ॥ 2.104.60 ॥
दर्भैराच्छाद्य तान्सर्वान्सलिलेन समुक्षयेत् ॥
तत्राग्निं जुहुयान्मन्त्रैर्महाव्याहृतिपूर्वकम् ॥ 61 ॥
यथोक्तदेवतालिंगैस्तथा मन्त्रैश्च भार्गव ॥
ओंकारेण तथास्त्राणां नामयुक्तेन वै पृथक् ॥ 62 ॥
अश्वत्थोदुम्बरप्लक्षबिल्वार्कखदिराः शमी ॥
स्वराह्वयमपामार्गं पलाशयवकान्यपि ॥ 63 ॥
वंशिका चाश्वगन्धा च कदम्बश्चार्जुनासनौ ॥
एतेषां समिधः शस्ताः किष्कुमात्रा घृतप्लुताः ॥ 64 ॥
एकैकमप्यष्टशतं हव्यं सर्षपसंयुतम् ॥
तिलान्यवांस्तथाक्षोटाम्̐ल्लाजाश्चाग्नौ समावपेत् ॥ 65॥
2.21.m:
three equal, square, charming ones, O tiger of the Bhṛgus, / decorated with garlands of flames and respectful offerings in the directions and intermediate directions.
All around, in the vicinity of the bathing circles, / cows with their calves and well-worshipped bulls should be stationed,
and goats accompanied by kids, and birds set free alive; / in the northern part of the wall he should make a well-adorned altar.
Covering all of them with darbha grass, he should sprinkle them with water; / there he should sacrifice into the fire with mantras preceded by the Great Utterances,
with mantras containing the marks of the deities as prescribed, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / and separately with the syllable Om joined with the names of the weapons.
Aśvattha, udumbara, plakṣa, bilva, arka, khadira, śamī, / apāmārga, palāśa, and yavaka,
vaṃśikā, aśvagandhā, kadamba, arjuna, and asana: / firewood of these measuring a span and soaked in clarified butter is recommended.
One hundred and eight offerings of each, accompanied by mustard seeds; / he should cast sesame, barley, walnuts, and parched grain into the fire.

2.21.d:
ततश्चावपयेच्छान्तिं ब्राह्मणान्गुणसंयुतान् ॥
अभ्यर्च्य दक्षिणाभिश्च पुष्पाक्षतफलैस्तथा ॥66॥
ततस्तु स्थापयेत्कुम्भान्मण्डले सागरोपरि ॥
यथा दिग्देवनामाङ्कान्दिशासु विदिशासु च ॥ 67 ॥।
काञ्चनान्राजतांस्ताम्रानथ वापि महीमयान् ॥
नामान्यथैषां वक्ष्यामि तानि मे गदतः शृणु ॥ 68 ॥
भद्रः सुभद्रः सिद्धार्थश्चतुर्थः पुष्टिवर्धनः ॥
अमोकश्चित्रभानुश्च पर्जन्योऽथ सुदर्शनः ॥69 ॥
वापीकूपसरिद्भ्यश्च पूजयित्वा जलेन तान् ॥
वनस्पतिसमायुक्तानर्घ्यमाल्यादिपूजितान्॥2.104.70॥
मन्त्रानुमन्त्रितानेतांस्तत्र मन्त्रं निबोध मे ॥
स्थापयन्तु घटानेतान्साश्विरुद्रमरुद्गणाः ॥ 71॥
विश्वेदेवास्तथादित्या वसवो मुनयस्तथा ॥
अधिश्रयन्तु सुप्रीतास्तथान्या अपि देवताः ॥72॥
एवं संस्थाप्य तान्कुम्भान्स्थाप्या मण्डलकेष्वथ॥
ऐन्द्रादिक्रमशः स्थाप्यास्त्वासने पूर्वचोदिते ॥ 73॥
2.21.m:
Then he should have peace rites recited by virtuous brahmins, / having worshipped them with sacrificial fees, flowers, unbroken rice, and fruits.
Then he should place jars in the sacred diagram above the oceans, / marked with the names of the directional deities in the directions and intermediate directions,
made of gold, silver, copper, or earthen; / I shall now declare their names; listen to them as I speak:
Bhadra, Subhadra, Siddhārtha, and the fourth Puṣṭivardhana, / Amogha, Citrabhānu, Parjanya, and Sudarśana.
Having filled them with water from tanks, wells, and rivers, / furnished with herbs and worshipped with respectful offerings, garlands, and so on,
consecrated with mantras—hear from me the mantra for that: / 'May the hosts of the Rudras and Maruts, together with the Aśvins, establish these jars;
likewise, may the Viśvedevas, the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the sages, / well-pleased, abide [here], and so also the other deities.'
Having thus established those jars, they should then be placed in the circles; / they should be set sequentially beginning with Indra's [direction] on the seats prescribed earlier.

2.21.d:
पूर्वे मण्डलके स्थाप्यः शुक्लपुष्पान्वरान्वितः ॥
सर्वत्र ग्राहयेद्विप्रैर्वक्ष्यमाणगुणान्घटान् ॥ 74 ॥
प्रत्येकं स्याच्चतुर्भिस्तु द्वारस्योपरि भार्गव ॥
अपां पूर्णं घटं तत्र यथाशं च यथास्वकम् ॥ 75 ॥
तथा दद्याद्यथास्नानं सम्यक्स्नाप्यस्य जायते ॥
ओषधीश्चात्र वक्ष्यामि यास्तु कुम्भेषु निक्षिपेत् ॥ 76 ॥
अस्थापितेषु धर्मज्ञ ततः संस्थापनं भवेत् ॥
जयां जयन्तीं विजयां सूकरीं मर्कटीं वचाम्॥ 77 ॥
कायस्थां च वयस्थां च बृहतीं बहुपुत्रिकाम् ॥
सहस्तशतवीर्ये च त्रायमाणां कटुम्बराम् ॥ 78 ॥
अतिच्छत्रां तथा च्छत्रां जीवन्तीमपराजिताम् ॥
जटिलां पूतनां कीशां सुरां यक्षसुरां तथा ॥ 79 ॥
अवीतराक्षसीं वीरां स्थिरां भद्रां यशोबलाम् ॥
शङ्खपुष्पीं विष्णुदत्तां नाकुलीं गन्धनाकुलीम् ॥ 2.104.80 ॥
2.21.m:
In the eastern circle should be placed [a jar] adorned with white flowers and garments; / everywhere he should have the priests hold the jars possessing the qualities to be declared.
There should be four for each [person], O descendant of Bhṛgu, above the door; / a jar full of water there, according to portion and appropriately,
he should provide so that the bath of the person being bathed is properly effected; / and here I shall declare the medicinal herbs that one should cast into the jars.
When they are not yet installed, O knower of dharma, their installation should then take place:
jayā, jayantī, vijayā, sūkarī, markaṭī, vacā,
kāyasthā, vayasthā, bṛhatī, bahuputrikā,
sahasravīryā, śatavīryā, trāyamāṇā, kaṭumbarā,
aticchatrā, likewise chatrā, jīvantī, aparājitā,
jaṭilā, pūtanā, kīśā, surā, as well as yakṣasurā,
avītā, rākṣasī, vīrā, sthirā, bhadrā, yaśobalā,
śaṅkhapuṣpī, viṣṇudattā, nākulī, gandhanākulī,

गोलोम्यतिबले चैव व्याघ्रीमश्ववतीं तथा ॥
श्यामां ज्योतिष्मतीं चैव तेषु कुम्भेषु निक्षिपेत् ॥ 81 ॥
चन्दनोशीरतगरकुम्भमागुरुकेसरान्॥

कस्तूरिकां तरुष्कं च कर्पूरं नाडिकं तथा ॥
जातीफलं लवङ्गाश्च कक्कोलैः सह चूर्णिताः ॥ 84 ॥
गन्धद्रव्याणि चान्यानि यथालाभं विनिक्षिपेत् ॥
श्वेता रक्ता तथा पीता कृष्णा चैव हि मृत्तिका ॥ 85 ॥
याश्चान्या विविधाः शस्ता मृत्तिकास्ता निबोध मे ॥
वृषाग्रशृङ्गाद्वल्मीकाद्देवतायतनाद्व्रजात् ॥ 86 ॥
अग्न्यागाराद्धस्तिदन्तात्सुभगागणिकागृहात् ॥

कुम्भकारगृहान्नद्याः पद्मिन्याः श्रोत्रियालयात् ॥

golomī, atibalā, vyāghrī, as well as aśvavatī,

nutmeg, and cloves powdered together with kakkola fruits,

and the other various kinds of earth praised [for the rite]—hear them from me:
from the tip of a bull's horn, an anthill, a temple of a deity, a cowpen,
a fire-sanctuary, an elephant's tusk, the house of a fortunate courtesan,
the king's gate, the city gate, a well, and a charitable hall,
a potter's house, a river, a lotus pond, the dwelling of a śrotriya,
an indranīla pool, a deep lake, and a mountain spring,

चतुष्पथात्सप्तपथान्मृत्तिकाशकटात्तथा ॥
गजाश्वगणशालाभ्यस्तथाथर्वणवेश्मनः ॥ 89 ॥
अजाविकान्वितागाराद्राजकोशान्महासनात् ॥
अशोकात्क्षीरवृक्षाणां समीपात्सफलस्य च ॥ 2.104.90 ॥
सदाध्ययनशालातो यज्ञभूमेश्च मृत्तिकाः ॥
प्रगृह्य सर्वाः सम्भृत्य पञ्चगव्यसमन्विताः ॥ ॥ 91 ॥
सर्वबीजैः समायोज्य स्नानकुम्भेषु निक्षिपेत् ॥
ततः कुम्भान्प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्नाप्यं संस्थापयेद्द्विजः ॥ 92 ॥
मण्डलेषु क्रमेणैव दिशासु विदिशासु च ॥
पूर्वे मण्डलके स्नाप्यः श्वेतमाल्यानुलेपनः ॥ 93 ॥
श्वेतश्चैव पटो धार्यश्चतुर्भिर्ब्राह्मणैर्भवेत् ॥
एवं दक्षिणतस्तस्य सर्वं नीलं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 94 ॥
कृष्णं च कल्पयेत्सर्वं तथा दक्षिणपश्चिमे ॥
( पीतं प्रकल्पयेत्सर्वं तथा भागे तु पश्चिमे ॥)
पश्चिमोत्तरयोः सर्वं शुक्लवर्णं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 95 ॥
2.21.m:
a crossroads, a junction of seven roads, an earth-cart,
the stables of elephants and horses, and the house of an Ātharvaṇa priest,
a shed containing goats and sheep, the royal treasury, a royal throne,
an aśoka tree, from the vicinity of milky trees, and from a fruit-bearing tree,
from a school for constant recitation [of the Veda], and from the sacrificial ground—
taking all these soils, gathering them together, combined with the five products of the cow,
joined with all seeds, one should cast them into the bath jars.
Then, having consecrated the jars, the twice-born should place the person to be bathed
successively upon the maṇḍalas in the cardinal and intermediate directions.
In the eastern maṇḍala the one to be bathed should wear white garlands and unguent,
and a white cloth should be held over him by four brahmins.
Likewise, to his south, one should prepare everything in blue;
and one should prepare everything in black in the southwest;
(one should prepare everything in yellow in the western region;)
and in the northwest one should prepare everything in a white color;

2.21.m:
likewise in the northern direction one should prepare lotus color;
and in the northeast direction one should prepare everything multicolored.
The mantra prescribed for the royal consecration is prescribed here
for each of the jars in the cardinal and intermediate directions.
Thus he should be bathed, O fortunate one, amid the sounds of conches and auspicious chants.
Having bathed, clad in white garments, adorned with white garlands and unguent,
he should then, composed, perform the worship of the gods
seated in the maṇḍala, [attaining] purity with an abundance of perfume, garlands, and arghya,
with lamps, incenses, prostrations, garments, and ornaments.
He should offer cakes, milk-rice, edible treats, white garlands and unguent,
and various fruits and milk to the brahmins.
With curd, supreme food, white garlands, and unguents,
and with fruits and flowers, he should present a bali to Keśava.
With milk, supreme food, curd, and seasoned rice-and-sesame,
