apūpaiḥ paramānnena bhakṣyaiḥ kṣīreṇa sarpiṣā .. 103 ..
2.21.d:
फलैः कालोद्भवैः पुष्पैः शङ्कराय हरेद्बलिम् ॥
अपूपैः परमान्नेन भक्ष्यैः क्षीरेण सर्पिषा ॥ 103 ॥
2.21.m:
and with seasonal fruits and flowers, he should present a bali to Śaṅkara.
With cakes, supreme food, edibles, milk, and clarified butter,

2.21.s:
mālyānulepanaiḥ śuklairmahendrāya haredbalim ..
yavānāṃ ca tilānāṃ ca godhūmānāṃ tathā sakṛt ..104 ..
2.21.d:
माल्यानुलेपनैः शुक्लैर्महेन्द्राय हरेद्बलिम् ॥
यवानां च तिलानां च गोधूमानां तथा सकृत् ॥104 ॥
2.21.m:
and with white garlands and unguents, he should present a bali to Mahendra.
With barley, sesame, and wheat at once,

2.21.s:
bhakṣyaiḥ saguḍasarpiṣkairbaliṃ kuryāttu vahnaye ..
guḍodanaguḍāpūpānpakvamāṃsaṃ tathāmiṣam .. 105 .. .
2.21.d:
भक्ष्यैः सगुडसर्पिष्कैर्बलिं कुर्यात्तु वह्नये ॥
गुडोदनगुडापूपान्पक्वमांसं तथामिषम् ॥ 105 ॥ ।
2.21.m:
with edibles mixed with jaggery and clarified butter, he should make a bali to Agni.
Boiled rice with jaggery, jaggery cakes, cooked meat, and flesh,

2.21.s:
yamāya ca baliṃ dadyādraktamālyānulepanam ..
pakvamāṃsaṃ tathā māṃsaṃ kṛṣṇamālyānulepanam .. 106 ..
2.21.d:
यमाय च बलिं दद्याद्रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनम् ॥
पक्वमांसं तथा मांसं कृष्णमाल्यानुलेपनम् ॥ 106 ॥
2.21.m:
with red garlands and unguent, he should offer as a bali to Yama.
Cooked meat and flesh, with black garlands and unguent,

2.21.s:
virūpākṣāya tu surāṃ dadyātsauvīrakaṃ tathā ..
mudgāpūpāṃstilāpūpāñjalajānmandirāṃstathā .. 107 ..
2.21.d:
विरूपाक्षाय तु सुरां दद्यात्सौवीरकं तथा ॥
मुद्गापूपांस्तिलापूपाञ्जलजान्मन्दिरांस्तथा ॥ 107 ॥
2.21.m:
and liquor and sour gruel he should give to Virūpākṣa.
Cakes of mung beans, cakes of sesame, aquatic [flowers], and temples [of sweetmeats],

2.21.s:
varuṇāya baliṃ dadyātpītaṃ mālyādikaṃ tathā ..
yavagodhūmacaṇakamāṣasaktūnsagorasān .. .. 108 ..
2.21.d:
वरुणाय बलिं दद्यात्पीतं माल्यादिकं तथा ॥
यवगोधूमचणकमाषसक्तून्सगोरसान् ॥ ॥ 108 ॥
2.21.m:
along with yellow garlands and the like, he should offer as a bali to Varuṇa.
Barley, wheat, chickpeas, roasted meal of black gram with dairy products,

2.21.s:
kulmāṣaghṛtasaṃyuktānbaliṃ dadyāttu vāyave ..
bhakṣyāṃśca madhusaṃyuktānmudgamiśrāṃstathāmiṣam .. 109 ..
2.21.d:
कुल्माषघृतसंयुक्तान्बलिं दद्यात्तु वायवे ॥
भक्ष्यांश्च मधुसंयुक्तान्मुद्गमिश्रांस्तथामिषम् ॥ 109 ॥
2.21.m:
accompanied by boiled pulses and clarified butter, he should offer as a bali to Vāyu.
Edibles mixed with honey and combined with mung beans, as well as flesh,

2.21.s:
citraṃ mālyaṃ kuṃkumaṃ ca kuberāya haredbalim ..
śimbidhānyabhavānbhakṣyāñśālyannaṃ saguḍaṃ dadhi ..2.104.110..
2.21.d:
चित्रं माल्यं कुंकुमं च कुबेराय हरेद्बलिम् ॥
शिम्बिधान्यभवान्भक्ष्याञ्शाल्यन्नं सगुडं दधि ॥2.104.110॥
2.21.m:
multicolored garlands, and saffron he should present as a bali to Kubera.
Edibles made of legumes, rice of winter grain, curd with jaggery,

2.21.s:
īśānāya baliṃ dadyācchuklamālyānulepanaiḥ ..
śuklaudanaṃ śuklamālyaṃ śūlāyopaharedbalim ..111..
2.21.d:
ईशानाय बलिं दद्याच्छुक्लमाल्यानुलेपनैः ॥
शुक्लौदनं शुक्लमाल्यं शूलायोपहरेद्बलिम् ॥111॥
2.21.m:
with white garlands and unguents, he should offer as a bali to Īśāna.
White boiled rice and white garlands he should present as a bali to the Trident;

2.21.s:
tathā pañcarasaiḥ siddhaṃ dadyādvijñāya buddhimān ..
kṛsaraṃ gandhapuṣpāḍhyaṃ dadyācchakrāya pāyasam..112..
2.21.d:
तथा पञ्चरसैः सिद्धं दद्याद्विज्ञाय बुद्धिमान् ॥
कृसरं गन्धपुष्पाढ्यं दद्याच्छक्राय पायसम्॥112॥
2.21.m:
likewise, prepared with the five flavors, the wise man should offer it to the knowledgeable one.
He should offer rice-and-sesame rich in fragrant flowers, and milk-rice to Śakra.

2.21.s:
phalodanaṃ raktamālyaṃ dadyācchaktyai tathā balim ..
snānamaṇḍalakebhyo'pi baliṃ dadyāttato balim..113..
2.21.d:
फलोदनं रक्तमाल्यं दद्याच्छक्त्यै तथा बलिम् ॥
स्नानमण्डलकेभ्योऽपि बलिं दद्यात्ततो बलिम्॥113॥
2.21.m:
He should offer boiled rice with fruits and red garlands as a bali to the Spear;
and then he should offer a bali to the bath-diagrams as well.

2.21.s:
bālakrīḍanakānbhakṣyānphalāni vividhāni ca ..
matsyāmiṣaṃ sarudhiraṃ pāyasaṃ tilataṇḍulam .. 114 ..
2.21.d:
बालक्रीडनकान्भक्ष्यान्फलानि विविधानि च ॥
मत्स्यामिषं सरुधिरं पायसं तिलतण्डुलम् ॥ 114 ॥
2.21.m:
Children's toys, edibles, various fruits,
fish and meat along with blood, milk-rice, sesame and rice grains,

2.21.s:
sakṛdantrāṇi hṛdayaṃ bhūtebhyo balimāharet ..
oṃkārādyaiścaturthyantaiḥ svāhākārasamanvitaiḥ ..115..
2.21.d:
सकृदन्त्राणि हृदयं भूतेभ्यो बलिमाहरेत् ॥
ओंकाराद्यैश्चतुर्थ्यन्तैः स्वाहाकारसमन्वितैः ॥115॥
2.21.m:
excrement, entrails, and a heart he should present as a bali to the spirits.
With the names of the deities mentioned in the royal consecration mantras,

2.21.s:
rājyābhiṣekamantroktadevatānāṃ pṛthakpṛthak ..
nāmabhirjuhuyādvahnau yathāśraddhaṃ yathāghṛtam .. 116..
2.21.d:
राज्याभिषेकमन्त्रोक्तदेवतानां पृथक्पृथक् ॥
नामभिर्जुहुयाद्वह्नौ यथाश्रद्धं यथाघृतम् ॥ 116॥
2.21.m:
beginning with the syllable Oṃ, ending in the dative case, and accompanied by the word 'svāhā',
he should sacrifice into the fire separately according to faith and with clarified butter.

2.21.s:
pūrṇāhutiṃ tato dattvā deyā vipreṣu dakṣiṇā ..
kanakaṃ rajataṃ gāvo vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca .. 117 ..
2.21.d:
पूर्णाहुतिं ततो दत्त्वा देया विप्रेषु दक्षिणा ॥
कनकं रजतं गावो वासांसि विविधानि च ॥ 117 ॥
2.21.m:
Then, having offered the final oblation, a dakṣiṇā should be given to the brahmins:
gold, silver, cows, and various garments.

2.21.s:
kartre ca dakṣiṇā deyā tathā rāma viśeṣataḥ ..
dattaṃ vastrādi devebhyastathā stānaghaṭādikam .. 118 ..
2.21.d:
कर्त्रे च दक्षिणा देया तथा राम विशेषतः ॥
दत्तं वस्त्रादि देवेभ्यस्तथा स्तानघटादिकम् ॥ 118 ॥
2.21.m:
And a dakṣiṇā should be given particularly to the officiating priest, O Rāma;
whatever garments and other things were given to the gods, as well as the bath-jars and the like,

2.21.s:
kartā yatheṣṭaṃ vibhajettasya bhāgo hi sa smṛtaḥ ..
ghṛte'tha vadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā namaskṛtya ca devatāḥ ..119 ..
2.21.d:
कर्ता यथेष्टं विभजेत्तस्य भागो हि स स्मृतः ॥
घृतेऽथ वदनं दृष्ट्वा नमस्कृत्य च देवताः ॥119 ॥
2.21.m:
the officiating priest may divide as he pleases, for that is recorded as his portion.
Then, having looked at his face in clarified butter and having bowed to the deities,

2.21.s:
maṅgalyālambhanaṃ kṛtvā phalapāṇirudaṅmukhaḥ ..
tasmāddeśādvinirgatya gṛhaṃ yāyāttataḥ svakam .. 2.104.120 ..
2.21.d:
मङ्गल्यालम्भनं कृत्वा फलपाणिरुदङ्मुखः ॥
तस्माद्देशाद्विनिर्गत्य गृहं यायात्ततः स्वकम् ॥ 2.104.120 ॥
2.21.m: Having touched auspicious objects, holding fruit in his hand and facing north, / he should depart from that place and then go to his own home.

2.21.s:
tatra tiṣṭheddhaviṣyāśī brahmacārī ca tāṃ niśām ..
snāpito brahmapūtena snānenāyaṃ yathā bhavet .. 121 ..
2.21.d:
तत्र तिष्ठेद्धविष्याशी ब्रह्मचारी च तां निशाम् ॥
स्नापितो ब्रह्मपूतेन स्नानेनायं यथा भवेत् ॥ 121 ॥
2.21.m: There he should remain for that night, eating sacrificial food and observing celibacy. / As he becomes bathed with this bath purified by the sacred word,

2.21.s:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati ..
purā devāsure yuddhe śakrāyaitadbṛhaspatiḥ .. 122..
2.21.d:
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति ॥
पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे शक्रायैतद्बृहस्पतिः ॥ 122॥
2.21.m: he attains all desires and goes to heaven. / Formerly, in the war between gods and asuras, Bṛhaspati performed this for Śakra,

2.21.s:
kṛtavānpuruhūtāya tataḥ śakraḥ surādhipaḥ ..
jaghāna daityamukhyānāṃ navatīrnava bhārgava .. 123..
2.21.d:
कृतवान्पुरुहूताय ततः शक्रः सुराधिपः ॥
जघान दैत्यमुख्यानां नवतीर्नव भार्गव ॥ 123॥
2.21.m: for Puruhūta; then Śakra, lord of the gods, / slew ninety-nine of the foremost Daityas, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

2.21.s:
dhanyaṃ yaśasyaṃ ripunāśakāri rakṣohaṇaṃ pāpaharaṃ pavitram ..
rogāpahaṃ vighnavināśakāri snānaṃ mayā te vihitaṃ yathārtham..124..

śatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 104 ..

rāma uvāca ..
snānamanyatsamācakṣva bhagavanduritāpaham ..
vināyakopasṛṣṭānāṃ sarvakarmaprasādhakam .. 1 ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
vināyakaḥ karmavighnasidhyarthaṃ viniyojitaḥ ..

antyajairgardabhairuṣṭraiḥ sahaikatrāvatiṣṭhate .. 4 ..
vrajamānastathātmānaṃ manyate'nugataṃ paraiḥ ..
vimanā viphalārambhaḥ saṃsīdannanimittataḥ .. 5 ..
2.21.d:
धन्यं यशस्यं रिपुनाशकारि रक्षोहणं पापहरं पवित्रम् ॥
रोगापहं विघ्नविनाशकारि स्नानं मया ते विहितं यथार्थम्॥124॥
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे द्वितीयखंडे मा0सं0 रामं प्रति पुष्करोपाख्याने दिक्पालस्नानवर्णनन्नाम चतुरुत्तर
शततमोऽध्यायः ॥ 104 ॥
2.105
राम उवाच ॥
स्नानमन्यत्समाचक्ष्व भगवन्दुरितापहम् ॥
विनायकोपसृष्टानां सर्वकर्मप्रसाधकम् ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
विनायकः कर्मविघ्नसिध्यर्थं विनियोजितः ॥
गणानामधिपत्ये च केशवेन पितामहैः ॥ 2 ॥
तेनोपसृष्टो यस्तस्य लक्षणानि निबोध मे ॥
स्वप्नेऽवगाहतेऽत्यर्थं जलं मुण्डं च पश्यति ॥ 3 ॥
काषायवाससश्चैव क्रव्यादांश्चाधिरोहति ॥
अन्त्यजैर्गर्दभैरुष्ट्रैः सहैकत्रावतिष्ठते ॥ 4 ॥
व्रजमानस्तथात्मानं मन्यतेऽनुगतं परैः ॥
विमना विफलारम्भः संसीदन्ननिमित्ततः ॥ 5 ॥
2.21.m:
Conferring wealth, bringing renown, destroying foes, slaying demons, removing sin, pure, / warding off disease, and destroying obstacles—the bath has been truly prescribed by me for you.
Thus ends the hundred and fourth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Bath of the Guardians of the Directions', in the second book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the narrative of Puṣkara to Rāma.
Rāma said: / Declare another bath, O venerable one, which removes misfortune, / for those afflicted by Vināyaka, accomplishing all undertakings.
Puṣkara said: / Vināyaka was appointed for the accomplishment of obstacles to actions / and to the lordship of the Gaṇas by Keśava and the grandfathers.
Learn from me the signs of one who is seized by him: / In a dream he plunges deeply into water and sees a shaven-headed person.
He mounts those wearing ochre robes and carnivorous animals. / He stays in one place with outcasts, donkeys, and camels.
Likewise, as he walks, he thinks himself followed by others. / Despondent, his undertakings fruitless, he sinks down without cause.

2.21.s:
tenopasṛṣṭo labhate na rājyaṃ rājanandanaḥ ..
yā kumārī ca bhartāramapatyaṃ garbhamaṅganā .. 6 ..
ācāryatvaṃ śrotriyaśca na śiṣyo'dhyayanaṃ tathā ..
vaṇiṅ na lābhamāpnoti na kṛṣiṃ tu kṛṣīvalaḥ .. 7..
snapanaṃ tasya kartavyaṃ puṇyehni vidhipūrvakam ..
hastapuṣyāśvayuksaumyavaiṣṇavānyatame śubhe .. 8..

carmaṇyānuḍuhe rakte sthāpyaṃ bhadrāsanaṃ bhavet .. 9 ..
bhadrāsanopaviṣṭasya svasti vācyaṃ dvijottamān ..
gaurasarṣapakalkena medhyenotsāditasya ca .. 2.105.10 ..
sarvauṣadhaiḥ sarvagandhaiḥ praliptaśirasastathā ..
caturbhiḥ kalaśaiḥ kāryaṃ snapanaṃ mantrasaṃyutam ..11 ..
tathaikavarṇāḥ kalaśāḥ kartavyāste hradāmbhasā ..
aśvasthānādgajasthānādvalmīkātsaṅgamāddhṛdāt .. 12 ..
2.21.d:
तेनोपसृष्टो लभते न राज्यं राजनन्दनः ॥
या कुमारी च भर्तारमपत्यं गर्भमङ्गना ॥ 6 ॥
आचार्यत्वं श्रोत्रियश्च न शिष्योऽध्ययनं तथा ॥
वणिङ् न लाभमाप्नोति न कृषिं तु कृषीवलः ॥ 7॥
स्नपनं तस्य कर्तव्यं पुण्येह्नि विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
हस्तपुष्याश्वयुक्सौम्यवैष्णवान्यतमे शुभे ॥ 8॥
नक्षत्रे च मुहूर्ते च मैत्रे वा ब्रह्मदैवते ॥
चर्मण्यानुडुहे रक्ते स्थाप्यं भद्रासनं भवेत् ॥ 9 ॥
भद्रासनोपविष्टस्य स्वस्ति वाच्यं द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
गौरसर्षपकल्केन मेध्येनोत्सादितस्य च ॥ 2.105.10 ॥
सर्वौषधैः सर्वगन्धैः प्रलिप्तशिरसस्तथा ॥
चतुर्भिः कलशैः कार्यं स्नपनं मन्त्रसंयुतम् ॥11 ॥
तथैकवर्णाः कलशाः कर्तव्यास्ते ह्रदाम्भसा ॥
अश्वस्थानाद्गजस्थानाद्वल्मीकात्सङ्गमाद्धृदात् ॥ 12 ॥
2.21.m:
Seized by him, a king's son does not obtain a kingdom, / nor does a maiden obtain a husband, nor a woman offspring [or] pregnancy.
Nor does a learned brahmin attain the status of a teacher, nor a pupil his study; / a merchant does not gain profit, nor does a farmer [attain] agriculture.
A bath should be performed for him on an auspicious day according to the rule, / under any auspicious [constellation] such as Hasta, Puṣya, Aśvinī, Mṛgaśiras, or Śravaṇā,
and under an auspicious lunar mansion and in a favorable moment sacred to Mitra or Brahmā. / An auspicious seat should be placed upon the red hide of an ox.
One should have the foremost twice-born recite blessings for him when he is seated on the auspicious seat / and has been rubbed with pure paste of white mustard,
and whose head has been anointed with all herbs and all perfumes. / The bath should be performed with four jars accompanied by mantras.
Likewise, the jars should be made of one color, with water from a lake, / and with earth from a horse-stable, an elephant-stable, an anthill, a confluence, and a pool.

2.21.s:
mṛttikāṃ rocanaṃ gandhānguggulaṃ teṣu nikṣipet ..
sarvauṣadhīśca bījāni snānamantrānataḥ śṛṇu .. 13 ..
sahasrākṣaṃ śatadhāramṛṣibhiḥ pāvanaṃ kṛtam ..
tena tvāmabhiṣiñcāmaḥ pāvamānīḥ punantu te .. 14 ..
bhagaṃ te varuṇo rājā bhagaṃ śukro bṛhaspatiḥ ..
bhagamindraśca vāyuśca bhagaṃ saptarṣayo daduḥ .. 15 ..
yatte keśeṣu daurbhāgyaṃ sīmante yacca mūrdhani ..

2.21.d:
मृत्तिकां रोचनं गन्धान्गुग्गुलं तेषु निक्षिपेत् ॥
सर्वौषधीश्च बीजानि स्नानमन्त्रानतः शृणु ॥ 13 ॥
सहस्राक्षं शतधारमृषिभिः पावनं कृतम् ॥
तेन त्वामभिषिञ्चामः पावमानीः पुनन्तु ते ॥ 14 ॥
भगं ते वरुणो राजा भगं शुक्रो बृहस्पतिः ॥
भगमिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च भगं सप्तर्षयो ददुः ॥ 15 ॥
यत्ते केशेषु दौर्भाग्यं सीमन्ते यच्च मूर्धनि ॥
ललाटकर्णयोरक्ष्णोरापस्तद्धन्तु ते सदा ॥ 16 ॥
दर्भपिञ्जलमादाय वामहस्ते ततो गुरुः ॥
स्नातस्य सार्षपं तैलं सुवेणौदुम्बरेण तु ॥ 17 ॥
जुहुयान्मूर्ध्नि धर्मज्ञ चतुर्थ्यन्तैश्च नामभिः ॥
ओंकारपूतैर्धर्मज्ञ स्वाहाकारसमन्वितैः ॥ 18 ॥
मिताय संमितायाथ सालङ्कटकटाय च ॥
कूष्माण्डराजपुत्राय तथैव च महात्मने ॥ 19 ॥
2.21.m:
One should throw into them yellow orpiment, perfumes, bdellium, / all herbs, and seeds. Hear now the mantras for the bath:
'[The water] has a thousand eyes and a hundred streams, made purifying by the sages. / With it we consecrate you; may the purifying verses cleanse you.
May King Varuṇa grant you good fortune; may Śukra and Bṛhaspati grant you good fortune; / may Indra and Vāyu grant you good fortune; may the Seven Sages grant you good fortune.
Whatever misfortune is in your hair, in your parting, and on your crown, / on your forehead, in your ears, or in your eyes—may the waters destroy that always for you.'
Then, taking a bundle of darbha-grass in his left hand, the guru, / using a ladle made of udumbara wood, should offer into the mustard oil
upon the crown of the one who has bathed, O knower of dharma, with names ending in the dative, / purified by the syllable Om, O knower of dharma, and joined with the exclamation Svāhā:
'To Mita, to Saṃmita, then to Sālaṅkaṭakaṭa, / to Kūṣmāṇḍarājaputra, and likewise to the great-souled one.'

2.21.d:
नामभिर्बलिमन्त्रैश्च वषट्कारसमन्वितैः॥
दद्याच्चतुष्पथे शीर्षे कुशानास्तीर्य सर्वतः ॥2.105.20॥ ।
कृतरक्तांस्तण्डुलांश्च पललौदनमेव च ॥
मत्स्यान्पक्वांस्तथैवामान्मांसमेतावदेव तु ॥ 21 ॥
पुष्पं चित्रं सुगन्धं तु सुरां च त्रिविधामपि ॥
मूलकं पूरिकापूपास्तथैवैण्डर्यकाणि च ॥ 22॥
एतान्सर्वानुपाहृत्य भूमौ कृत्वा ततः शिरः॥
विनायकस्य जननीमुपतिष्ठेत्ततोऽम्बिकाम्॥23॥
रूपं देहि यशो देहि सौभाग्यं सुभगे मम॥
पुत्रान्देहि धनं देहि सर्वान्कामांश्च देहि मे॥24॥
ततः शुक्लाम्बरधरः शुक्लमाल्यानुलेपनः॥
भोजयेद्ब्राह्मणान्दद्याद्वस्त्रयुग्मं गुरोरपि ॥ 25 ॥
विनायकस्नानमिदं यशस्यं रक्षोहणं विघ्नविनाशकारि॥
सर्वामयघ्नं रिपुनाशकं च कर्तव्यमेतन्नियमेन राम॥26॥
2.21.m:
With the names and offering-mantras accompanied by the exclamation Vaṣaṭ, / having strewn kuśa grass all around, he should offer it at a crossroads, upon the head:
rice grains colored red, boiled rice with sesamum paste, / cooked fish as well as raw, and meat of just this sort,
variegated fragrant flowers, and the three kinds of liquor, / radish, fried cakes, and pies, and likewise sweets of flour.
Having brought all these and placed his head on the ground, / he should then wait upon Ambikā, the mother of Vināyaka:
'Grant me beauty, grant me renown, grant me good fortune, O auspicious lady; / grant me sons, grant me wealth, and grant me all desires.'
Then, wearing white garments, adorned with white garlands and unguents, / he should feed the brahmins and also give a pair of garments to the guru.
This bath of Vināyaka brings renown, slays demons, destroys obstacles, / removes all diseases, and destroys foes; it should be performed by strict rule, O Rāma.
